chapters.title: Chapter 501: The Easy Interrogation
paragraphs: "I didn’t say anything." The young man looked at him angrily.
"You didn’t have to, any reaction when everyone else is staying silent can be an answer." Lian replied with a smile.
Although the real answer was that he already knew they were from the Third Region, he only wanted to gain some kind of control over the conversation that was about to happen.
The commander gave the young soldier a cold look, that look said as much as a shout.

He sat down in front of the commander, the man was still connected to the ground by ice from his wrist and lower leg, and despite his defeat, he had not lowered his head ...his eyes were full of hatred.
"I would like to ask why you are stopping us from moving forward?" Instead of wasting time, he went straight to the main point.
The commander remained silent.
At that moment, One took a step forward and slammed his foot against the ground.
Boom.
The ground under his foot sank slightly.
The man gave a short look at his jaws and then put his eyes back on Lian.
"Even if you know, it is useless for a foreign thief like you."
"So there is something worth hiding." Lian tilted his head slightly.
The muscles in the commander’s jaw tightened.

"If your goal was to protect the Third Region, you wouldn’t stay here. If you wanted to drive us out of this area, you would destroy the camp. If you wanted to start a war, you would kill many more people."
The commander did not take his eyes off him and Lian leaned forward a little more.
"But you attack exactly enough to stop the groups from moving forward... not enough to make the base decide to send real forces."
There was no answer, but this silence was different from the man’s expression, it was no longer simple hatred and he had become alert toward him.
The young Vorhelm noticed it, he had hit the right point.
"So you only want to buy time."
"Shut up, foreigner." One of the younger prisoners, who was tied to the ground with ice several meters away, suddenly said.
The commander immediately turned his head toward him.
Lian did the same, there was silence for a moment and then he gave a small smile.
"I think you should have said that to your commander, but anyway, then my guess was right."
The young man only then realized that his own reaction had been an answer, he clenched his teeth and closed his mouth.
Lian stood up again.
So this part was clear too, they wanted time.
But for what? A caravan that had to pass? A transfer of forces? The evacuation of an area? A monster that had to be hunted?
Or something that had to be taken away before the people from Earth arrived?
He looked at his Colony member and gave him a signal to increase the pressure on these natives.
One lowered his large head, now his jaws were exactly above the commander’s shoulder.
"What is on the other side of the pass?" Lian then asked.
"Nothing." The commander answered without hesitation.
He looked at him for a few seconds, since this man did not want to answer, the pressure had to be increased even more.
Then his eyes moved to One and the ant bent down a little more, his jaws closed right beside the man’s ear.
Clack!
The sound of them hitting each other echoed through the ruins.
The commander did not even blink, but a drop of sweat moved down from the side of his temple.
"That was a bad answer, if I don’t get a better answer, you will lose one of your ears."
"Even if you cross this pass, you will find nothing but death!" The man looked at him with hatred.
Lian stayed silent for a moment and then one of his eyebrows rose slightly.
Interesting.
The man had not said,
"We won’t let you cross."
He had not said,
"That area belongs to us."
He had said that they would find nothing but death, this choice of words could have been conscious or unconscious, if it was the first, it could have been some kind of word game.
But if it was the second, then there was something there that this man considered dangerous.
But either way, both confirmed one thing.
"So there is something there and you are not done with it yet, that’s why you need time."
Again, there was no direct answer, but the young Vorhelm no longer needed a verbal answer, he had almost understood everything and only did not know exactly what that thing was.
"When the priests finish their work, none of you will—" At that moment, the young man who had exposed himself earlier said angrily.
"Shut up!" The commander shouted and cut him off.
But it was too late and Lian calmly turned his head toward the young man.
"Priests?"
The man’s face changed slightly and the young Vorhelm looked toward the commander again.

It should not be forgotten that their languages were different and the System was currently providing advanced translation, so if this man had used a word in their language that was translated as priests, he was referring to religious authorities.
He took one calm step forward.

"A few days of buying time and priests who are working on something on the other side...let me guess, there is a religious place there, right? Since you are from the Third Region, then it is related to the Divine of Light."
This time, the younger man held his breath and the commander closed his eyes, even the others could not control the expressions on their faces.
And this revealed everything that needed to be revealed.
"I found it." Lian smiled.
"It doesn’t belong to you, barbarian thieves!" The commander said in a voice full of anger.
"I haven’t even said what I plan to do yet." He shrugged, although it was already certain that their next destination would be that place.
The commander did not answer, but that sentence was the final confirmation.
There was something on the other side of the pass, something belonging to the Divine of Light’s religion and the people of the Third Region only needed a few more days to finish their work.
Considering that the attacks were still continuing, it was clear that they had not finished yet.
Lian moved a few steps away from the prisoners, from the top of the bridge, he looked at the other side of the broken gate.
The thick fog was still hiding a large part of the plain.
He put all the new information together in his mind again.
People from the Third Region.
Priests.
An operation that would take several days.
Limited attacks on exploration groups.
Avoiding a massacre that could anger the Federation.
And a religious area connected to the Divine of Light.
They did not want to defend the borders of their country, they were hiding something and more exactly, they wanted no one to find that place until a certain task was completed.
He turned back toward the commander.
"What did you find?
"That has nothing to do with you."
"Tell me its name."
"You think because you beat a few people, I will tell you anything you want?" The man gave a cold smile.
He looked at him for a moment, then simply turned his head toward One.
"Do whatever you want." The commander said simply, as if he had accepted death.
This time he was truly ready, and Lian noticed it too, more threats probably would not give him any new information, so he chose another path.
"Okay."
He walked over to one of the younger prisoners, the same one who had made the mistake about the priests earlier.
"Bastard, you—" The commander immediately said, but before he could finish his sentence, his mouth was sealed with ice.
One came toward them and, following his master’s order, opened his jaws and completely licked the young man’s face.
Fear filled the young prisoner so much that he even soiled himself.
Lian ignored it and told One to place half of the man’s head between his jaws, and the giant ant did exactly that.
The young man’s fear became several times stronger, his whole body started shaking, but even then he still did not dare to open his mouth.
He did not even dare to curse anymore, afraid that he would become the next meal of this damn monster.
"How many days are left until the priest finishes the work?"
"Two?"
There was no reaction from the other side.
"Three?"
Suddenly, his eyes moved very slightly.
"So there are three days left, well, what are they doing that takes so long? Are they just opening the door there now?"
Again, there was no clear reaction, the young man was still trying to stay silent despite all the fear he was feeling.
"No...then it has already been opened."
This time, the man’s eyebrows tightened slightly.
Lian paused, maybe that was wrong.
"Or part of it has been opened and the main part is still sealed."
This time, the man’s jaw tightened.
He smiled, he had gotten the answer he wanted.
Now the situation was clearer.
A ruin, probably only recently revealed, one part was accessible and another part was still sealed, the priests needed three days to fully open it.
The Third Region was willing to fight foreigners for several days to stop them from reaching that place.
And its connection to the Divine of Light was almost certain too.
"Thank you, our next destination is clear."

"Don’t even think about going there." The young man finally opened his mouth and said with hatred. "That shrine does not belong to you, no foreigner has the right to set foot inside it, the moment you enter, you will be punished by the goddess!"
Lian simply ignored him.
"a shrine belongs to the Divine of Light, huh?" His eyes turned toward the distance.
Kain also looked toward the place where the fog behind the broken gate had swallowed everything.
Only a few hours ago, they had been discussing that they might find something interesting in the unknown areas.
Apparently, they did not need to search for very long.
And worse...or perhaps better, what they had found could be directly connected to him.
"Now at least we know where we need to go."

chapters.title: Chapter 502: Kain’s Crazy Idea
paragraphs: "Well...at least now we know where we need to go." Lian said while keeping his eyes on the fog on the other side of the pass.
The native commander looked at him with hatred, but he said nothing else.
There was nothing left to say either.

Within a few minutes, they had learned more than they were probably supposed to know; the forces of the Third Region had blocked the path of the Earth Awakened for several days, their priests were working on something on the other side of the pass, and their destination was also related to the Divine of Light.
The only thing he still did not know was exactly what was waiting for them there.
The camp leader came forward with several of his people.
"Thanks again for what you did." The man gave the native prisoners a short look and then continued more seriously.

"But if you really want to go to the other side, be careful. They are not the only group they have. If they have been blocking this path for three or four days, then they clearly have more people ahead."
"I know." Lian replied.
His eyes fell on the black restraint rings that one of the natives had brought to capture Kain.
A very small smile appeared on his face.
"Use the same things they brought to restrain us and tie them up."
The man was confused for a moment and then understood what he meant.
A few minutes later, the same restraint rings were around the native commander’s wrists.
The others were also restrained with special ropes and their own equipment.
The young Vorhelm only deactivated Frost Dominion after making sure that their hands and feet were completely restrained.
The ice around the prisoners’ feet cracked and turned into cold Mana particles within a few seconds, disappearing from the stones.

"Send the news to the base, both about the attacks over the past few days and about the fact that you captured some natives alive. If some of the missing Awakened really were captured, these people might know something, or at least it might be possible to negotiate with them."
"Don’t worry. I’ll send the report today." The camp leader nodded.
The native commander, whose hands were now tied with the same restraint device, slowly raised his head.
His eyes fixed directly on Kain.
"Pass through here and you will never return alive! What you stole will soon be taken back by our people!"
Kain, who was standing beside One, narrowed his eyes for a moment.
"I understand, apparently you don’t have anything besides nonsense." He said in a dry tone.
The commander sneered.
"When you see the people of the Third Region again, keep that same tone."
He said nothing and simply turned around and climbed onto One’s back, Lian also gave the prisoners one last look.
If the people of the Third Region still did not know that Kain was here, it was better for this situation to continue for as long as possible.
This group could no longer send the news, but sooner or later their disappearance would attract attention.
So there was no reason to waste time.
He also climbed onto One’s back.
"Let’s go."
The giant ant started moving.
A few minutes later, his six huge legs landed on the stone bridge of the pass and they crossed the last point where the groups from Base #9 regularly operated.
The sound of the camp slowly disappeared behind them, the lights became smaller and then the fog swallowed them.
For almost the first hour, the path was not very strange.
A wide road stretched between the rocks and most of its old stone pavement was buried under dirt and dust.
On both sides of the path, lantern statues appeared every few hundred meters.
Some were broken, some had no heads and some were still strangely well-preserved.
One passed between them without any problem.
Kain was mostly silent during that hour, Lian looked at him a few times, but he did not ask any questions.
In the end, his friend broke the silence himself, he raised his right hand slightly and a golden-white light the size of a small flame appeared between his fingers.
He looked at it for a few seconds.
There was nothing strange about it to him, it was the same light he had used many times during the past months.
He closed his fingers and the light disappeared.
"Do you think that from now on, every time I use the light, someone will realize that I absorbed the Tear?" He asked.
"Not everyone." Lian was looking at the path ahead.
"Are you sure?"
"Look at that previous group, all of them saw your light. But only one of them noticed it at first. Then he told the commander and the others reacted too."
"So it’s something obvious, but only to someone who knows what to look for." Kain thought for a few moments and reasoned with himself.
"Probably."
"So ordinary people won’t notice, but people who really know about the Divine of Light might realize it."
"So far, it seems that way."
A cold wind passed between the rocks, for a few seconds, only the sound of One’s footsteps remained.
Then Kain spoke again.

"It isn’t just that they want to capture me, that man looked at my power and understood something that I still don’t know after using it so much, I think that part bothers me more than the fact that they want to capture me."
This time Lian looked at him, what he said was not meaningless.
This boy had absorbed the Tear of the Divine of Light, his Class had changed, and he had gained new Talents.
The light inside his body could even be recognized by the followers of the Divine of Light, but he himself still did not know exactly what had entered his body.
With all the benefits it had given him so far, they still had no idea what exactly the Tear of the Divine of Light was.
And what made the light he used different from the light used by other users of the Light Element.
"Don’t worry, the place we’re going to belongs to the Divine of Light and the priests connected to it are there too, we should be able to get the information you want."
Kain stayed silent for a few seconds and then gave a short smile.
"I never thought that one day I would have to enter a place belonging to my enemy just to find out what is inside my own body."
"You had better choices."
"Like what?"
"Not absorbing it."
"That wasn’t a choice, remember? Even I didn’t understand what happened, but anyway, it caused me to have a four-star Class now." Kain laughed.
He then wanted to say something but suddenly stopped, his eyes stared ahead for a few seconds, but it was clear that his mind was somewhere else.
It was as if something had suddenly come to his mind ...and then he asked.
"Lian."
"Hmm?"
"Do you think the other six Divines also have something like that Tear?"
This time Lian slowly turned his head and only looked at his friend for a few seconds.
"Why? Do you want to absorb them too?"
Kain said nothing and that silence was the answer.
The young Vorhelm stared at his friend for a few seconds and then let out a short sigh.
"Are you crazy?"
"I haven’t said anything yet." The Child Of Light smiled.
"You didn’t have to."
Lian placed his hand on the armor on One’s back so that he would not lose his balance because of the movement of his huge body.
"You absorbed one Tear and the people of the Third Region want to capture you alive. Then your plan is to go after the other six? Do you want to make all seven native regions chase after you?"
"Well...when you put it like that, it sounds really bad."
"Because it is really bad."
Kain stayed silent for a few moments, this time the playful look on his face was weaker.
"But if one Tear was able to change my evolution path, then what happens if I absorb the other six?"
Lian looked at him.
And he continued.
"My Class is four-star. If these things can really affect the evolution path...maybe I can reach a five-star Class."
The Vorhelm said nothing for a moment, this time his friend’s words were not only about greed for power.
A five-star Class meant the possibility of five evolutions, much higher limits.
If something existed in this world that could change the number of stars of a Class, its value was impossible for most people to imagine.
But the problem was that Kain still did not know whether a second Tear would even be compatible with his body.
Or whether something like a Tear really existed for all the Divines.
Or whether two effects belonging to two different Divines would destroy his body.
"Let’s first find out what this is." Lian said.
Kain nodded.
"After that, you can make plans to make the other six regions your enemies."
"It’s good that you support me."
"I never said I would come with you."
"If I go, you’ll come." Kain leaned slightly toward him.
"No."
"You will."
Lian did not answer.
Kain waited for a few seconds and then nodded with satisfaction.
"That silence means yes."
"Now I understand that silence really can be interpreted very badly." The young Vorhelm only gave him a look this time.
When almost two hours had passed since they started moving, the road began to change.
The soft dirt became less common, the color of the ground became lighter and white layers that looked like salt could be seen between the cracks in the rocks.
In some places, black and shiny pieces were scattered across the ground.
Kain first thought they were pieces of stone, but when the light from the sky fell on one of them, its surface reflected it like glass.
Unfortunately, they had no map to know whether they were even going in the right direction or not, and the farther they went, the stranger the path became.
World Memory could not help by itself either.
This ability did not create maps.
It could only match its old information with an existing map and rebuild missing areas, old roads, or recorded structures on it.
But now there was no map.
Although this did not mean that World Memory had become completely useless ... perhaps it was time to combine it with the Celestial Book Of Treasures.

"Do you think that from now on, every time I use the light, someone will realize that I absorbed the Tear?" He asked.
"Not everyone." Lian was looking at the path ahead.
"Are you sure?"
"Look at that previous group, all of them saw your light.
But only one of them noticed it at first.
Then he told the commander and the others reacted too."
"So it’s something obvious, but only to someone who knows what to look for." Kain thought for a few moments and reasoned with himself.
"Probably."
"So ordinary people won’t notice, but people who really know about the Divine of Light might realize it."
"So far, it seems that way."
A cold wind passed between the rocks, for a few seconds, only the sound of One’s footsteps remained.
Then Kain spoke again.

"It isn’t just that they want to capture me, that man looked at my power and understood something that I still don’t know after using it so much, I think that part bothers me more than the fact that they want to capture me."
This time Lian looked at him, what he said was not meaningless.
This boy had absorbed the Tear of the Divine of Light, his Class had changed, and he had gained new Talents.
The light inside his body could even be recognized by the followers of the Divine of Light, but he himself still did not know exactly what had entered his body.
With all the benefits it had given him so far, they still had no idea what exactly the Tear of the Divine of Light was.
And what made the light he used different from the light used by other users of the Light Element.
"Don’t worry, the place we’re going to belongs to the Divine of Light and the priests connected to it are there too, we should be able to get the information you want."
Kain stayed silent for a few seconds and then gave a short smile.
"I never thought that one day I would have to enter a place belonging to my enemy just to find out what is inside my own body."
"You had better choices."
"Like what?"
"Not absorbing it."
"That wasn’t a choice, remember?
Even I didn’t understand what happened, but anyway, it caused me to have a four-star Class now." Kain laughed.
He then wanted to say something but suddenly stopped, his eyes stared ahead for a few seconds, but it was clear that his mind was somewhere else.
It was as if something had suddenly come to his mind ...and then he asked.
"Lian."
"Hmm?"
"Do you think the other six Divines also have something like that Tear?"
This time Lian slowly turned his head and only looked at his friend for a few seconds.
"Why?
Do you want to absorb them too?"
Kain said nothing and that silence was the answer.
The young Vorhelm stared at his friend for a few seconds and then let out a short sigh.
"Are you crazy?"
"I haven’t said anything yet." The Child Of Light smiled.
"You didn’t have to."
Lian placed his hand on the armor on One’s back so that he would not lose his balance because of the movement of his huge body.
"You absorbed one Tear and the people of the Third Region want to capture you alive.
Then your plan is to go after the other six?
Do you want to make all seven native regions chase after you?"
"Well...when you put it like that, it sounds really bad."
"Because it is really bad."
Kain stayed silent for a few moments, this time the playful look on his face was weaker.
"But if one Tear was able to change my evolution path, then what happens if I absorb the other six?"
Lian looked at him.
And he continued.
"My Class is four-star.
If these things can really affect the evolution path...maybe I can reach a five-star Class."
The Vorhelm said nothing for a moment, this time his friend’s words were not only about greed for power.
A five-star Class meant the possibility of five evolutions, much higher limits.
If something existed in this world that could change the number of stars of a Class, its value was impossible for most people to imagine.
But the problem was that Kain still did not know whether a second Tear would even be compatible with his body.
Or whether something like a Tear really existed for all the Divines.
Or whether two effects belonging to two different Divines would destroy his body.
"Let’s first find out what this is." Lian said.
Kain nodded.
"After that, you can make plans to make the other six regions your enemies."
"It’s good that you support me."
"I never said I would come with you."
"If I go, you’ll come." Kain leaned slightly toward him.
"No."
"You will."
Lian did not answer.
Kain waited for a few seconds and then nodded with satisfaction.
"That silence means yes."
"Now I understand that silence really can be interpreted very badly." The young Vorhelm only gave him a look this time.
When almost two hours had passed since they started moving, the road began to change.
The soft dirt became less common, the color of the ground became lighter and white layers that looked like salt could be seen between the cracks in the rocks.
In some places, black and shiny pieces were scattered across the ground.
Kain first thought they were pieces of stone, but when the light from the sky fell on one of them, its surface reflected it like glass.
Unfortunately, they had no map to know whether they were even going in the right direction or not, and the farther they went, the stranger the path became.
World Memory could not help by itself either.
This ability did not create maps.
It could only match its old information with an existing map and rebuild missing areas, old roads, or recorded structures on it.
But now there was no map.
Although this did not mean that World Memory had become completely useless ... perhaps it was time to combine it with the Celestial Book Of Treasures.

chapters.title: Chapter 503: A New Map
paragraphs: Lian thought for a few moments.
Then he took out the Celestial Book of Treasure and opened it.
Ever since he had obtained this artifact, he had understood that one of its abilities for searching for treasures depended on a local map.
The book could rebuild the area around the user on its pages as a very simple map, but it was limited.
[Regional Search Mode activated.]
[Maximum Treasure Mapping Range: 300 kilometers.]
Golden threads came out from between the pages and formed a large circle on the page.
Its center was their current location.
An area up to three hundred kilometers around them appeared as very simple and incomplete lines, although it had previously been only 10 kilometers and had made good progress.
It showed rocks, elevations, several paths, and a small number of marks related to valuable resources.
But the farther areas were still almost unclear.
He placed World Memory beside the book, the two artifacts shook at the same time for a moment.
[External Map Detected.]
[Map Source: Celestial Book of Treasure.]
[World Memory synchronization has begun.]
The lines on the page changed.
The road that had been only a rough line a few seconds ago gained several branches.
Faint ruins appeared on both sides of the path.
An old tower, two pilgrim paths, and part of a mountain wall that did not exist on the current map.
But the farther the distance became, the weaker the information was.
[Historical data incomplete.]
[Distance from the current recorded area is too great.]
[Move closer for more accurate recovery.]
"It works." Lian gave a faint smile.
He now practically had a map that showed up to three hundred kilometers around them and in addition, all the treasures within this distance were also marked.
And no matter how far they moved forward, this range would move with them.
He now had a map that he could use anywhere.
He could now see the same thing on the page.
The things close to them were shown almost clearly.
But the possible destination was still only a group of unclear lines and marks at the farthest part of the map.
A faint golden mark could also be seen almost in the same direction.
But it was so far away that even the book could not fully read its information.
[Valuable source detected.]
[Distance: Too far for accurate evaluation.]
Almost half an hour later, the book suggested the first small detour.
A white mark appeared less than one kilometer from the main path, the book had managed to detect something valuable.
The young Vorhelm ordered One to leave the road slightly.
A few minutes later, between two white rocks, they found a plant that had only three thick and partly transparent leaves.
A golden drop was gathered in the center of the leaves, and it was shining even without direct light.
[Lightdew Leaf.]
[Rank: C.]
[Usage: An additional material for making spirit recovery medicine and temporarily increasing compatibility with the four elements.]
Lian pulled it out of the ground together with its roots and placed it inside his storage space.
"Aren’t you going to offer me some too? How did you even find this?" Kain looked at him.
"Instinct, and no, if you want something, find it yourself, although if there were several of them, I would give you one."
"Thank you, has anyone ever told you how generous you are?"
Several hours later, the book once again led them away from the path for another short stop.
This time it was not a plant, inside a narrow crack in the rock, there were three pieces of dull yellow crystal.
[Sunvein Crystal.]
[Rank: C.]
[Usage: Can increase Mana recovery speed by up to ten percent.]
Lian took two.
Kain naturally took one for himself and put it in his own storage space and after that they continued on their path.
About three hours after they started moving, the signs around them became truly strange.
It was no longer only a few pieces of black glass on the ground, some parts of the road had completely turned into a smooth and shiny surface.
The rock on their right looked natural a few meters above the ground, but its lower part was wavy and glass-like, as if it had once melted and then frozen again.
One had to slow down, some parts of the surface were so smooth that even his feet slipped slightly on them.
Kain got down from his back and stood beside part of the wall, running the tip of his finger across the smooth surface.
It was cold, but its shape looked like the result of extreme heat.
"Was this burned?"

Lian got down and examined the wall, then his eyes moved toward the rocks several hundred meters away, the same glass-like surface, a half-ruined tower in the distance, and its lower part was also melted.
Whatever had happened, it was clear that this place had been heavily burned.
Signs of heat and burning could be seen everywhere and all the structures that had once been along this path had been burned.
But it was impossible to say exactly when it had happened.
Kain moved away from the wall.
"Do you think whatever happened was the same event that destroyed this area?"
"Maybe."
World Memory showed several very old structures on the map, but it did not say anything about the cause of the destruction.
The only clear point was that the glass-like marks were very old.
But the narrow path that now passed between two parts of the mountain was not that old.

The edges of the rocks were still newer, the separated pieces were not completely buried under dust yet, a landslide or the collapse of the mountain had recently opened a path that did not exist before.
In simple words, something had recently opened the path ahead, and anything beyond it might still be intact.
In the middle of the fourth hour, Predator’s Instincts warned Lian.
He immediately placed his hand on One’s back.
"Slow down."
One slowed his speed.
"What?" Kain looked at him.
He did not answer, his eyes were fixed on the glass-like surface beside the road.
The wind was coming from the left and the thin dust on the ground was moving in the same direction.
The reflection of the rocks could also be seen on the black surface, but one of the reflections was moving differently.
"Watch the ground!"
Kain immediately jumped off One and at that exact moment ...KRRRRRRRRRK!
The glass-like surface beside the giant ant’s rear leg exploded and a long creature came out from underneath it.
Six short and thick legs and a body almost four meters long that was only half a meter above the ground.
Its back was covered with dark and partly transparent plates and no clear head could be seen.
Then the front part of its body opened, revealing a wide jaw with several rows of teeth.
[Glass Crawler.]
[Rank: Common.]
[Level: 32.]
The jaws closed directly toward One’s leg, but the ant was faster and pulled his leg back.
The creature’s teeth closed on nothing and One lowered his head and closed his own jaws on the edge of the Glass Crawler’s shell.
Crack!
The monster struggled, its shell was hard, but at the same moment Kain raised his palm and concentrated light came out of it.
Boom!
The attack hit the monster’s glass back, part of the light spread across the surface of its shell and created cracks, but the damage was less than he expected.
"Did it absorb it?"
"No, more exactly, it spread it out." Lian said while sensing another presence behind them.
The glass-like surface on the other side broke and a second creature came out.
Then a third.
[Level: 30.]
[Level: 33.]
The young Vorhelm moved toward one of them.
The Glass Crawler lowered its body and came forward like a heavy blade, but he planted his foot firmly on the ground and at the moment of impact, both of his hands grabbed the edge of its shell.
Boom!
The stone under his foot cracked, but he did not move at all and his eyes moved over the creature for a moment.
Then he used the strength of his body to push it away from its path.
The monster turned onto its side and its lower body became visible, unlike its armored back, its belly was soft and gray.
"Kain."
Kain understood.
One lifted the first Glass Crawler with all his weight, the creature’s body rose several meters above the ground and this time Kain did not aim the light at its shell.
He lowered his hand.
Boom!
A concentrated beam entered the monster from below, its soft flesh burned and the creature struggled with a sharp sound.
The giant ant slammed it against the rock beside the road.
Kaboom!
The shell broke.
Lian also turned the creature in front of him onto its side with a strike and blocked its path with a layer of ice.
The Glass Crawler tried to enter the surface again and ice grew into the cracks under its body.
Its movement stopped.
Kain sent his second attack and a few seconds later the last creature also fell to the ground.
The battle had lasted no more than a few seconds.
One went to the cores and ate them one by one.
"Anyway, the road here is still way too strange."
"Let’s hope the road gets easier ahead." Kain said after looking into the distance and they continued moving.
But unfortunately, during the next two hours, the path became more complicated.

chapters.title: Chapter 504: City Of Silent Light
paragraphs: Sometimes the road between the two high walls became so narrow that One had to slow down.
A few times, parts of the path had completely collapsed, and Lian and Kain had to get off so One could cross the rocky slope.
They stopped for about twenty minutes to eat and drink water.
During that stop, the Celestial Book of Treasure was still open, and the three-hundred-kilometer map that had shown only weak lines at the beginning of the journey had now become much clearer.
The World Memory was also adding more information to it as they moved forward.
Old roads, the locations of former towers that were now ruins, parts of a water supply system, and even what seemed to have been a path for pilgrims.
Everything on the World Memory showed that they really seemed to be heading toward something like a religious place.
However, it was not very surprising either, since according to the natives, their destination was a shrine.
But the center of the region was still unclear.
There were several very large lines there whose nature the Book could not determine, and the golden mark had also become clearer, although not enough to provide complete information.
But there was no longer any doubt that the destination was worth investigating.
[Valuable treasure source has entered the identifiable range.]
[Accurate information is blocked by several unknown obstacles and structures.]
[Accuracy will increase as the distance decreases.]
Since this golden treasure mark was exactly on the same path as them and their destination, Lian guessed that it could be the same thing the natives of the Third Region were looking for.
Of course, this was only a guess and nothing more, and there was also a good chance that he was wrong.
Anyway, their journey continued.
Around the fifth hour, the first clear signs of the natives’ operation appeared.
The wheels of several carts had left marks on the white dirt of the road.
Near one of the turns, several broken boards, ropes, and dark pieces of cloth were lying on the ground.

A little farther ahead, they could see the remains of a temporary camp, and the extinguished fire was still not completely covered by dust, making it clear that the troops had passed through here recently.
Lian slowed One down.
"It looks like there aren’t a few of them," Kain also said after seeing the scene.
A few minutes later, from the top of a small hill, they saw two carts about one kilometer ahead, with six natives accompanying them.

The load of the first cart was covered with cloth, but something large and round was underneath it, and as far as they could see, it seemed to be a metal frame several meters in diameter, with pieces that looked like mirrors attached to its edges.
"They’re taking something inside," Kain said quietly.
"Yeah." Lian looked at their path, if their goal was only to take a treasure out of a ruin, why were they carrying heavy equipment there?
So the operation was not finished yet, maybe the main part had not even started yet.
"Do you think it’s for opening that place?"
"Maybe."
The young Vorhelm went over the words of the captured natives in his mind again.
The priests needed at least three days, and whatever they wanted to open was half open and half closed.
If they were only breaking a door open by force, they could not know with such certainty that it would take three days.
Unless there was a specific amount of work left.
Or
"I think they’re waiting for something to happen."
"What kind of thing?" Kain looked at him.
"I don’t know."
Lian looked at the carts as they slowly disappeared from sight.
"But if they were only opening something, being so exact about the time would be strange."
"You mean something like a door that only opens at a certain time? Or a ritual that can only be performed at a certain time?" Kain thought for a moment.
Lian said nothing this time, that was possible too, but whatever was inside those carts could also be part of it.
They did not enter the fight directly.
If those six people disappeared, there was a chance that a warning would reach the destination faster than they could.
So they waited for a few minutes, and when the carts moved farther away, they started moving again.
Almost six hours had passed since they left the pass, and the road was now squeezed between two huge stone walls.
The sound of the wind moved through the gaps like a long cry.
Under One’s feet, real stone pavement appeared again for the first time in several kilometers, and a complete road was now in front of them.
Both sides of the road were marked by white pillars, most of which were half-broken.
The Celestial Book of Treasure shook, and the map on its page quickly became clearer, while the World Memory also recovered several new structures.
[Old road detected.]
[Historical use: Pilgrim’s Path.]
[Destination name: Damaged information.]
But a few seconds later, the golden mark on the Book became stronger.
[Distance to the main area has decreased.]
One passed through the stone passage, and the road made a gentle turn to the right, then a second turn, and suddenly the giant ant stopped.
This time, Lian had not told it to stop.
Its antennae slowly rose, and its master took his eyes away from the Book, saying nothing for several seconds.
Kain was the same.
All three of them fell silent and stared at the scene in front of them.
Because there was no longer only a road and mountains in front of them, an entire world had opened below them.
At first glance, Lian thought he was looking at a sea, a black area stretched from the bottom of the cliff for several kilometers, and its surface reflected the gray light of the sky.
But the wind passed over it, no waves formed and there was no movement at all, instead, only a thin layer of dust moved across the black surface.
Then he saw the first ship, its huge wooden body was placed at an unnatural angle on the black area.
The main mast was broken and the sails had rotted many years ago, half of its body had sunk into the same black surface.
The entire bottom of what had once been a sea or a huge lake had now turned into a black layer, it was not clear at all what that layer was.
But whatever it was, it was definitely not normal water.
Farther away, more ships could be seen, some had fallen onto their sides and some had been broken in half, and one of them was so large that small buildings could have fit on its deck.
But the view did not end with the sea.
Beside the old shore, there was a city, with white and gray buildings built at several different heights on the rocky slopes.
Half-collapsed domes, wide streets, and stone bridges that crossed between cliffs.
Docks that were now dozens of meters above the black sea, and tall, narrow towers could also be seen in different parts of the city.
Huge statues could be seen in different parts of the city, people wearing long robes with their faces raised toward the sky.
Several statues were also holding a stone sun between their two hands, and in the farthest part of the city, inside the mountain wall, there was a building that made everything around it look small.
Huge white pillars came out from the mountain slope, and a very wide staircase continued from the city level all the way to the entrance.
The main door was closed, but light was coming through a narrow gap between its two sides, a white and warm light that seemed to have life.
In a city where almost everything was dead, only that building was still lit.
It seemed that this was the shrine.
Kain said nothing for several seconds, then his eyes stopped on a ship stuck in the black liquid, and then on the dock that was dozens of meters above it.
"This isn’t a ruin."
Lian was still holding the Book, and the lines on the page became more complete at that moment.
Alleys, towers, districts, and more parts of the city appeared one after another.
The golden mark was also almost directly in the direction of the same huge building.
"No, it’s a city," he said quietly, and his eyes moved across the size of the area.
[City of the Silent Light.]
The wind passed through the passage behind them, moving their clothes, but neither of them moved for several seconds.
Even Lian, who had seen many very strange things during the past few months, could not deny the greatness of the scene.
The first thing that caught his attention after a few minutes was the presence of the natives.
Fresh tents could be seen on several terraces higher in the city, and there were several small camps with people moving between the towers.
On one of the main roads, carts were moving back and forth, and near one of the mirror towers, several people in bright long clothes were working beside a group of soldiers.
The priests.
Two round metal frames were also beside the tower, almost the same as the ones they had seen on the cart.
"Those frames we saw on the way..." Kain pointed at the same place.
"I saw them."
"So they’re not just waiting."
"No. They’re preparing something." Lian examined the structure of the tower for a few seconds.
It was still unclear whether repairing the towers was necessary to open the shrine or for another ritual, but one thing was clear.
The forces of the Third Region had arrived before them, and they had not been doing nothing for a long time either.
Kain looked at the number of forces in the city.
"I think getting down there isn’t going to be a problem with only monsters."
The young Vorhelm looked at one of the old streets that entered the first district from the top of the cliff.
"We already knew that from the pass." Then he made One move again.
They had not gone down from the high area yet.

Kain moved closer.
There were several lines written under the lantern, but the inside of the building was so dark that it was difficult to read them.
He opened his palm, and a small, controlled light formed between his fingers.
Only enough to light up the writing, and then he bent down slightly, but before he could read the sentence... Click.
A very small sound came.
One of the narrow lines on the lantern frame lit up.

Kain immediately turned off his light, but the line did not turn off, instead, a white glow moved down from the frame, entered the base, and then a thin line of light moved across the stone floor from the base.
Lian immediately looked at the city.
Nothing happened for several seconds, but then something moved in one of the nearby towers.
A huge mirror-like panel placed on that tower, which had probably remained still for centuries, slowly turned.
Although it was strange that there was a mirror panel on a tower, they had a more important concern right now.
What exactly was happening...?
KRRRRRRR...
Dust and pieces of stone fell from its edges.
Kain looked at it with his eyes slightly wider, and the mirror continued to move.
It turned until its dark surface was directly facing the building where they were.
A very weak light appeared on it and then reflected, a white line moved from the mirror to a smaller panel on the second tower.

The second mirror shook for a moment and then sent the line of light downward, onto an old staircase, a staircase that had been almost invisible in the shadow of the mountain wall until a few seconds ago.
The light moved across the stones.
Step by step.
Until it reached the first district of the city, and then stopped.
It was as if part of a city that had been dead for centuries had detected their presence.
Kain looked at his now-dark hand and then at the mirror again.
"My god... what was that?"
Lian examined the glowing line beside the lantern, now there was no doubt, the effect of the Tear had not only changed Kain’s talents and Class.
There was something inside his light that even the structures belonging to the Divine of Light could recognize.
"Those natives aren’t the only ones who can recognize your light." He answered after thinking for a moment.
"Is that good or bad?"

sentences.text: Sometimes the road between the two high walls became so narrow that One had to slow down.
A few times, parts of the path had completely collapsed, and Lian and Kain had to get off so One could cross the rocky slope.
They stopped for about twenty minutes to eat and drink water.
During that stop, the Celestial Book of Treasure was still open, and the three-hundred-kilometer map that had shown only weak lines at the beginning of the journey had now become much clearer.
The World Memory was also adding more information to it as they moved forward.
Old roads, the locations of former towers that were now ruins, parts of a water supply system, and even what seemed to have been a path for pilgrims.
Everything on the World Memory showed that they really seemed to be heading toward something like a religious place.
However, it was not very surprising either, since according to the natives, their destination was a shrine.
But the center of the region was still unclear.
There were several very large lines there whose nature the Book could not determine, and the golden mark had also become clearer, although not enough to provide complete information.
But there was no longer any doubt that the destination was worth investigating.
[Valuable treasure source has entered the identifiable range.]
[Accurate information is blocked by several unknown obstacles and structures.]
[Accuracy will increase as the distance decreases.]
Since this golden treasure mark was exactly on the same path as them and their destination, Lian guessed that it could be the same thing the natives of the Third Region were looking for.
Of course, this was only a guess and nothing more, and there was also a good chance that he was wrong.
Anyway, their journey continued.
Around the fifth hour, the first clear signs of the natives’ operation appeared.
The wheels of several carts had left marks on the white dirt of the road.
Near one of the turns, several broken boards, ropes, and dark pieces of cloth were lying on the ground.

A little farther ahead, they could see the remains of a temporary camp, and the extinguished fire was still not completely covered by dust, making it clear that the troops had passed through here recently.
Lian slowed One down.
"It looks like there aren’t a few of them," Kain also said after seeing the scene.
A few minutes later, from the top of a small hill, they saw two carts about one kilometer ahead, with six natives accompanying them.

The load of the first cart was covered with cloth, but something large and round was underneath it, and as far as they could see, it seemed to be a metal frame several meters in diameter, with pieces that looked like mirrors attached to its edges.
"They’re taking something inside," Kain said quietly.
"Yeah." Lian looked at their path, if their goal was only to take a treasure out of a ruin, why were they carrying heavy equipment there?
So the operation was not finished yet, maybe the main part had not even started yet.
"Do you think it’s for opening that place?"
"Maybe."
The young Vorhelm went over the words of the captured natives in his mind again.
The priests needed at least three days, and whatever they wanted to open was half open and half closed.
If they were only breaking a door open by force, they could not know with such certainty that it would take three days.
Unless there was a specific amount of work left.
Or
"I think they’re waiting for something to happen."
"What kind of thing?" Kain looked at him.
"I don’t know."
Lian looked at the carts as they slowly disappeared from sight.
"But if they were only opening something, being so exact about the time would be strange."
"You mean something like a door that only opens at a certain time?
Or a ritual that can only be performed at a certain time?" Kain thought for a moment.
Lian said nothing this time, that was possible too, but whatever was inside those carts could also be part of it.
They did not enter the fight directly.
If those six people disappeared, there was a chance that a warning would reach the destination faster than they could.
So they waited for a few minutes, and when the carts moved farther away, they started moving again.
Almost six hours had passed since they left the pass, and the road was now squeezed between two huge stone walls.
The sound of the wind moved through the gaps like a long cry.
Under One’s feet, real stone pavement appeared again for the first time in several kilometers, and a complete road was now in front of them.
Both sides of the road were marked by white pillars, most of which were half-broken.
The Celestial Book of Treasure shook, and the map on its page quickly became clearer, while the World Memory also recovered several new structures.
[Old road detected.]
[Historical use: Pilgrim’s Path.]
[Destination name: Damaged information.]
But a few seconds later, the golden mark on the Book became stronger.
[Distance to the main area has decreased.]
One passed through the stone passage, and the road made a gentle turn to the right, then a second turn, and suddenly the giant ant stopped.
This time, Lian had not told it to stop.
Its antennae slowly rose, and its master took his eyes away from the Book, saying nothing for several seconds.
Kain was the same.
All three of them fell silent and stared at the scene in front of them.
Because there was no longer only a road and mountains in front of them, an entire world had opened below them.
At first glance, Lian thought he was looking at a sea, a black area stretched from the bottom of the cliff for several kilometers, and its surface reflected the gray light of the sky.
But the wind passed over it, no waves formed and there was no movement at all, instead, only a thin layer of dust moved across the black surface.
Then he saw the first ship, its huge wooden body was placed at an unnatural angle on the black area.
The main mast was broken and the sails had rotted many years ago, half of its body had sunk into the same black surface.
The entire bottom of what had once been a sea or a huge lake had now turned into a black layer, it was not clear at all what that layer was.
But whatever it was, it was definitely not normal water.
Farther away, more ships could be seen, some had fallen onto their sides and some had been broken in half, and one of them was so large that small buildings could have fit on its deck.
But the view did not end with the sea.
Beside the old shore, there was a city, with white and gray buildings built at several different heights on the rocky slopes.
Half-collapsed domes, wide streets, and stone bridges that crossed between cliffs.
Docks that were now dozens of meters above the black sea, and tall, narrow towers could also be seen in different parts of the city.
Huge statues could be seen in different parts of the city, people wearing long robes with their faces raised toward the sky.
Several statues were also holding a stone sun between their two hands, and in the farthest part of the city, inside the mountain wall, there was a building that made everything around it look small.
Huge white pillars came out from the mountain slope, and a very wide staircase continued from the city level all the way to the entrance.
The main door was closed, but light was coming through a narrow gap between its two sides, a white and warm light that seemed to have life.
In a city where almost everything was dead, only that building was still lit.
It seemed that this was the shrine.
Kain said nothing for several seconds, then his eyes stopped on a ship stuck in the black liquid, and then on the dock that was dozens of meters above it.

Lian was still holding the Book, and the lines on the page became more complete at that moment.
Alleys, towers, districts, and more parts of the city appeared one after another.
The golden mark was also almost directly in the direction of the same huge building.

The priests.

chapters.title: Chapter 505: The City That Should Be Dead
paragraphs: "Is that good or bad?" Kain asked without taking his eyes off the mirror panel that was still slowly turning.
Lian did not answer immediately.
His eyes first moved to the thin line of light that had come down from the tower and stretched along the old stairs beside the mountain wall.
Only a few seconds ago, that path had been almost completely hidden in the shadows, and even the Celestial Book of Treasure had only shown an incomplete line in that direction.
But now, the white stairs had appeared one after another through the shadows.
He opened the Book again.
The local map created by the Book was clearer than it had been a few minutes ago.
The World Memory also reacted as soon as the new path appeared and placed new information on the same part of the map.
[Historical structure detected.]
[Pilgrim’s Path.]
[Recorded destination: White District.]
Then he looked at Kain.

"If it only showed us the path, that’s good, but if it also told the rest of the city that the owner of the Tear has arrived... then probably not." They had no way to know whether what happened was some kind of special mechanism or not.
What if it was some kind of special mechanism that reacted to something specific? In that case, it was possible that all the forces of the Third Region that had come here would notice their presence.
Kain stayed silent for a few seconds, then let out a short sigh and looked at the city below them again.
The mirror panel was no longer moving, and the thin line of light was still fixed on the same stairs.
For now, no bell had sounded from the native camps, and no group was moving toward them either.
But Lian had no interest in checking how long this situation would continue.
"We’re moving."
Kain nodded.
One also moved its antennae from a few steps behind them.
Even when the giant ant kept its body low, it was still not something that could be hidden behind a pillar or a small wall.
"I don’t think with that size, even if it hides behind a wall, anyone would believe it’s a rock, shouldn’t you cancel its summoning?" Kain reminded him of this before they moved.
"It’s not time yet." Lian did not plan to send it back to the Colony House for now. They were still in the outer part of the city, and they did not know what kind of monsters lived there.
One was not only useful for moving quickly, but its tough body and raw strength were also very valuable against ordinary monsters.
When they got closer to the main forces of the Third Region, he could send One back at that time.
For now, having a several-meter-tall monster beside them was more of an advantage than a problem.
They left the old pilgrim rest area and entered the glowing stairs.
From above, the City of the Silent Light had a huge and even impressive view.
But the farther down they went, the more the beauty of the view was replaced by something more unpleasant.
The stairs were extremely wide, and hundreds of people could probably pass through them at the same time in the past.
On both sides of the stairs, small stone pillars had been built at regular distances.
As the young Vorhelm passed the first pillar, he noticed writing on it.
A name.
Another name was carved on the next pillar.
And then hundreds of other pillars and hundreds of other names had been carved on them, to the point that it seemed like some kind of tradition or ritual.
"Are those the names of the pilgrims?" Kain asked while examining one of the writings.
Lian activated the World Memory on the same part of the map.
[Pilgrim Memorial Pillar.]
"Looks like it." There was no explanation, but the name itself could partly confirm their guess.
Some names had almost disappeared, while some could still be seen on the stone with faint golden lines.

But several pillars were different, their surfaces had turned black, and it did not look like smoke or stains, the stone itself seemed to have burned from the inside, and the letters on it had completely melted.
Lian gave one of them a short look and continued without stopping.
A few hundred stairs later, they saw the first statue.
A woman in a kneeling position.
Both of her hands were placed in front of her chest, and her face was slightly raised toward the sky.
Kain did not even slow down at first, the city was full of statues, and he saw no reason to stop just because of one statue.
But Lian stopped, something about the statue was not natural and it gave him a strange feeling, he needed to check it.
The surface of the woman’s body was not stone, under a black and semi-transparent layer, the dried skin of her face could still be seen.
Her eyes were closed and her lips were slightly open, even strands of her hair had been preserved inside the same layer.
"This isn’t a statue." Lian said quietly, causing Kain to frown heavily and giving him a bad feeling.
One also came closer and moved its antennae.
A few meters lower, there was another statue, a man with one hand held in front of his face.
Then a third, a child beside another woman, and all of them were in different positions, but they had one thing in common, they had been stopped at the exact moment.
It was as if the same black layer that had trapped the ships had held the bodies of these people at the exact last moment.
There were some kind of black stains on them that seemed to be the same liquid that had trapped the ships inside it.
Kain and Lian both looked at them in silence, for some time they did not know how they should react.
"Did they die just like this, in that moment? But how?" The first one asked after thinking for a while.
The second one could not be sure, his eyes moved between the different statues.

"Yeah, if they had turned into statues after death, it would be unlikely for all of them to be exactly in the positions they were in while doing something, their deaths and being frozen happened at the same time."
"Then whatever destroyed this city... happened very quickly." Kain kept his eyes on the woman’s face.
Lian said nothing, but it was probably like that, whatever had happened had happened in the blink of an eye, and it probably had something to do with that black liquid.
They started moving again, and the farther down they went, the more of these statues they saw.
The map of the Book was also becoming more complete at the same time, as the distance became shorter, the faint lines of the districts gained more details.
Alleys that had previously been only a single line now had several branches.
Small buildings, courtyards, temples, and even part of the city’s water supply system slowly appeared on the page.
The golden treasure mark shown by the Book was still deep inside the city, almost in the same direction as the huge shrine.
But now other marks had also appeared, a white mark on the left side of the path, a blue mark under one of the lower streets, and several much weaker points inside scattered buildings.
Lian looked at the map, the white mark was almost eight hundred meters away from their path.
But one of the native camps was between them and the destination.
It was not worth making the natives aware of their presence for a treasure that was probably even below Rank C.
He preferred to explore more of the city before getting into a fight.
A few minutes later, the Book reacted again, this time the small mark was almost beside their path.
Lian moved only a few meters away from the main stairs and entered the courtyard of a half-ruined temple, a small white plant was growing in the middle of the shadow of one of the pillars.
Its leaves had almost no color, and their edges looked very soft, like ash.
The Book showed a short amount of information.
[Light Ash Flower.]
[Rank: C.]
[Usage: A medicinal material used to reduce damage caused by curses.]
Lian pulled the plant out with some of the soil around its roots and placed it inside his storage space.
Kain had also seen these things, but since a few hours ago, he had understood that his friend was good at finding treasures, or that it might have something to do with the map he was carrying.
Whatever it was, he had gotten used to it and did not seem to care about it anymore.
Instead, he tried to search through the half-ruined temple for information about the Divine of Light or anything related to himself.
But after they found nothing, they returned to their path.
It did not take long before the stairs finally ended.
The System immediately showed a new notification.
[Sub-area discovered.]
[White District.]
The district looked very different from what they had seen from above, white buildings had been built on both sides of arched streets.
Stone pools were placed between small squares, but no water had flowed through them for a very long time.
In some places, narrow channels reached the pools from the walls of the buildings.
There were also statues in different places that held large circular panels above their heads.
But something other than the architecture caught Lian’s attention.
The shadows... or more exactly, the lack of them.
The sun was behind a layer of clouds, yet no corner of the street was completely dark.
Very weak light came through the stones of some buildings, not strong enough to make the area look bright, but only enough to prevent complete darkness from forming.
"It’s bright even in the shadows, how is something like this possible? Is it some kind of city mechanism?" Kain also noticed it.
The young Vorhelm placed his hand beside one of the walls, faint light was coming from inside the stone itself.
"Yeah, since it was a religious city that belonged to the religion of Light, maybe they liked light too much and didn’t allow darkness to exist."
"But how? Then what did they do at night... or don’t tell me they didn’t even have nights? Then how did they sleep?"
"You shouldn’t ask me these questions, actually, I should be asking you these questions, after all, you’re the Child Of Light, right?" Lian gave him a mocking look.
Kain ignored him and they continued along their path.
One entered the street from a few steps behind them, its huge body taking up almost half the width of the street.
But only a few minutes had passed when its antennae suddenly rose, it had sensed danger!
Lian also sensed danger at the same moment, more exactly, six unknown presences were approaching them.
Six of them, and they were inside the surrounding buildings.
Kain also stopped at the same time as them and looked around, his sense of danger was no weaker than theirs either.
He created a small light between his fingers, and when they felt his light, the first creature came out from behind a pillar.
At first glance, it was a human, or at least, it had once been human...

There were also statues in different places that held large circular panels above their heads.
But something other than the architecture caught Lian’s attention.
The shadows... or more exactly, the lack of them.
The sun was behind a layer of clouds, yet no corner of the street was completely dark.
Very weak light came through the stones of some buildings, not strong enough to make the area look bright, but only enough to prevent complete darkness from forming.
"It’s bright even in the shadows, how is something like this possible?
Is it some kind of city mechanism?" Kain also noticed it.
The young Vorhelm placed his hand beside one of the walls, faint light was coming from inside the stone itself.
"Yeah, since it was a religious city that belonged to the religion of Light, maybe they liked light too much and didn’t allow darkness to exist."
"But how?
Then what did they do at night... or don’t tell me they didn’t even have nights?
Then how did they sleep?"
"You shouldn’t ask me these questions, actually, I should be asking you these questions, after all, you’re the Child Of Light, right?" Lian gave him a mocking look.
Kain ignored him and they continued along their path.
One entered the street from a few steps behind them, its huge body taking up almost half the width of the street.
But only a few minutes had passed when its antennae suddenly rose, it had sensed danger!
Lian also sensed danger at the same moment, more exactly, six unknown presences were approaching them.
Six of them, and they were inside the surrounding buildings.
Kain also stopped at the same time as them and looked around, his sense of danger was no weaker than theirs either.
He created a small light between his fingers, and when they felt his light, the first creature came out from behind a pillar.
At first glance, it was a human, or at least, it had once been human...

chapters.title: Chapter 506: The Square of Confession
paragraphs: The creature had a dry and cracked body, a white and rotten robe still hanging from its shoulders, and the skin on its hands was cracked and almost without color.
And stranger than that was the fact that it had no face, a smooth white layer like wax covered everything from its forehead to under its chin, without any eyes, nose, or mouth.
And in the center of its chest, there was an empty circular hole.
[Hollow Pilgrim.]
[Rank: Normal.]
[Level: 31.]
The creature slowly walked toward them, but it was not alone and a second one came out of the nearby building.
[Level: 28.]
A third.
A fourth.
In less than a few seconds, six Hollow Pilgrims spread out on both sides of the street, but their movements were slow. They did not even look threatening.
The first Hollow Pilgrim came forward and was almost ten meters away from them.
Kain had not turned off the light yet and the Pilgrim’s head turned toward the light in his hand for a moment and then toward Lian.
Lian released a very small amount of mana and the creature’s head turned again.
He wanted to see if these monsters only reacted to light or if they reacted to any form of energy.
If it was the first one, it could mean that there was a deeper meaning behind them but if it was the second one, then they were like any other monster.
And this thing reacted to mana too.
"It is not only light."
"What?"
"They can sense fresh mana, simply put, they are like any normal monster, there is no need to worry about this."
Lian turned off his mana again.
The creature hesitated for a fraction of a second, but the Pilgrim standing in front of Kain reacted more strongly to his light and started moving closer.
He watched its movement, the monster was still slow but then suddenly as the creature got closer, its body bent down and the dry muscles in its legs contracted in an unnatural way.
At that moment, the Hunter’s instincts warned him of danger.
BOOOM!
The stone under the Pilgrim’s feet broke.
The creature that had been walking at the speed of an old human only a moment ago closed the distance in a fraction of a second.
Kain did not even have time to say a word, but Lian raised his hand and placed his palm directly on the creature’s white face.
TAK!
All of the Pilgrim’s momentum stopped right there.
Its feet stayed off the ground for a moment and its dried body shook from the sudden stop.
But his hand did not move back even a few centimeters.
Kain only watched for a few moments and sighed, this thing’s speed had been so high for a moment that even he could not follow it with his eyes.
But the young Vorhelm turned his hand and the Pilgrim’s body changed direction in the air.
BOOM!
Its back crashed into the white wall, the force was so strong that the stone cracked.
Kain moved at the same moment, the light around his palm became concentrated and his direct attack hit the center of the creature’s chest, right inside the hole.
For a moment, a golden symbol lit up inside the Pilgrim’s body, shaped like a circle with several lines coming from the center.
"Did you see that?"
"Yeah."
The light became stronger.
BOOM!
The Pilgrim’s body became weak and it fell down from the wall.
[You killed a Level 28 Hollow Pilgrim.]
The other Pilgrims attacked at the same moment and this time all of them moved quickly and did not waste any more time, it was clear that they had understood that they were facing dangerous enemies.
Two of them went directly toward Kain.
One moved in front of one of them, the Pilgrim jumped onto one of the ant’s front legs without fear and its dry claws scratched across One’s natural armor.
KRRRK!
A thin line was left behind and at the same moment One lowered his head, his jaws closed.
TAK!
The upper half of the Pilgrim’s body was caught between his jaws and the giant ant lifted it from the ground and then slammed it directly into the stone street.
BOOM!
The street broke, the creature still tried to stand up but Kain moved past One and sent a beam of light into the hole in its chest.
The inner symbol lit up for a moment and the creature’s body stopped moving.
[You killed a Level 27 Hollow Pilgrim.]
Another Pilgrim attacked from Lian’s right side, he allowed it to come closer and when its dry hand was only a few centimeters away from his face, he grabbed its wrist.
He took one step forward and moved his shoulder under the creature’s body, then the monster passed over his shoulder like a piece of wood and fell to the ground.
CRACK!
The young Vorhelm put his foot on its chest and the bones broke, but the creature still moved, as if this attack was not enough to kill it.
He looked at the hole in its chest, so the main weak point was really there, he tried to target that point with lightning or normal mana.
But it still had no effect, it seemed that they needed the Light Element to kill these creatures.
"Kain."
"Got it"
The light came from the other side of the street and entered the hole, the Pilgrim stopped and its body became completely lifeless.
In less than two minutes, all six creatures had fallen to the ground.
Lian knelt beside the first corpse, put his finger inside the edge of the hole, there was no natural structure there, the hole had not been a part of their bodies from the beginning.
Something had come out of their chest or had been removed.
Kain stood beside him.
"What do you think was there?"
"I don’t know, whatever it was, maybe it was one of their internal organs, the hole is in the chest so logically it should be the heart, but the heart is still in its place, so God knows."
He was still not sure either, who had even done this to these former humans?
At that moment, a very weak sound came from the top of one of the buildings.
Without raising his head, Lian sensed the presences, four people were coming closer and these were humans.
They had probably noticed them since the fight had started and had been watching them.
Their battle had not made much noise but it was still a battle and it was normal for it to attract attention.
Kain noticed it after a few seconds as well, his gaze went up and what he saw was one of the soldiers of Region Three, crouching beside the edge of the rooftop.
He was holding a thin and cylindrical device in his hand and a red light was gathering at its tip, something like a warning signal.
"These are outsiders." One of the people behind the soldier said in a low voice.
"Then what were those idiots doing? Weren’t they supposed to stop outsiders from passing?"
"Looks like these two escaped from them."
"Quick, catch them before they escape!"
