chapters.title: Chapter 507: Oops, They Found Us
paragraphs: Lian turned his attention toward them, and noticed that the soldier holding the signal had placed his finger on the activation part.
He did not stay still either.
[Grave Fang.]
Two mana jaws formed on both sides of the soldier’s arm.
"What the fuck is this?"
TAK!
The jaws closed and stopped the movement of his hand and at the same moment the device fell from between his fingers.
Tak.
It fell onto the roof.
The man looked at his restrained arm in shock, then looked down but Lian was no longer there.
[Ashen Thunder Step.]
BOOM!
A line of lightning went up the wall and at the same moment one of the soldiers drew his sword to prepare for battle.
But the young Vorhelm was coming directly toward him, the man brought his blade down but just before Lian’s body hit him, his body turned into ash.
A gray stream twisted past the edge of the blade and took shape again through the broken window on the upper floor.
The soldier only had time to turn his head and now Lian was behind him.
The man turned his sword back but he also placed two fingers on his wrist.

The path of the blade was redirected and with his other hand, he struck the side of his neck, the man’s body became weak and before he could fall to the ground, Lian grabbed his collar and gently let him down beside the wall.
"Die, foreign barbarian!" The second soldier also attacked and his fist was covered in light.
The young Vorhelm easily moved the attack aside and his elbow hit the man’s stomach.
TAK!
The man fell to his knees.
But the third person did not fight and instead jumped from the rooftop and quickly ran toward the opposite direction.
"Someone is running away!" Kain shouted from below.
"Instead of shouting, go catch him yourself." Lian turned around.
The man landed on the roof of a lower building, his legs bent, but before Kain or he had a chance to move, he pulled something small from his clothes and pressed it.
FSSSH!
A yellow spark went up from there, toward one of the nearby towers, the small signal hit the wall of the tower and a point of light appeared for a moment...then disappeared.
Lian could have caught the man, but it no longer mattered, the message had been sent, however, he still did not let the soldier escape.
A few seconds later, he caught the soldier with a simple movement and put him on the ground.
When he returned, Kain was coming up.
"Well... I guess our stealth ends here." He looked at the point where the warning light had disappeared.
The young Vorhelm looked at the area from the edge of the building, surprisingly, no group was coming toward them yet.
"We continue on our path, we would have had to face them sooner or later anyway." Lian added without worry.
The bright path continued, but only until a large square in the center of the White District and when they entered the square, they understood why.
Twelve different streets came out from it, some going toward the lower parts of the city and some toward the higher areas.
Two paths also went toward the main shrine, but the light only fell on one of them.
And that path did not go directly to the shrine, instead, it reached another tower with a mirror at a distance.
"Do we have to light these one by one?" Kain looked at the path for a few seconds and then at the first tower behind them.
Lian looked at the map.
[Pilgrim Guidance System.]
[Status: Most sections are inactive.]
[Path Towers: Incomplete information.]
"Or at least we need to find out where this path is supposed to take us."
"What I see is that the priests of Region Three are using those metal frames to force the same thing I did by turning on a light." Kain stood with his hands on his waist.
The young Vorhelm had thought the same thing, if it was true, Kain was not only a carrier of a sacred artifact for this city.
He could activate systems that the priests needed equipment and time to use and that meant they had an advantage.
On the western side of the square, a large mural was still mostly intact.
[Square of the Light Confession.]
They stood in front of the wall, pilgrims were standing in lines in the picture.
In front of each one, there was a priest holding something like a lantern.
But the strangest part was below the pilgrims’ feet, more precisely, their shadows.
In the picture, the priest shone the light on each person and their shadow was unnaturally separated from the ground and pulled into a black container.
"What is this?" Kain asked with a frown.
Lian checked the remaining writing, most of it had been destroyed, but some of it could still be read.
[The one who wishes for pure light must first see what they hide behind them.]
What The Fuck?
"So they were really taking their shadows?" Kain read the sentence again.
"Maybe it was symbolic."
"You said that very hopefully, but how can taking someone’s shadow be symbolic?"
Lian looked at the picture of the priest, of course, he had said that sentence as a joke, at first glance, taking someone’s shadow might not seem like something wrong.
But how could such a thing be normal?
The Divine Ritual of Light was apparently not as simple as just seeing light as something pure and holy.
For them, light revealed things and anything that could be against the light had to be destroyed.
This could even include shadows.

"I expected the Ritual of Light to be something logical and fair and stuff like that, but these traditions are giving me a bad feeling, it feels like they were crazy or something." Kain let out a short sigh.

"I guess they were too extreme, besides, we cannot say it was a bad thing, maybe it looks unreasonable from our point of view, but until we understand the purpose behind it, we cannot fully judge it." The young Vorhelm answered simply.
"You’re right... maybe we should not judge too quickly.
"That’s right, but anyway, whatever it was, luckily it has nothing to do with me."
"Ha!" Kain looked unhappily at his so-called best friend.
They crossed the square. The path of light passed beside a tall building whose wall had partly collapsed.
Through the gap between the buildings, the black area below the city could be seen again.
This time, it was much closer.
"I still don’t understand what that place down there is."
Lian did not understand either, from this distance, its surface looked even more like a solid material than before.
But in some places, the reflections were too deep, as if there was something under the upper layer.
And then there was no doubt that something was moving inside it.
At first, Lian thought it was the reflection of a cloud, but no, a huge shadow moved under the black surface.
It was perhaps more than fifty meters long, its exact body could not be seen and there was only a very large dark spot that slowly passed under one of the broken ships.
The surface did not make any waves but along the path where the shadow passed, old cracks began to glow with a very weak light for a few seconds.
"Don’t tell me something is living under there." Kain stayed still for a few seconds and then said.
The young Vorhelm kept his eyes on the shadow and a few seconds later... it disappeared.
"Okay."
"Okay what?" Kain turned his head toward him.
"I’m not going to say something is living down there."
"Bastard."
Lian moved, for now, they had no good reason to get close to that area and if a fifty-meter creature really lived under it, it could stay there.
Almost half an hour later, the second tower appeared in front of them, the tower was much taller than it had looked from a distance.
Most of it was made of white stone, but the upper part was covered by a huge dark plate.
Fresh equipment could be seen around the base of the tower.
Several circular metal frames, mana crystals, and wires that connected the frames to old grooves on the tower.
"It’s the same thing we saw on the carriage." Kain knelt beside one of them to examine it.
Lian examined it as well.
The locals had apparently worked on this tower for hours or even days.
Some crystals were empty and several parts of the frames were warm but the tower was still not fully active.
The forces responsible for it were not there at the moment.
They had probably gone to rest or after the previous warning, some of the forces had moved to check the area.
Kain went closer to the center of the tower, there was a circular groove there, exactly like the frame of the first lantern that had reacted to his light and turned on.
Both of them looked at it, it was clear what they had to do.
"Do we have another way?" The Child Of Light said after thinking for a moment.
"No." Lian shook his head, it was clear that they had to do this to open the shrine, almost all the evidence pointed to it.
And since they had come this far, they also had no reason to retreat.
Kain placed his hand on the groove, nothing happened for a moment and then he released a very small amount of light from his palm.

Kain placed his hand on the groove, nothing happened for a moment and then he released a very small amount of light from his palm.

chapters.title: Chapter 508: The Tear of Witness
paragraphs: The first line lit up.
Then the second.
The third.
All of the metal frames that the priests had installed around the tower lit up at the same time.
He immediately pulled his hand back, but it was already too late, the huge mirror at the top of the tower moved.
Krrrrrrrr...
Dust fell from its edges and the plate started to turn.
At the same moment, light came from behind them, from the first tower, a white beam moved hundreds of meters above the buildings and hit the mirror of this tower directly.
The surface of the mirror lit up, for one second it was so bright that the two of them had to narrow their eyes a little.
Then the second tower caught the beam, turned, and sent the light into the depths of the city.
The third tower.
Tak.
It lit up and caught the next beam, then the fourth tower, then the fifth, of course, this did not happen throughout the entire city but only a specific chain of towers lit up, but that was enough.
For a few seconds, a huge white path of light appeared across the entire dead city, from the upper entrance to the depths of the area.
In one of the Region Three camps in the city, a priest who was standing beside a table full of maps raised his head.
The light from the third tower fell onto the wall of the tent, the man only watched it for a few seconds.
Another priest came outside and when the fourth tower lit up, the color left his face.
"This is impossible."
The high priest who was standing beside one of the half-completed frames slowly raised his head.
His eyes followed the path of light.
The fifth tower.
The fourth.
The third.
The second.
Then directly toward the same district where Lian and Kain were.
His eyes narrowed and he said only one sentence.
"They are there."
A few seconds later... DOOOOOOONG!
A huge bell rang in the camp, its sound spread between the buildings and then a second bell... DOOOOOOONG!
In different parts of the city, the forces of Region Three came out of their tents, soldiers picked up their weapons, and the patrols changed their routes.
And the priests one after another looked toward the towers that had lit up.
"I think they know exactly where we are now." Kain listened to the sound of the bells from beside the tower.
Lian opened the Heavenly Book of Treasures, this time the map had changed, the barrier that had kept the central area unclear until now had moved back.
The golden treasure mark became clearer.
[Treasure Information Updated.]
[The main source is located deep inside the shrine.]
[Path identified.]
A golden line appeared on the map, from the second tower, to the third and from there to the fourth and finally to the Shrine of Light.
He had already guessed that the treasure was in the shrine, but now the book had confirmed it too.
Kain listened to the bells that were waking the dead city one after another.
Then a thin light formed between his fingers.
"Looks like we can’t delay the confrontation anymore." Then his eyes fell on a group of Region Three soldiers who had reached the end of the street they were on.
DOOOOOONG!
The sound of the first bell passed through the towers of the Silent Light city.
A few moments later, the second bell answered, and before the first echo had completely disappeared from the abandoned streets, the third one also rang.
Lian closed the Celestial Book of Treasure.

Soldiers were coming out of the tents, guards were taking positions on the bridges, and groups that had been scattered around the city until a few moments ago were moving toward the mirror tower from several different paths.
Kain took his eyes away from the street below.
But the ordinary soldiers were not what caught their main attention.
Three stronger presences were moving among the crowd, coming from three different directions.
All three were wearing light-colored clothes under their light armor and, unlike the soldiers, they were not carrying normal weapons.
The first one was carrying a long staff with a golden ring at its end, the second had several thin tablets tied around his arm, and the third only had a white circular seal on his chest.
If he had to guess their levels based only on their presence, they were at least Level 39.
They were three priests who seemed to be leading the forces of Region Three.
None of them was a serious threat to Lian alone, they were not even an ordinary threat.
But looking at the mirror towers around them, he doubted they would fight alone, he did not know why, but he had a bad feeling about them and his instincts were warning him to be careful.
His instincts had never been wrong before.
Kain gathered light around his fingers again.
"About thirty soldiers are getting close, but three of them are more interesting."
"So you noticed too?" The young Vorhelm looked at his friend.
"Yeah, they give me a bad feeling too."
One moved a little forward.
Its antennae were raised, and its huge body almost completely blocked the entrance of one of the streets.
Lian sent a short command through the link.
Don’t kill them for now.
One sent a very slight feeling of dissatisfaction.
"Maybe I will let you later." Lian said quietly.
"You talked to One?" Kain looked at him.
"Yeah."
"What did you tell him?"
"Don’t eat people for now."
"I really don’t know when I should understand that you are joking." Kain looked at One for a few seconds.
The first group of soldiers entered the square.
Six came from the northern path, eight came from the stone bridge, and more than ten came from the street that led directly from the main camp.
None of them attacked immediately, the reason was obvious.
One.
The presence of the giant ant in the center of the square was enough to make even trained people slow down for a moment.
But then several of them noticed Kain.
"Outsiders!" one of the soldiers shouted loudly.

"Honored priests, what do you order us to do with them? They are barbarian outsiders! Whatever judgment you make, we will deal with them accordingly." The commander of the group turned toward the priests and asked in a very respectful and somewhat fanatical tone.
Lian and Kain both turned their attention toward the priests, they somewhat wanted to see whether the priests of this religion of light were the kind who were kind or not.
"They are stains that entered the city."
"Kill them. If they resist, it only proves that they have something to hide." The priest who seemed to be the leader of the other two priests said calmly.
"Light was not given to forgive everyone, they must be punished for existing in our holy city."
"The light decides what is worthy and their blood will make the light pure."
None of the priests seemed interested in forgiving them.
The commander of the group then turned his eyes toward his soldiers.
"You heard the orders! Kill the barbarians!"
"They are really good at welcoming guests." Kain gave a smile without any happiness.
"You know, I expected more from the religion of light, I guess I expected the wrong thing."
Two arrows made of light came from the building in front of them.
He raised his hands, a dense layer of light formed in front of his body for a moment.
Tak! Tak!
Both arrows were deflected and hit the wall behind him, the white stone cracked and then he moved his right hand forward.
A short beam of light was fired, directly toward the archer, although the archer immediately activated a defensive skill.
The beam of light broke through the defensive skill but was deflected and hit beside him.
Boom!
The wall behind the man exploded and he was forced to jump backward.
Kain was still looking at him when one of the three priests entered the square, his steps were slow and he did not seem to consider these outsiders a threat.
Then he completely stopped and his eyes fixed on the light around Kain’s hand, for a few seconds, he did not even pay attention to One or Lian anymore.
"Wait!"

chapters.title: Chapter 509: This Light Faith Is Not Very Friendly
paragraphs: "Wait!"
His command made everyone stop.
The priest took one step forward, the light around Kain’s fingers was still moving and the man’s eyes opened slightly wider.
"That light ..." He looked carefully for a few seconds and then the color of his face changed.
His first disbelief was replaced by something close to anger.
"This is The Tear of Witness..."
Kain stayed silent for a moment, Lian also heard the word.
Tear of Witness.
So they finally had a more specific name for it, although this name seemed more like a local name than something completely accurate.
"Honored priest, are you sure?" The commander of the soldiers looked at the priest.
"I am sure, this is sacred light, only the Tear of Witness can create such pure light, this is the outsider who stole the Tear of Witness! The same tear that the Divine Of Light created for us!"
"Outsider! Return that tear and you will be forgiven!" One of the priests turned toward Kain and said calmly.
"Forgiven? The tear itself chose me, I am not going to return something to people who wanted to kill me until a few moments ago." Kain looked at them with mockery
"Look at him. He carries the sacred light and still refuses to return it, he must be punished!" The youngest priest said with disgust.
"He is touching the light with those filthy hands."
"That light does not belong to you, outsider."
"You stole something that was never meant for you. Do you really think you have the right to use it?" The elder priest looked at Kain with hidden anger, still trying to keep his anger under control.
"Stealing? The tear itself chose me, what is my fault if your god thinks you are useless?" Kain said honestly.
Lian barely held back his laughter.
But this only increased the tension.
All three priests could no longer hold back their anger.
"Capture that outsider alive!"
"And do not worry. We will cut those hands off before taking the Tear back."
"Capture that one alive!" The commander did not waste even a moment thinking.
Several soldiers immediately changed their formation, the people who had been surrounding One until a moment ago changed their path.
"Here we go again." Kain gave Lian a quick look.
"At least we know its name this time."
"That was very helpful, but isn’t Divine Of Light’s Tear better? Why would they call it the Tear of Witness?"

"It seems that Tear of Witness is more like a special name rather than a name everyone uses, if you noticed, the other natives of Region Three we encountered called it Divine Of Light’s Tear." Lian answered after thinking for a moment.
This was the first time they had heard the words Tear of Witness, and the person who had used them was a priest.
The priests might have a completely different view of the tear, and because of that, they used a more specific name for it.
"You barbarian outsiders do not deserve to have the Tear of Witness! I will take it back." The priest then said in a calm and emotionless tone, but with complete certainty.
The first soldier closed the distance, his spear was covered in light and its tip was coming directly toward Kain’s shoulder.
But before he entered attack range, Lian was already in front of him, the attacker did not even understand what had happened for a moment.
He grabbed the body of the spear with one hand, the man immediately tried to pull it back but ...the spear did not move.
The young Vorhelm turned his body, and the attacker was lifted off the ground together with his own weapon.
Boom!
His back crashed into the stone floor of the square.
Lian released the spear and moved forward without stopping, the second soldier came from the right and his short sword cut a fast line toward Lian’s side.
He moved half a step to the side, the edge of the blade passed in front of his clothes, his hand landed on the man’s shoulder.
He applied a little pressure ...that was all.
Crack!
The soldier’s body hit a stone pillar and fell to the ground.
Three more moved forward at the same time, one from above, the second directly from the front, and the third from the side, but Lian did not even look at all three of them.
He grabbed the first soldier’s hand, spun the soldier’s body in the air, and used that same body as an attack.
Boom!
The other two soldiers went down under the weight of their own companion.
Kain, who was fighting two attackers several meters away, looked over for a moment.
"Leave some for me too, I want to see what fighting other Light Element users is like."
Lian grabbed the wrist of another soldier and pulled his weapon out of his hand.
"We don’t have time to waste, if you really want to fight them then be faster."
Kain smiled and said nothing else, an attacker came from behind him, and he allowed him to get close first.
A moment before the attack landed, the light around his left hand became dense like a cover, the attacker’s forearm hit it and its path was deflected.
Kain placed his other palm on the man’s chest.
Boom!
A wave of light pushed him several meters backward.
The next soldier swung his sword from below to above, he took one step backward, allowed the blade to pass in front of him, and then sent a short beam toward the ground beside the attacker.
Tak!
The stone exploded and the man lost his balance.
Kain pushed him away with his glowing fist, it was not bad for himself.
But the real difference in power became clear when four more soldiers moved toward him at the same time.
He increased the amount of light.
But it seemed he did not need to...Lian passed through them at that moment.
One.
Two.
Three.
Four strikes.
Crack!
Boom!
Tak!
Boom!
Four bodies fell to the ground almost less than a second apart.
"You are really annoying sometimes, those were mine!" Kain stayed silent for a few moments.
"You’re slow."
Kain was about to answer when the three priests finally moved.
And at that exact moment, the atmosphere of the square changed.
The first priest slammed his staff onto the ground.
Thoom!
The old grooves between the stone floor of the square lit up with white light.
The second priest raised both hands, two mirror plates on the surrounding towers began to rotate.
The third priest closed his eyes and whispered a sentence in an ancient language.
Three beams rose from the towers into the sky but stopped several dozen meters above.
Then three white circles formed one after another, each one was somewhat like a sun, but more accurately, they were three cores made of extremely dense light.
Each one shone in the air like a white, shadowless plate.
[Three Shadowless Suns Array.]
At that moment, the first sun lit up, and all the shadows in the square became faint.
Lian felt that every flow of mana leaving his body left a white trail behind it.
Kain took one step to test it, even the simple movement of mana around his hand was recorded as a bright line in the air.
"Nothing can hide from the judgment of light here." The first priest said.
The second sun lit up.
Boom!
Pressure came down from above, the stone under Kain’s feet cracked and his body bent for a moment, one of his knees almost touching the ground.
"Damn it..."
One spread its legs wider, but its huge body lowered.
Even Lian felt more weight on his shoulders, not enough to stop his movement, but enough that he could not ignore it.
Then the third sun activated.
The mirror plates on several nearby buildings lit up at the same time.
The young Vorhelm gathered a small amount of ice in his hand and sent only a simple projectile toward one of the priests.
But before it could hit, light struck one of the mirrors and the path of the attack was deflected.
The ice projectile came out from another direction and hit a wall farther away.
Boom!
He moved his eyes across the mirrors, the three priests were not the main source of this power.
The city was.
These people only knew how to activate part of a structure that had been built centuries ago and use it for themselves.
This was probably some kind of defensive mechanism belonging to the city that these people knew how to activate and use.
He now understood what his instincts had been warning him about, more interestingly, the priests had directly activated it.
One of the priests reached his hand toward Lian, three beams moved from the mirrors at the same time.

chapters.title: Chapter 510: The Priests Really Thought They Could Stop Me ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: But before the attack could hit, he disappeared.
[Ashen Thunder Step.]
Boom!
Thunder ran across the stone floor, but right before the exit point, the first sun became brighter.
A white trail of Lian’s movement appeared across the square.
The priest turned his head, another beam went exactly toward the point where he planned to appear.
The young Vorhelm’s eyes narrowed slightly, at the last moment, his body turned into ash among the thunder.
He changed the exit point.
KABOOM!
The beam exploded his previous position and he appeared several meters to the side again.
Dust passed beside his face.
"Interesting." Lian looked at the place where the attack hit, this man had been able to predict his path.
Was this his own power or was it part of the array? His own guess was the second one.
"Your speed is useless against light, nothing is above the judgment of light, you infidel barbarian!" The priest said coldly.
"I said interesting, not that it was enough." The young Vorhelm disappeared and appeared in front of him a moment later.
His fist moved forward and the priest did not have enough time to fully defend himself, but before the attack landed, a white shield appeared in front of his body.
BOOOOM!
The man was pushed several meters back, but he did not fall, at the same time, to his surprise, the other two priests also slid backward.
"Oh? So that’s how it is." Lian immediately understood, it was clear from one look that his attack had affected all three of them even though he had hit only one.
The force of his attack had been divided between them, this was probably also part of the mechanism and was somewhat similar to the ability of his armor.
His eyes moved between the three of them.
"So as long as all three of you are standing, you divide the damage between yourselves."
"And what? You think you can break what our ancestors built with a few attacks? How stupid." The younger priest said angrily.
"We shall see." The young Vorhelm nodded.
The priest’s expression changed, he did not know why, but this infidel’s confidence was annoying him.
But Lian did not attack again either, his eyes moved toward the towers, the three suns, and the grooves on the ground.
He had to understand how this structure worked.
Kain was fighting two soldiers, he pushed one back with a beam of light, but the other one used the pressure of the second sun and came closer from the side.
He placed his hand on the ground, a wave of light spread out in a half-circle and pushed the attacker back.
But at that moment, a white beam came toward Kain from one of the mirrors.
He placed his own light in front of him and the two streams collided.
KRRRRRR!
He was pushed several meters back, but at least the beam was deflected.
His eyes stayed on the priest who had said the name of the tear for a moment.
"Anyway, what is the Tear of Witness?"
The man did not answer, both of his hands were still controlling part of the array.
Kain threw another light attack toward a soldier who was approaching, the attacker hit the wall.
"At least shouldn’t you tell me what entered my body? Maybe I will decide to give it back to you.
"It entered you by itself?" The priest’s expression truly changed, as if he really did not like that sentence.
"Yeah."
"It...chose you?" The man’s focus almost left the array for a moment.
"I thought you knew this part, besides, I already told you."
"Idiot... I thought you were talking nonsense, that thing should not even have awareness to be able to choose you!" The priest stared at him in disbelief and anger.
In the report that had reached them, there had been no mention that the tear itself had chosen an outsider, and all the scenarios were based on the idea that someone had forcibly absorbed the tear.
He had already heard this infidel say that the tear had chosen him, but he thought he was only talking nonsense.
"No... That is impossible."
"The Tear does not choose."
"It is an object of the Divine Of Light. It does not possess a will of its own."
"You are lying."
"You must be lying!"
The priest was in such disbelief that he even started speaking nonsense.
Lian, who was moving a few meters away from one of the towers, heard the sentence, his movement slowed for a fraction of a second.
So the Tear of Witness should not be able to choose its own host? Then what exactly had happened to Kain that day in those ruins?
"So what was it supposed to do?" Kain immediately asked as well, he was confused too.
"You swallowed it and now the light thinks you are the bearer of a covenant! It is impossible for the tear to have chosen you!" The priest shouted angrily.
"Shut up!" The elder priest shouted angrily, it was clear that those words were not supposed to become public, and after his warning, the other priest went silent.
Lian and Kain looked at each other, they had not gotten enough information and there were still many questions.
"Anyway, you have to accept that the tear chose me, I already told you, it is not my fault that your god preferred me over you useless people." Kain used the same taunt again.
"Do not speak of the Divine Of Light with that filthy mouth!" The younger priest said with fanatical anger.
In any case, the priests continued their attacks and the young Vorhelm once again focused his attention on the array, he had to shut this thing down.
[True Sequence.]
For a moment, the world in front of his eyes changed, clear mana paths appeared.

The energy did not start from the bodies of the priests, the beam entered the first priest from the first tower, went from him to the first sun, and then was transferred through one of the grooves in the square to the second tower.
From the second tower to the second priest, then to the second sun and after that to the third tower, the third priest, and finally the third sun.
It was some kind of closed circuit where the three priests were only control points, if he hit one of them with force, the other two would divide the pressure.
If he attacked the suns directly, the towers would supply their energy again.
So he did not need to destroy any of them, he only needed to break the path.
Lian held his palm toward the ground.
[Frost Dominion.]
This time, no huge wall came out of the ground, instead, a thin sheet of ice formed in front of one of the towers.
With more precise control, Lian polished its surface, making something like a mirror.
The priests did not understand his goal and seemed to be thinking about what exactly he wanted to do.
At that moment, a beam came out of the tower but instead of reaching the sun directly ...it hit the sheet of ice.
The angle changed.
The white line passed beside the first sun and hit the third sun directly.
The circuit suddenly broke!
BOOOOOOM!
All three suns shook.
The priests lost their balance for a moment.
"What did you do?!" One of them shouted angrily.
The young Vorhelm did not answer, and his eyes stayed on the sheet of ice, the goal was simple, he had changed the flow and path of those beams.
And in general, he had caused the array’s process to break down.
In any case, the sheet of ice began to melt, the light was too powerful.
But there was no need to worry, so what if one was destroyed once? He could simply make another one.
A second sheet formed and then he made a third one.
This time the priests understood, one of them raised his hand and a white beam went toward the ice sheets.
Lian changed their positions, two beams collided in the air and the array shook again, but it still had not broken.

Kain looked at one of the towers at the same moment, the tower that he himself had activated earlier with his light, it was not clear what he was thinking about, but it seemed an idea had come to his mind.
"Lian."
"What?"
"This thing recognizes my light, right?"
"Try it." Lian looked at Kain for a moment and then understood.
Without asking anything else, Kain raised both hands toward the tower and golden-white light came out of his palms.
"Don’t!" The priest shouted.
It was too late.
Kain’s light hit the mirror plate, but unlike the other attacks, the mirror did not push it back, it absorbed it and all the lines on the tower became golden for a moment.
The priest who was controlling that tower suddenly opened his eyes.
His mana connection was cut off and suddenly the first sun shook.
This was the chance.
[Ashen Thunder Step.]
Boom!
Lian disappeared.

The priests tried to identify his movement like before and with the help of the array, but one of the towers was no longer under the priest’s control and the result was simple, the array had become weaker.
They could no longer predict Lian’s movement using this skill.
The white trail became incomplete for a moment and Lian’s body turned into ash during the movement, then a moment later he appeared in front of the first priest.
The man only had enough time to raise his staff.
"Have a good sleep." The young Vorhelm placed his palm on the man’s chest.
Boom!

chapters.title: Chapter 511: Another Region Is Here ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: The air was forced out of the priest’s lungs, his body was dragged several meters across the ground and his eyes rolled back.
The power of the attack was enough to knock him unconscious.
At the same time as he lost consciousness, the first sun completely turned off.
The pressure in the square suddenly decreased.
The second and third priests tried to keep the array active at the same time, but the three-part structure now had only two points, and that was enough to make everything fall apart.
Mana flow returned through one of the paths.
Crack!
One of the mirror plates cracked, the second sun shook, then the third, and finally ...both of them exploded.
BOOOOOOM!
A wave of mana covered the entire square and the soldiers of Region Three were pushed backward.
"Move." Lian looked at his friend and said, Kain did not ask any questions and both of them went directly toward the shrine.
One also moved behind them.
The forces of Region Three were still large in number, but breaking the array had caused their formation to become disorganized for a few moments.
"Stop them!" A commander shouted from far away.
Ten soldiers took positions in the main street, Kain gathered light between his hands.
Lian moved forward.
This time, he had no intention of stopping.
The first spear came toward him but he easily grabbed the body of the weapon and pulled, causing its owner to move forward together with the spear.
He gave him a short punch to the chest and boom!
The man’s body hit the two soldiers behind him.
Kain passed through the opening that had been created and two walls of light formed on both sides of him, arrows made of light hit them.
The path opened.
One entered the line from behind with its huge body.
The soldiers standing in front of the creature either moved aside...or were pushed aside.
But Region Three was not completely backing down.
Those three priests were not the only priests present, other priests had gathered near the main stairs of the shrine.
Some of them were not even looking at Lian and Kain and seemed to be doing something else, whatever it was, it was important enough for them to completely ignore all the chaos that was happening.
This caught Lian’s attention and he looked more carefully to understand what they were doing, and that look was enough.
"They are trying to open the shrine’s door."
"Right in the middle of all this fighting? How can they focus on opening that door in all this chaos?"
"It’s simple, whatever is inside is more important to them than us."
That itself was important information.
When they got close to the upper part of the city, the real structure of the gate became clear to them.
What had looked like only one huge white door from far away actually had two layers.
The first layer had twelve large mirror sections around the entrance, each one connected to one of the city’s towers, although not through cables or physical wires as it would logically have to be.
Instead, they were connected by paths of light that moved from one building to another.
The World Memory panel recovered new information after matching it with the map.
[Seal of Twelve Reflections.]
There were twelve huge grooves around the gate.
Eleven of them were already lit, and the twelfth one lit up at the exact moment one of the priests adjusted the last metal frame on the distant tower.
Kaaang!
The entire gate shook, the outer section slowly moved back into the mountain wall, first a few meters and then even farther, white light came out from the gap behind it.
"So this is what they were working on." Kain stopped for a moment.
Lian nodded, this was what the natives had been trying to buy time for all this time and with one look, he understood why they still needed at least three more days.
They had managed to completely open the first gate, but behind the first gate, there was another door.
It was completely smooth and completely white, without a handle and without any gap, and a large symbol was carved into its center.
It was an eye and below it was a drop, as if a tear had fallen from the eye.
The priests of Region Three gave short cries of joy when they saw the first layer opening.
But no one moved forward, because the main part was still closed.
Lian moved his eyes toward the priests who were preparing in front of the second seal.
They had several large tools with Light Crystals and mirror plates, they were clearly trying to replace something...something they did not have.
He thought for a moment, his eyes moved toward Kain, and then everything slowly started to make sense in his mind, like a puzzle whose pieces had finally been put together.
Nine months ago, two natives from Region Three had gone to those ruins to retrieve the Tear of Divine Of Light, the same ruins that Kain had entered by chance.
That tear was a key, a key that could activate this city and all of its mechanisms.
The natives of Region Three needed it to awaken this city and open the sanctuary, but Kain had accidentally obtained that tear.
The natives of Region Three had probably been searching for the tear during this time, but they had not been able to find it, and for some reason, they could not delay opening the sanctuary.
So they had decided to find another way to open the sanctuary, a way that was probably harder, more expensive and more dangerous, with a very low chance of success.
Even so, they had no other choice, there was something inside that sanctuary that they had to obtain, and it seemed they were in a hurry to get it.
And that itself raised some questions, what was inside that sanctuary? And why was Region Three so desperate to obtain it?
"Continue the preparations! There isn’t much time left until the Shadowless Hour!" one of the priests said.
Lian heard this sentence, so his previous guess had been correct, there was a specific time for opening the sanctuary, the Shadowless Hour.
They had probably found a way to open the sanctuary, or at least trick its mechanism for a while.
But the main key was standing only a few dozen meters away from them right now.
And wasn’t this very good for them? If Kain was the key, they could enter the sanctuary without any problems.
Lian wanted to move toward the seal when...BOOOOOM!
A huge explosion came from the western part of the city, and everyone stopped for a moment.
One of the temporary guard towers of Region Three broke in half, and pieces of wood and stone fell down.
Kain quickly turned around, and the young Vorhelm also looked in that direction, it seemed that some other people had also become involved in this matter.
People were coming out from the western street, and surprisingly, they were humans too!

But they were not Earth humans, their equipment did not look like anything from Earth, and their auras were extremely strange, they were different from both the Earth humans and the natives of Region Three.
Their armor was also different from Region Three, it was darker, with parts that were blue and gray.
The symbol on their flag also looked nothing like the sun symbol of Region Three.
"Region Six?!" one of the commanders of Region Three said, and his face changed when he saw them.
"What? Another Region? Damn it!" Kain turned his head toward Lian.

chapters.title: Chapter 512: The Shrine Of Light I ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian also only stared for a few seconds, the newcomers did not pay the slightest attention to the two of them and surprisingly attacked the forces of Region Three directly.
Spears.
Dark arrows.
Heavy attacks from behind the lines.
One of the priests of Region Three blocked the attack with a Light Shield.
"Disable the towers! No artifact inside the sanctuary can fall into the hands of Region Three!" the commander of Region Six shouted loudly.
His soldiers split into several groups, some went directly toward Region Three, while others moved toward the mirror towers.
The rest went toward the people who were trying to open the sanctuary door.
"You bastards from Region Six, what the hell are you doing here?! Get lost!"
"Do you think we will let you Light Dogs obtain that weapon of your false god and use it to suppress us?!"
"Whether you like it or not, we will obtain the weapon!"
"We will see about that! soldiers of darkness, slaughter all of them!"
While the two sides were fighting, the two outsiders in the middle were completely forgotten.
"I thought they all hated us." Kain even forgot about the fight for a moment.
Lian looked at the two groups of natives who were now killing each other in the middle of a holy city.
"Apparently, they also found time to hate each other, but this is great." He also had not expected there to be conflicts between the natives of this world.
He had expected that after everything that had happened to them, at least all of them would be united.
But what they were seeing was completely opposite to what he expected.
"For us?"
The young Vorhelm moved his eyes toward the sanctuary gate, half of the Region Three forces had been forced to return.
The priests had also spread out to protect the towers.
The direct path to the only remaining door was almost empty.
"Yeah."
"Let’s go." Kain understood.
The two of them ran, One was also behind them, neither of the two Regions was paying full attention to them for now.
Region Three was trapped in the sudden attack, and Region Six was more focused on destroying the towers.
"This chance won’t happen again."
Kain nodded.
They reached the only remaining door, and as soon as Kain was only a few meters away, the eye and tear symbol lit up.
"Did it react to me? Or did I imagine it?" He stopped.
"Get closer." Lian, who had already understood what was happening, said to him calmly.
Kain placed his palm on the center of the seal, light entered the white surface from his body, and the entire gate shook for a moment.
Then twelve lines came out from the center.
Each one moved toward one of the points around the gate, but only nine paths were completed, three lines were cut off in the middle.
[Mechanism activated.]
[Child of Light identified.]
[Structural error.]
[3 Reflection Paths are disconnected.]
[Entry Ritual cannot be completed.]
Kain looked at the notification for a few seconds and then looked at Lian.
"Looks like there is a problem."
Lian narrowed his eyes.
[True Sequence.]
The mana paths appeared in front of him, Kain’s light was entering the seal perfectly, the problem was not him.
In three parts of the structure, the inner reflection plates were broken, one on the left side of the entrance, one dozens of meters higher, and the third one behind a section of a collapsed pillar.
"The key is fine, but the lock is broken." He then said calmly.
"Of course, how did I think things would finally go easily?" Kain let out a short sigh.
The young Vorhelm raised his hand.
[Frost Dominion.]
An ice plate formed in the air, but this time its purpose was not defense.
He made it thinner, smooth and clear, and then controlled its surface so precisely that it became almost like a mirror.
He placed the ice mirror at the exact angle between the two sections.
"Now."
Kain summoned his light without asking any questions, the beam hit the surface of the ice, changed direction, and entered the next part of the path.
Click!
The first node lit up.
[Path 10/12 recovered.]
"Oh? It worked haha." Kain said with excitement without taking his hand away from the seal.
"I saw it." As he expected, he really was a genius.
But unfortunately, the natives of Region Three finally noticed.
"They are opening the seal!" one of the distant priests shouted.
Several soldiers changed their path and moved toward them, they could not allow the outsiders to open the sanctuary.
One stepped forward.
Lian sent only one command through the link, no one gets close.
"Although I guess One won’t be enough." After thinking for a moment, he decided to summon his second Special Colony Member for the first time.
[Name: Two]
[Special Colony Member]
[Status: Summoning]
One stood in front of the stairs, his body covering the entire width of the main section.
But before the soldiers had a chance to confront him, thousands of particles of light suddenly appeared from nowhere.
The particles of light gathered in the air and were quickly pulled toward one point, until something huge started to take shape inside the intense light.
A few seconds later, a monster appeared that could cause fear even among terrifying creatures.
A giant wolf.
It was more than fifteen meters tall, and its huge body almost filled the entire street.
Its thick black fur moved slowly in the wind, and every movement of its body created a heavy sound.
But what was more frightening than the size of its body was its head.
Eight closed eyes were placed across its face.
None of the eyes were open, but even so, the presence of those eight closed eyes made the soldiers feel as if something was looking directly into the deepest part of their bodies.
Its claws were as large as a human body, and its teeth were so huge that each one was enough to easily crush a human’s bones.
Heavy pressure spread from its body.
Even without moving, small cracks appeared in the ground under its feet, and at the exact moment it completely appeared...
"Grrrrrrrrr!"
The terrifying roar of the wolf spread across the entire city.
The sound was so loud that the windows of the nearby buildings shook, and several soldiers lost their balance.
"By the Divine Of Light... what the hell is this...?"
"A Dev—A Devil!"
"This is a True Devil!!"
The soldiers of Region Three fell to the ground in fear and stepped back one after another.
None of them dared to get close to the creature.
Two stared at them with his huge mouth and teeth that were large enough to crush a building.
He did nothing for a few seconds, then turned his head.
His eight closed eyes turned toward Lian, and unlike a moment ago, the giant wolf became completely calm and even showed a respectful attitude.
"I don’t want anyone to get in the way."
His master only said that, and the wolf immediately lowered his head, then took a step forward and placed his huge body directly in the soldiers’ path.
No one could pass through anymore.
The presence of Two alone was enough to make the soldiers of Region Three not even dare to come closer.
One let out a short growl after seeing this scene, the sound was almost like a complaint...as if he was even a little jealous

chapters.title: Chapter 513: The Shrine Of Light II ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: "Lian..." Kain also did not have a better reaction.
"Hmm?"
"You could summon something like this too?"
"Yeah."
"Then damn it, why did you hide something this cool until now?!"
He looked at the giant wolf in disbelief.
"How do you even have something like this?!"
"This is cooler than anything I’ve ever seen!"
"How?!"
"Just how did you manage to get such a skill?!"
"I want one too!"
"We have more important things to do for now." Lian only looked at him and turned his attention back to the door.
Kain stared at him for a few moments and then looked at the wolf again.
"At least tell me what you named him?"
He thought for a few moments.
"Or let me guess."
"God of all wolves?"
"God of Destruction in the Mortal World?"
"Or even better!"
"Doomsday Wolf?"
He suddenly opened his eyes wider.
"Or wait... Fenrir!"
"It has to be one of these, right?" He asked his best friend excitedly.
"Um...none of them?" the young Vorhelm simply said, feeling that all those names were far too complicated.
Kain stayed completely silent for a few seconds and then slowly looked at the giant wolf, and then looked back at Lian.
"...Please don’t tell me you named him Two."
Lian stayed silent, he gave no answer, but that silence was enough to be taken as a response.
Kain’s face slowly became empty.
"My God..."
He looked at the giant wolf again, then looked at the sky with an expression as if all hope in his life had disappeared.
"Why do you give such a cool skill to people who don’t deserve it?" He could barely stop himself from crying.
Lian completely ignored him and looked at the second section, it was much higher.
He created an ice platform under his feet and then activated [Ashen Thunder Step].
Boom!
His body shot upward with a line of lightning, but at that exact moment, an attack beam came toward him from one of the priests of Region Three.
In the middle of his movement, his body turned into ash and the beam passed through him.
He appeared again several meters away, on a second ice platform, and then created the next ice mirror while pointing toward Kain at the same time.
The beam of light hit the second plate and the ice immediately started to turn into steam.
"Come on...
The path was completed.
Click!
[Path 11/12 recovered.]
Kain was still holding his hand against the seal below, because of the presence of Two and One, who were taking all the priests’ attacks, he did not need to worry.
The more he saw how useful the two tamed monsters were, the more jealous he became.
Lian went to the last one, the third path was behind a collapsed pillar, but unfortunately, a large part of the structure was covered, which could cause trouble.
He looked from above and used True Sequence to find out where he needed to place the mirror, and he understood that the mirror had to be placed almost behind the pillar.
But there was not enough space, he had to move part of the pillar.
Lian came down, his palm touched the stone.
Krrrrrrck!
A crack spread across the pillar, but he did not break it, he only pushed the broken section a few centimeters.
Finally, enough space was created, and the third ice plate took shape, at the same moment the light reached it and the surface of the ice started melting quickly.
"You filthy outsiders! That sanctuary does not belong to you! Stop right now!" a priest shouted from a distance after seeing the final path.
"Looks like the sanctuary doesn’t agree with you." Kain said sarcastically.
Finally, the beam broke and moved across the ice plate, reaching the last node.
Kaaaaang!
[Path 12/12 completed.]
The entire gate lit up.
The eye and tear symbol on the final door began to shine, then the symbol carved into the gate moved aside like a huge eyelid.
The drop below it turned golden, and Kain’s light passed through all the grooves of the gate for a moment.
[Child of Light identified.]
[The Sanctuary of Light is opening.]
The gate opened from the middle, but not completely, only enough for two people to enter.
White light poured out from inside, so pure that the details of the inside could not be seen for a few moments.
Lian gave a command to One and Two through the link, and then both of their bodies turned into particles of light.
[One and Two have returned to the Colony House.]
Kain entered, and he moved right behind him.
One of the priests of Region Three managed to get through the forces of Region Six.
When he saw Lian passing through, he ran at full speed.
"Wait!"
The young Vorhelm looked behind him.
The priest was only a few meters away, and he reached his hand toward the opening.
But as soon as he entered...BOOOOM!
The gate closed.
The priest arrived just one moment too late, and both of his palms hit the white surface.
"Open!"
But nothing happened, no matter what he did, no matter how hard he tried, the sanctuary door was completely closed.
Behind him, the forces of Region Three and Region Six were still fighting, but none of them could enter.
On the other side of the gate, a notification slowly appeared in front of Lian.
[Entry recorded.]
[Internal Ritual started.]
[External access blocked until the end of the ritual.]
"Luckily, I think we really are alone now, we don’t need to worry anymore." Kain let out a heavy breath.
Then the first line of light on the floor lit up.
Click.
Then the second one, and it did not take long before ten lines, one hundred lines, and thousands of thin grooves on the floor, walls, and ceiling lit up one after another.
The space that had been almost completely dark until a few seconds ago slowly became visible.
Kain raised his head and became completely still, Lian also said nothing for a few seconds.
Because contrary to what they expected, there was not a hall behind the gate, but a huge abyss stood in front of them, its end disappearing into darkness.
White bridges crossed the empty space at different heights.
Some were straight, some formed circles, and some reached buildings that had been built inside the walls of the abyss.
Thousands of statues stood on circular terraces around the space.
Humans.
Priests.
Pilgrims.
All of them were kneeling, and all of them were looking toward the center.
Kain took a few steps forward, then he saw something that made everything around him seem unimportant.
In the center of the abyss floated a sphere, a huge white sphere that was perhaps several hundred meters in diameter.
Twelve giant metal and mirror rings surrounded it and held it in the center of the space.
The surface of the sphere was not still, it moved like some kind of living material, slow waves of light moved across it, but among all that white, black lines could be seen.
Thin cracks, and every few seconds, extremely strong light came out from one of them.
Thum.
The huge space shook with every pulse of the sphere.
Kain could not even make a joke immediately, he was truly shocked.
"This...what is this?" His voice was quieter than usual.
Something inside Lian’s storage space started to shake, it was the Celestial Book of Treasures, but it was not a calm shake, it was almost shaking wildly.
He took it out and the book opened by itself, the entire page suddenly turned golden.
[Treasure Source is in front of you.]
[Evaluation started.]
[Evaluation failed.]
[The structure is beyond the current evaluation range.]
He slowly raised his eyes from the page and looked at the huge white sphere, the twelve rings, and the black lines that passed through the light.
And then he thought about the entire city that was buried outside under the unknown black substance.
About all those pilgrims who had been frozen in time and turned into statues...statues with black spots.
Or even the Hollow Pilgrims.
Something that had once destroyed the Silent Light City may have never left this place...maybe all this time...it had remained lit right in front of them.
Maybe the reason for this city’s death...was right in front of them...

chapters.title: Chapter 514: The Shrine Of Light III
paragraphs: Kain continued staring at the huge white sphere for several seconds.
Each pulse created a very weak wave through the space of the sanctuary, and the twelve huge metal rings floating around it slowly moved in the darkness at a fixed distance.
The black lines on the surface of the sphere stretched for a moment with every pulse and then returned to their previous positions; almost like veins moving under the skin of a living creature.
The Celestial Book of Treasure was still open in Lian’s hand.
[Treasure Source is in front of you.]
[Evaluation failed.]
[The structure is beyond the current evaluation range.]
He looked at the sphere again, at least now he knew that the treasure was exactly in front of them.
And if he had to guess, he had no doubt that this was what Region Three had been trying to obtain.
But one question still remained? What exactly was this thing?
He and Kain looked at each other, and both of them made an unspoken agreement through their eyes before stepping forward.
The white bridge under their feet continued toward one of the circular terraces around the abyss.
The farther they went, the more the real size of the sanctuary revealed itself.
What had looked like several bridges and scattered platforms from the entrance was actually a multi-layered structure, with many parts built inside the huge walls of the abyss.
Thousands of kneeling statues stood on different terraces, and all their heads were turned toward the white sphere.
"Are these the same pilgrims?" Kain slowed down as he passed one of the statues, the statues looked exactly like the frozen pilgrims they had seen a few hours ago.
The young Vorhelm looked at the stone robe of the statue, it seemed that these were also like the dried pilgrims outside.
"Yeah, they were humans once too."
They reached a circular platform, part of the wall behind it was still almost intact.
There were very old drawings on the stone, an eye with a drop under it, and in the center of a circle surrounded by twelve rings.
Lian opened the Celestial Book of Treasure again, the inner map of the sanctuary appeared on the page, and the World Memory immediately placed new information on the same map.
[Historical structure identified.]
[Hall of Witness.]
[Recovered information: Incomplete.]
Several more lines slowly appeared on the page.
[Central Artifact Name: Sphere of Witness.]
[Owner: Divine Of Light.]
"So this thing belongs to Divine Of Light himself?" Kain stayed completely silent for a moment and then asked very quietly.
Lian read the line again.
"Apparently.
The thing floating several hundred meters in front of them had once directly belonged to one of the Seven Divines.
Not an artifact made by his followers, not something that was later created in his name, but something that belonged to him directly, this was an artifact that belonged to a godlike being.
Now it was even more clear why Region Three wanted to take it back so badly, but unfortunately for them, they had bad luck.
Kain’s eyes unconsciously moved back toward the sphere.
A different expression appeared on his face; a mix of amazement, obvious greed, and a small amount of caution, which was relatively rare for him.
"I want to touch it." It was as if something inside him was pulling him toward the sphere.
Some of the writings were still there, but most of the lines had been worn away or broken, luckily, some of them could still be read.
[Light does not forget what it has seen.]
[Light is the only witness.]
"First the Tear of Witness and now the Sphere of Witness, what exactly does this witness refer to?" Kain asked with some curiosity.
He had some guesses and felt that it might be referring to Divine Of Light, but why would that godlike being be called a witness?
What exactly did witness mean?
"Witness should refer to Divine Of Light." Lian answered after thinking for a moment, their guesses were the same.
"But why? Why would a godlike being be called a witness? Is it some kind of title? But it doesn’t make sense..."

The young Vorhelm did not answer him immediately, and his own mind also became a little occupied with this matter, he looked again at the sentences [Light does not forget what it has seen] and [Light is the witness].
Could this mean that Light was a witness to everything? That Divine Of Light considered himself the witness of everything?

It was not wrong either, they said Light was one of the first elements to form during creation, something that gave meaning to life, and it could even be possible that it witnessed the creation itself.
Maybe that was exactly what it referred to.
Witness was another title for Divine Of Light, Divine Of Light was the witness of everything.
"For now, we have more important things to deal with, like that sphere." In any case, he did not answer, and instead of answering, he activated True Sequence.
Whatever that sphere was, it was clearly usable like a treasure, so they were not going to leave it behind.
But there was one problem, the black lines on it had a very noticeable similarity to the black spots on the dried pilgrims outside and the same black liquid that had trapped the ships.
Something about the black lines on the sphere had been bothering him from the very beginning, if they were only normal corruption, there should not have been such an organized flow between them.
The world in front of his eyes changed.
Energy paths appeared across the surface of the sphere.
The white light inside the sphere formed a huge and organized network; flows came out from the center, entered the twelve rings, and then returned to the core.
But the darkness had entered it, the black lines moved between the paths of light, and some of them even had their own secondary structure, including flow, density, and transfer.
It was almost like the energy transfer network of a living creature.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, and at that exact moment, something inside his body reacted.
It was a very instinctive feeling, and it was also the first time he had ever felt such a strange feeling, he did not even know what this feeling was.
But it was strangely similar to wanting...as if his body wanted those black veins...?
As if a structure inside his body had suddenly understood that there was something in front of it that it had been made for.
"Did something happen?" Kain noticed the change in his expression.
Lian was still looking at the sphere.

"Those black things, they’re strange, they’re like an energy transfer network. Whatever their source was, they were once part of a living creature, and if I had to make my own guess, they probably belonged to the monster that destroyed this city."
Kain’s eyes moved back to the black lines moving across the sphere, but the shock in his eyes was completely clear.
"How strong would a monster have to be to keep something that belonged to a Divine corrupted even after all these years?"
Lian did not answer, because he had the same question, and before they could investigate more...Thum!
The twelve rings around the sphere shook at the same time.
Kain immediately prepared his Light, and the young Vorhelm also took one step forward and raised his guard.

But surprisingly, no attack happened, instead, the first ring slowly turned, then the second, the third, and in less than a few seconds, all twelve rings started moving around the sphere at different speeds.
The white lines on the bridges and terraces lit up again.
[Internal Ritual activated.]
[Ritual of Witness.]
[First Stage: Witness Identification.]
Kain had not even said anything when a very thin beam separated from the sphere.
The light went directly into his chest, he did not even have time to defend himself, his body became slightly stiff but there was no pain.
The light passed through his clothes for several seconds, and something inside his body responded.
All twelve rings suddenly turned golden.
[Trace of the Tear of Witness identified.]
[Child of Light identified.]
The next notification immediately appeared.
[The Sphere of Witness structure is damaged.]
[External corruption detected in the main structure.]
[The ritual cannot continue without separation.]
At that exact moment, the twelve rings became even brighter, but nothing happened, as if they had become stuck at one stage and could not move forward.
It was clear with just one look, as long as those black veins remained on the Sphere of Witness, whatever this Ritual of Witness was, it was not going to be completed.
"I guess without separating those black veins, we are not going to obtain this sphere." Kain had also noticed this.

sentences.text: Kain continued staring at the huge white sphere for several seconds.
Each pulse created a very weak wave through the space of the sanctuary, and the twelve huge metal rings floating around it slowly moved in the darkness at a fixed distance.
The black lines on the surface of the sphere stretched for a moment with every pulse and then returned to their previous positions; almost like veins moving under the skin of a living creature.
The Celestial Book of Treasure was still open in Lian’s hand.
[Treasure Source is in front of you.]
[Evaluation failed.]
[The structure is beyond the current evaluation range.]
He looked at the sphere again, at least now he knew that the treasure was exactly in front of them.
And if he had to guess, he had no doubt that this was what Region Three had been trying to obtain.
But one question still remained?
What exactly was this thing?
He and Kain looked at each other, and both of them made an unspoken agreement through their eyes before stepping forward.
The white bridge under their feet continued toward one of the circular terraces around the abyss.
The farther they went, the more the real size of the sanctuary revealed itself.
What had looked like several bridges and scattered platforms from the entrance was actually a multi-layered structure, with many parts built inside the huge walls of the abyss.
Thousands of kneeling statues stood on different terraces, and all their heads were turned toward the white sphere.

The young Vorhelm looked at the stone robe of the statue, it seemed that these were also like the dried pilgrims outside.
"Yeah, they were humans once too."
They reached a circular platform, part of the wall behind it was still almost intact.
There were very old drawings on the stone, an eye with a drop under it, and in the center of a circle surrounded by twelve rings.
Lian opened the Celestial Book of Treasure again, the inner map of the sanctuary appeared on the page, and the World Memory immediately placed new information on the same map.
[Historical structure identified.]
[Hall of Witness.]
[Recovered information: Incomplete.]
Several more lines slowly appeared on the page.
[Central Artifact Name: Sphere of Witness.]
[Owner: Divine Of Light.]

"Apparently.

Not an artifact made by his followers, not something that was later created in his name, but something that belonged to him directly, this was an artifact that belonged to a godlike being.
