The lightning went directly inside the reservoir, the creature tried to eat it with corrupted light like before, the same light that was formed from the combination of Eclipse and pure light.
The same power that had managed to disable this move before.
But the young Vorhelm cut the flow before the skill collapsed, and a huge and destructive ice claw formed on his hand, and he slammed it into the fifth reservoir with all his strength.
BOOOM!
The force was enough to crack the reservoir, and Kain also sent the final attack from a distance like before.
[Dawn Spear.]
TAK!
The fifth reservoir broke as well ...and at the same time, Lian and Kain both retreated.
"Damn ...you did great!
You’re really a monster yourself." Kain laughed loudly and still could not believe that they had managed to go this far against such a monster.
His greatest achievement had always been defeating a Level 20 Fallen, and even that had been done with traps and a lot of planning.
But now?
With the help of his best friend, he was slaughtering a Level 50 Fallen!
"Your work isn’t bad either, you’re more skilled at teamwork than you think." Lian said calmly.
"You know, Lian, I think we make a great team, no joke, this has been the best battle of my life so far."
"We haven’t even won yet." the young Vorhelm laughed.
"Yeah, but I’m sure we’ll win, just look, the monster is almost dead."

The Child Of Light was right, only one reservoir remained, of course, destroying the reservoirs did not mean the complete death of the monster, but it would definitely disable its self-healing mechanism completely, and then they could finish it off.
With the help of True Sequence, Lian looked at the last one, the sixth reservoir was larger than the others.

The Leviathan had also realized how bad its situation was, it had lost a large part of its recovery power, and to protect the only remaining reservoir, all the corrupted light in its body moved toward the front part of its chest.
The black plates on that area became thicker, and at least three defensive layers were created there.
"I think it knows that this is its last one too." Kain looked at it from a distance of one hundred meters.
"Yeah."
"Please tell me you have a plan for this too?"
"Do you doubt me?
I always have a plan." Lian smiled and sent a direct order to his second Colony member.
Two raised its head, its eight red eyes were still under the effect of Blood Hunt Moon.
The Leviathan opened its mouth, corrupted light was gathering, and it looked like it was preparing to launch a large attack.
And the eight-eyed wolf moved forward as well.
[Reversed Maw.]
The space in front of its mouth twisted, and when the flood of corrupted light was released, part of the attack entered the reversed space directly.
The wolf lowered its body, and its bones made sounds from the damage.
The power of the light beam was too great, and part of the beam passed to the side and landed on the wolf’s shoulder, causing its skin and bone armor to burn completely.
Two roared in pain.
But the main path of the attack was redirected, and the result was a successful defense.
"Thanks, Wolf Of Doomsday, you did great." Kain moved.
[Dawn Chains.] wrapped around the Leviathan’s neck.
[Inverted Day.]
The light around Two changed, and the white light of Blighted Radiance became darker for a moment, the black parts inside it changed direction.
The power of the attack decreased.
Lian moved, now it was his turn ...but the Leviathan was waiting for him too.
All twelve eyes turned toward him at the same time, and the beams came from twelve angles.
Feeling the attack, he immediately activated [Ashen Thunder Step].
He passed two beams, and the third blocked his exit point, then his body turned into ash and the fourth followed the path of the ash.
Feeling that he could not save himself from these beams just by running away, he directly counterattacked.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
The shockwave redirected three beams, but unfortunately, he was not completely lucky, and the fourth hit the armor’s shoulder.
TAK!
The plate of the World-Devourer Bastion turned black, and the line underneath it went out.
[World-Devourer Bastion Integrity has decreased.]
[Structural Memory activated.]
The metal began to repair itself, but the corrupted light was still on it and the repair was eaten away again, the Leviathan’s special ability could even disable the armor’s recovery structure.
Lian immediately locked World-Bearing Frame onto that area, and the internal paths of the armor separated from the infected shoulder.
The corruption did not spread, this was the first time that instead of enduring an attack, he had been forced to use the armor to isolate the damage.
The Leviathan sensed this, and white-black strands came out from its armor.
But these were no longer beams ...they were more like living whips, and dozens of them danced in the sky like lightning.

chapters.title: Chapter 522: Leviathan Of Eclipse VI
paragraphs: All of those whips were aimed at Lian, as if the monster saw only him as a threat in this battle and saw everyone else as ants it could crush.
One of the strands wrapped around his armor.
But no, it seemed the target of those whip-like strands was not his life, it seemed that it wanted to get what was inside him.
Lian immediately frowned, he felt that thing moving directly toward his core, as if his core was its target.
He had already guessed that the monster wanted to obtain all the energy that belonged to the Demon Of Eclipse.
And now the Leviathan was doing exactly that.
But at that moment, something else happened, the connection was two-sided, through those strands, the monster had been able to find his core.
But Lian could also sense the path of all the strands, all the essence of the Leviathan’s body was gathered around the final reservoir at the center of the network.
He no longer needed to search for it, the source of these strands that the monster had connected to him was the monster’s own core, and the final reservoir was located exactly there.
"You made a mistake." A very small smile appeared on his face.
"Are you okay??" Kain shouted from a distance.
"Now I don’t need to search for it anymore." Lian fixed his eyes exactly on a specific part of the creature’s chest.
He did not pull the strands or try to separate them from himself, instead, he allowed them to pull him closer for a moment.
The monster tried to pull him toward itself with the strands, exactly like a chain.
The Leviathan expected resistance, but when there was none, Lian was pulled toward the creature’s chest like a bullet.
At the last moment, he activated [Ashen Thunder Step].
His angle changed and he passed beside one of the strands and landed on the outer layer of the monster’s chest.
[Mountain Anchor]
And he locked himself in the exact place where he was standing, the Leviathan moved its body and tried to throw the human away like an annoying insect.
But the young Vorhelm did not move and pointed toward his best friend, and that single gesture was enough for Kain to understand that it was time.
[Sun Mark]
The golden mark landed on the same spot and the light above the city gathered.
[Noonday Judgment]
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The first pillar of light fell onto the Leviathan’s body and as a result, the outer layer cracked, but unfortunately, the second defensive layer remained intact.
The monster knew what these humans were trying to do and had already prepared the strongest defenses possible for that spot.
"Heh heh, you thought you were the only one who could do cool things?" Kain said mockingly, and at the same time a sphere came out from inside his chest.
The sphere of Witness.
The thing started spinning around him and all of Kain’s stats began to increase.
[All of your stats have increased by ten percent.]
[All of your stats have increased by thirty percent.]
[All of your stats have increased by fifty percent.]
[All of your stats have increased by seventy percent.]
[Warning! This is the maximum amount of power your body can handle from the Blessing of Light.]
"This is enough." He smiled, this was one of the abilities of the sphere of Witness, the Blessing of Light.
Now it was time to see how much stronger his skills would become with such a large increase in his stats.
[Light Echo.]
A compressed light was shot toward the target, but a moment later, the same attack was repeated from the same point and hit the target twice from two directions one after another.
The first one was not enough, but the second one...BOOOOOOOM!
The second layer broke and the third layer was revealed.
The Leviathan raised one of its limbs with all its strength.
Kain was behind Lian, and if he moved away, the attack would hit him directly.
And naturally, the young Vorhelm did not dodge, besides his friend getting hurt, all their effort to reach the final reservoir could be wasted.
[Mountain Anchor]
[World-Bearing Frame]
[Molten Bastion Body]
His entire defensive structure locked into place and the monster’s limb came down.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sound silenced everything for a moment.
The stairs and street under Lian sank, the armor on his chest cracked, and all of his internal organs made sounds as they were torn.
The taste of blood filled his mouth.
His ribs resisted under the Molten Bastion Body, but the pressure was so strong that a sharp pain moved up from his side.
If this attack had hit him without armor, probably none of his bones would have remained intact.
But now, between the Leviathan and Kain, there was armor made from the body of a giant that had been created to endure weights far greater than this.
He did not move back.
[Giant’s Momentum.]
It was time to finish it.
Then he immediately sent an order through the connection to his present Colony Member.
Two released his final strength.
[Pathless World — Second Activation.]
His body almost immediately trembled, this time the ability would only last for a few seconds, but those few seconds were enough.
The Leviathan sensed Lian’s direction incorrectly and the eight-eyed wolf jumped toward the monster from the other side.
[Bone Mountain.]
Huge bones wrapped around one of its limbs.
[Bodiless Pack.]
Shadows poured onto the creature’s neck.
[Skyless Howl.]
The twelve eyes were disrupted again for a moment.
Two was using almost everything he had, and this was completely draining his strength, and he also had to use all of his power to make sure his attacks could work against a Level 50 target.
Lian had to do the same.
[Skill Overdrive]
[Skill power increased for 10 seconds.]
[Ashen Thunder Step]
[Giant’s Stored Momentum]
He also used the maximum of his speed and raw power, and his armored body passed through the opening like a projectile.
The third defensive layer that the monster had created for the reservoir was in front of him.
He raised his palm and used Eclipse energy.
[Eclipse Energy Storage: 68%.]
This was the highest amount of Eclipse energy he had ever used at once, and black lines covered his entire palm.
[Suppressing Palm]
Then a dense palm phantom formed and struck the third layer with all of his raw strength and Eclipse energy.
TUM!
The outside sound was small, but it caused enough damage for the Eclipse energy to enter the target.

And the structure of the defensive layer began to weaken from the inside, and at the same time Giant’s Momentum arrived behind it, and to make sure that the third layer would really break, a huge ice claw formed in his hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Feeling that it was still not enough, thunder surrounded his fist.
[Thunder Calamity]
This was not just an ordinary attack, he had put all of his raw strength together with his offensive skills into this strike.
And finally, he struck!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A huge pressure formed and shook the entire battlefield, like a huge storm wind that could tear buildings from the ground.
The entire front part of the Leviathan’s chest exploded, and the sixth reservoir broke immediately.
White-black light covered the monster’s entire body for a moment and then...went out.
All of the monster’s reservoirs that formed its main self-healing and recovery mechanism had been destroyed.
And because the self-healing mechanism no longer existed, because of Lian’s destructive punch, all the plates on the monster’s body that acted like natural armor began to fall.
One after another, and beneath them, the monster’s real body was revealed.
Gray and wounded skin, an ancient sea monster that had been buried under corrupted light for years.
But it was still alive.
The Leviathan released one last roar, a more painful and wild sound, it had realized that it was losing.
It pulled its entire body toward the city and no longer cared about protecting itself, it wanted to tear these humans apart no matter what.
Kain was breathing heavily, the sphere of Witness was still beside his shoulder and thanks to this sphere, he was still standing.
"Please don’t tell me it’s still not over."
"Unfortunately, it isn’t over." Lian wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth with the back of his hand

chapters.title: Chapter 523: Leviathan Of Eclipse ( Final )
paragraphs: "I really hate that answer." The Child Of Light moved his head back, he wanted to cry, no matter how much he loved fighting, all of his muscles were screaming in pain.
In the end, he was still a human and he had limits.
"But I have good news, now we can kill it." The young Vorhelm said calmly, as if he were announcing something normal.
Kain let out a breath and then smiled.
"Well, that’s at least better than nothing."
The Leviathan moved forward.
But at that moment, the eight-eyed wolf grabbed the left side of its neck and its huge jaws closed around the gray flesh.
The creature moved its head and dragged Two several meters across the ground, but the wolf did not let go.
"Awooooooo!" The wolf screamed in pain, the monster was practically dragging him across the ground like a corpse.
"Let go of the Wolf Of Doomsday, bastard!" Kain gathered the last of his Mana.
[Dawn Spear]
Light passed through the opening in the chest and landed on the monster’s shell.
BOOOOM!
At the same time, Lian also moved, seeing that this bastard dared to torture his Colony Member like this made his blood boil with anger.
There were not many things that could make him angry, but hurting something that belonged to him was definitely one of them.
[Ashen Thunder Step]
And after getting close to that damned monster, he raised his palm.
[Suppressing Palm]
He placed the small amount of remaining Eclipse energy on the point of impact, his goal was to weaken the defensive shell around the monster’s heart.
The best way to kill a monster was to destroy its heart and core.
TUM!
The attack hit the target and black lines spread across the shell.
Kain fired the final beam at the same moment.
BOOOOOOM!
The shell cracked and the internal pressure of Lian’s palm passed through the crack.
The monster’s cores and heart trembled and a deep crack appeared on the monster’s heart.
"Now it’s time!" Lian completely covered his fist with ice and then struck the place where the monster’s heart was with all his strength.
"GRAAAAAAAAH!" The monster screamed in pain and anger.
But the young Vorhelm did not stop, feeling that it was still not enough, he started punching with both hands with all his strength.
Kain also sent more Dawn Spears one after another.
Finally, the monster’s shell split open and the heart was revealed.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
Lian split that heart with his final strike, and to make sure the monster would not somehow survive by some miracle...he also tore its cores apart one after another.
The Leviathan became completely still for a moment, and then the twelve white holes on its skull went out one after another.
The first.
The second.
The third.
Until the last one.
Two released its jaws and its sixty-meter-long body slowly fell to its side.
Then...BOOOOOOM!
It crashed onto the remains of the pier, the ground of the city shook and a cloud of dust rose dozens of meters into the air.
But this time, the monster did not get up again.
For several seconds, no one moved, not Lian, not Kain, and not even the few survivors from the two Regions, and the only sound was the sound of pieces of stone falling from the cracked buildings.
[You have killed a Level 50 monster, Leviathan Of Eclipse.]
[Group Kill Reward is being distributed.]
But before reading the rest of the notifications, Lian looked at the corpse, this monster was truly incredible, and he still had three spots among his Special Members.
[Attempting to create a Special Colony Member connection...]
[Failed.]
[The target has no life.]
[Special Colony Membership is only possible with living creatures.]
"I should have tried before killing it." He stared at the corpse for a few seconds.
But he knew that something like this was not possible either, the monster would not surrender and making it surrender was impossible.
Even defeating it had seemed like a miracle.
Kain, who had almost fallen onto his knees, could no longer endure it and fell to the ground and lay down.
"It is finally over... My god, did we really kill a Level 50 Fallen...?"
"Why not? Is it really that unbelievable?" Lian looked at him.
Kain opened his mouth, but said nothing, probably for the first time he had realized that there was no point in answering.
How could someone logically argue with a person who thought killing such a monster was not that special?
[Level increased.]
[You have obtained an S-Rank Talent: Corrupted Sun (S).]
[Due to the Group Kill, the rewards are halved.]
[You have obtained 4730 stats points.]
The young Vorhelm looked at his new level.
Almost at the same time, Kain also looked at the space in front of him for a few seconds.
Then he gave a tired laugh.
"I finally reached Level 37! Who would have thought that killing a Level 50 monster could instantly take me to Level 37?"
Lian said nothing, in fact, he felt a little jealous, he had only increased by one level but this guy had instantly reached Level 37.
Life could really be unfair.
"Even though it was very difficult, killing it was really worth it." The Child Of Light smiled.
He ignored his best friend and walked toward the corpse of the Leviathan.
The monster’s cores were cracked, but the structure itself was still usable for extraction.
Without hesitation, he summoned One, thousands of points of light appeared in front of him and it did not take long before the giant ant appeared in front of him.
When it saw its master, its first reaction was annoyance and strong protest, to the point that it could almost be called anger.
But Lian only pointed toward the Leviathan’s cores and One saw them.
Its antennae rose.
[Level: 20.]
[First Evolution Saturation: High.]
He had been seeing the same sentence for a long time, maybe it was finally time for it to change, at least the cores of this monster should be enough now, right?
The ant went toward the cores and opened its jaws, and it did not take long before it swallowed all of the cores.
For several seconds, nothing happened.
Kain watched while waiting, Two also turned his head toward the ant, and Lian did the same, as if all three of them were waiting to see whether any change would happen or not.
Then One’s body trembled, white light came out from between the joints of its natural armor and its antennae rose sharply.
[Level 50 Fallen cores have been absorbed.]
[First Evolution Saturation: Complete.]
[The quality of the absorbed resources has exceeded the minimum requirement.]
[A rare trait has been detected in the final evolution resource.]
[All conditions for the First Evolution have been completed.]
[Would you like your Special Member to begin its First Evolution?]
One’s body was covered in light, its legs bent for a moment.
"Go back, you can start your evolution process there." Lian immediately opened the Colony House connection.
One did not resist and its body turned into particles of light.
[One has entered the Colony House.]
[Status: Evolution.]
He stared at the empty space in front of him for a few seconds.
Finally.
The giant ant had been waiting for this moment since it reached Level 20.
Now the only question was what it would become when it came out.
The young Vorhelm looked around, the cold air of the city touched his sweaty skin.
The armor was not in good condition, the left shoulder plate was still blackened and several parts of the chest were cracked.
Structural Memory was busy repairing it, but this time the repair was not fast.
The corrupted light had eaten away parts of the internal pathways.
Two was also not in good condition, a burned wound stretched from his shoulder to his side and several parts of his bone armor were broken.
His master sent him back to the Colony House as well.
Then Lian looked around, the city had become very quiet, the number of living humans could almost be counted with a single look.
Three people from the Third Region, a priest whose one arm was burned and whose robe was torn, and two wounded soldiers.
On the other side, the commander of the Sixth Region and three remaining warriors.
Only seven people in total.
All those forces that had been fighting each other to control the shrine an hour ago had now been reduced to seven people, and none of them were in good condition.
The priest of the Third Region looked at the sphere of Witness that had appeared beside Kain’s shoulder again.
Hatred was almost visible on his face, and the commander of the Sixth Region also gripped his cracked weapon more tightly.
Kain noticed it, a little light gathered around his fingers, as if he wanted to finish them as well, there was no reason to keep them alive.
"No." Lian raised his hand.
"Why?" Kain did not turn off the light, but he did not attack.
For several seconds, the two groups of natives only looked at each other and then at Lian.
It was as if they had only just remembered that before the Leviathan appeared, they had been killing each other.
The young Vorhelm took several steps forward, each step making a short metallic sound from his cracked armor.
Then his gaze moved first to the priest of the Third Region and then to the commander of the Sixth Region.
"Well."
He paused for a moment.
"Now I think it is time for someone to explain why two native Regions were killing each other over a shrine."
( Visualization of scenes )

Lian split that heart with his final strike, and to make sure the monster would not somehow survive by some miracle...he also tore its cores apart one after another.
The Leviathan became completely still for a moment, and then the twelve white holes on its skull went out one after another.
The first.
The second.
The third.
Until the last one.
Two released its jaws and its sixty-meter-long body slowly fell to its side.
Then...BOOOOOOM!
It crashed onto the remains of the pier, the ground of the city shook and a cloud of dust rose dozens of meters into the air.
But this time, the monster did not get up again.
For several seconds, no one moved, not Lian, not Kain, and not even the few survivors from the two Regions, and the only sound was the sound of pieces of stone falling from the cracked buildings.
[You have killed a Level 50 monster, Leviathan Of Eclipse.]
[Group Kill Reward is being distributed.]
But before reading the rest of the notifications, Lian looked at the corpse, this monster was truly incredible, and he still had three spots among his Special Members.
[Attempting to create a Special Colony Member connection...]
[Failed.]
[The target has no life.]
[Special Colony Membership is only possible with living creatures.]
"I should have tried before killing it." He stared at the corpse for a few seconds.
But he knew that something like this was not possible either, the monster would not surrender and making it surrender was impossible.
Even defeating it had seemed like a miracle.
Kain, who had almost fallen onto his knees, could no longer endure it and fell to the ground and lay down.
"It is finally over...
My god, did we really kill a Level 50 Fallen...?"
"Why not?
Is it really that unbelievable?" Lian looked at him.
Kain opened his mouth, but said nothing, probably for the first time he had realized that there was no point in answering.
How could someone logically argue with a person who thought killing such a monster was not that special?
[Level increased.]
[You have obtained an S-Rank Talent: Corrupted Sun (S).]
[Due to the Group Kill, the rewards are halved.]
[You have obtained 4730 stats points.]
The young Vorhelm looked at his new level.
Almost at the same time, Kain also looked at the space in front of him for a few seconds.
Then he gave a tired laugh.
"I finally reached Level 37!
Who would have thought that killing a Level 50 monster could instantly take me to Level 37?"
Lian said nothing, in fact, he felt a little jealous, he had only increased by one level but this guy had instantly reached Level 37.
Life could really be unfair.
"Even though it was very difficult, killing it was really worth it." The Child Of Light smiled.
He ignored his best friend and walked toward the corpse of the Leviathan.
The monster’s cores were cracked, but the structure itself was still usable for extraction.
Without hesitation, he summoned One, thousands of points of light appeared in front of him and it did not take long before the giant ant appeared in front of him.
When it saw its master, its first reaction was annoyance and strong protest, to the point that it could almost be called anger.
But Lian only pointed toward the Leviathan’s cores and One saw them.
Its antennae rose.
[Level: 20.]
[First Evolution Saturation: High.]
He had been seeing the same sentence for a long time, maybe it was finally time for it to change, at least the cores of this monster should be enough now, right?
The ant went toward the cores and opened its jaws, and it did not take long before it swallowed all of the cores.
For several seconds, nothing happened.
Kain watched while waiting, Two also turned his head toward the ant, and Lian did the same, as if all three of them were waiting to see whether any change would happen or not.
Then One’s body trembled, white light came out from between the joints of its natural armor and its antennae rose sharply.
[Level 50 Fallen cores have been absorbed.]
[First Evolution Saturation: Complete.]
[The quality of the absorbed resources has exceeded the minimum requirement.]
[A rare trait has been detected in the final evolution resource.]
[All conditions for the First Evolution have been completed.]
[Would you like your Special Member to begin its First Evolution?]
One’s body was covered in light, its legs bent for a moment.
"Go back, you can start your evolution process there." Lian immediately opened the Colony House connection.
One did not resist and its body turned into particles of light.
[One has entered the Colony House.]
[Status: Evolution.]
He stared at the empty space in front of him for a few seconds.
Finally.
The giant ant had been waiting for this moment since it reached Level 20.
Now the only question was what it would become when it came out.
The young Vorhelm looked around, the cold air of the city touched his sweaty skin.
The armor was not in good condition, the left shoulder plate was still blackened and several parts of the chest were cracked.
Structural Memory was busy repairing it, but this time the repair was not fast.
The corrupted light had eaten away parts of the internal pathways.
Two was also not in good condition, a burned wound stretched from his shoulder to his side and several parts of his bone armor were broken.
His master sent him back to the Colony House as well.
Then Lian looked around, the city had become very quiet, the number of living humans could almost be counted with a single look.
Three people from the Third Region, a priest whose one arm was burned and whose robe was torn, and two wounded soldiers.
On the other side, the commander of the Sixth Region and three remaining warriors.
Only seven people in total.
All those forces that had been fighting each other to control the shrine an hour ago had now been reduced to seven people, and none of them were in good condition.
The priest of the Third Region looked at the sphere of Witness that had appeared beside Kain’s shoulder again.
Hatred was almost visible on his face, and the commander of the Sixth Region also gripped his cracked weapon more tightly.
Kain noticed it, a little light gathered around his fingers, as if he wanted to finish them as well, there was no reason to keep them alive.
"No." Lian raised his hand.
"Why?" Kain did not turn off the light, but he did not attack.
For several seconds, the two groups of natives only looked at each other and then at Lian.
It was as if they had only just remembered that before the Leviathan appeared, they had been killing each other.
The young Vorhelm took several steps forward, each step making a short metallic sound from his cracked armor.
Then his gaze moved first to the priest of the Third Region and then to the commander of the Sixth Region.
"Well."
He paused for a moment.
"Now I think it is time for someone to explain why two native Regions were killing each other over a shrine."
( Visualization of scenes )

chapters.title: Chapter 524: The Corrupted Sun
paragraphs: For a moment, Lian took his eyes away from the survivors.
[Corrupted Sun.]
[Rank: S.]
[A talent formed from the coexistence of the Law of Light and Eclipse.]
[Compatibility with the Law of Light has greatly increased.]
[The user can perceive the movement path, refraction, reflection, and concentration of Light with greater accuracy.]
[The user can use Mana and Eclipse Energy to turn existing Light into Corrupted Light, as long as Light exists, you can create Corrupted Light.]
[Corrupted Light keeps the speed, penetration, and spreading properties of Light, but it will gain the properties of erosion and destruction.]
[Corrupted Light does not have the properties of healing and purification.]
[Controlling Corrupted Light in bright environments will be easier and require less energy.]
[Resistance against all offensive Light and Corrupted Light skills increases by 200%.]
Something changed in Lian’s perception, not like when his stats increased and his body came under pressure, this time the change was more like a sense opening that had not existed before.
The Light around him was no longer just "brightness."
He could see its path.

Sunlight came down through the clouds, broke across the white stones, part of it hit the blood-covered armor of a Region Three soldier and another part reflected from the surface of another soldier’s body.
Thousands and even millions and billions of lines of Light could be seen, and they were all connected to each other, if he wanted, he could choose one line from among all that Light.
And more interestingly? He could use each of them like a weapon, of course, they could only be useful when the enemy had no ability to deal with them.
He moved his fingers slightly, as if he was trying to move them like moving the notes of a musical instrument ... and he succeeded.
Interesting.
But Corrupted Sun was not over yet.
[New innate skill has been formed.]
[Six Sources of Immortality]
[Create six independent Sources within your body, each continuously circulating Corrupted Light throughout your physical structure.]
[Whenever physical damage is inflicted, the Sources automatically direct Corrupted Light toward the affected area.]
[Rather than regenerating damaged tissue through conventional healing, Corrupted Light erodes the very structure of the damage itself.]
[Cuts, fractures, burns, ruptures, destroyed tissue, and other forms of physical injury are treated as foreign alterations to the body’s recorded stable state and are gradually erased.]
[As the structure of the injury is destroyed, the affected area is forced back toward its previously stabilized condition.]
[Each Source functions independently, but the remaining Sources can partially compensate for destroyed ones.]
[The destruction of a Source reduces the overall response speed, restoration capacity, and stability of the ability.]
[As long as at least one Source remains active, the user possesses extreme resistance to death caused purely by physical destruction.]
[As long as all six Sources have not been destroyed, complete physical death is impossible.]
[The amount of Eclipse Energy consumed increases according to the severity, scale, and complexity of the damage being erased.]
[Multiple large-scale injuries occurring simultaneously can overwhelm the circulation rate of the Sources and greatly increase energy consumption.]
[This ability stabilizes only the physical structure of the body and does not grant absolute protection against direct destruction of the soul ]
[If all six Sources are destroyed, the immortality effect will immediately cease.]
[Requires 5000 Spirit for full activation.]

The corner of Lian’s lips rose slightly, he did not expect to be lucky enough to obtain this skill, the same crazy self-healing mechanism of the Leviathan that had made killing it impossible for them.
And now he had obtained it and could even activate it, but unfortunately, he did not currently meet its initial requirements for activation.
But once he could activate it, he would no longer be physically killable, unless the opponent was powerful enough to destroy all six sources in one attack.
And he doubted that there were any other beings besides Demons and Overlords and those above them that could have such power.
"What are you doing?" Kain asked after seeing his long silence.
"Nothing." He answered calmly and the notifications disappeared, now he could return to the problem in front of him.
"Why was Region Six here?" His eyes first stopped on the commander of Region Six.
The man only looked at him with hatred.
Lian waited for a few seconds but no answer came, so he turned his head toward the priest of Region Three.

"And why were you trying to open this shrine? Why did you want the sphere Of Witness?" From the conflict between these two Regions, he could guess that the sphere Of Witness was also related to their conflict.
But whatever it was, he did not mind knowing, the more he knew about the situation between the natives, the better.
The priest also said nothing.
His left arm was almost completely burned from the elbow to his fingers, and he could barely keep it beside his body.
Blood had come down from the cut beside his head and dried on his cheek, but there was no sign of begging or fear in his eyes.
Kain took one step forward.
"You lost almost all of your people." His eyes moved for a moment over the scattered bodies in the square.
"I don’t think now is a very good time to play the role of loyal people."
"Barbarian." The commander of Region Six spat the blood in his mouth beside his foot.
"You really like that word." Kain let out a short sigh.
"Death is better than selling the Region." The priest of Light raised his head slightly.
His voice was tired but did not shake, his fanaticism and faith in his words were completely clear.
Two stood a few meters behind Lian and slowly lowered his head.
The shadow of the giant wolf’s head fell over the priest’s body and one of the Region Three soldiers unconsciously took half a step back.
But the priest did not even blink.
The young Vorhelm looked at him, it was real fanaticism, not just an act of bravery and things like that, this man was truly ready to die.
Those few natives from Region Three that they had fought at that time and handed over to the Awakened, after seeing Two, had been extremely afraid of him.
But this priest was not like that, there was no fear in his eyes and more threats would probably only make him more determined.
Lian asked another question about Region Six and again there was silence, then he asked about the shrine but received no answer.

He asked about the sphere Of Witness but the only thing that changed was the priest’s expression, for a few seconds, he looked at the sphere Of Witness floating beside Kain with something close to anger.
He threatened them even more and tried to use physical torture as well, but the result was no different, neither of them was willing to speak.
He even went to the soldiers, questioned them separately, threatened them separately, but nothing... it was also clear that they were not ordinary soldiers.
It was normal too, if this mission was really important to both Regions, it was natural that they would not send a few ordinary soldiers.
Lian finally let out a short sigh and then turned toward Kain.
"It’s useless. Let’s forget about it."
"Okay." Kain looked at him and shrugged, he had also tried his own methods but had received no answer.
The young Vorhelm took one step toward the seven people, his right hand rose.
No skill had been activated yet, there was no need either.
The commander of Region Six clenched his jaw and his three warriors also seemed ready for death.
The two Region Three soldiers also prepared themselves and the priest? He laughed.
At first with a weak sound, almost like a cough, but
little by little the laugh became more real.
Blood came down from the corner of his mouth, but his smile did not disappear.
"Kill me, do you think the blood of a few priests will change anything? Do you think by killing us you can stop what has been promised?"
Lian kept his hand there and the priest took a short breath.
"The Child of Light will descend soon." His voice was firmer this time and something appeared in his eyes that pain and tiredness could not put out.
"And when he comes, all the blood you savage barbarians have spilled will be answered for. Every shrine you burned, every priest you killed, and every relic you stole... all of them."
He was no longer listening to the threats, two words remained in his mind.
Child of Light.
His hand slowly lowered and his head turned toward his best friend.
Kain also seemed to have realized something, he was not stupid either and those two words were enough to make several things come to his mind.
[Child of Light.] It was the name of his talent.
Tear of Witness, then the reaction of the shrine and the sphere Of Witness, or even the pure Light that the Region Three priests had immediately recognized.
And now it seemed that there was also a prophecy.
All of this was enough for Lian to reach a complete conclusion and a logical explanation, no matter how stupid it sounded, there could only be one explanation.
"I think your Child of Light is standing right in front of you right now." He looked at the priest again.
"What did you say?" The priest even forgot his pain for a moment.
"Him." But in response, the young Vorhelm only pointed at his friend.
Kain followed Lian’s finger down and then looked at himself.
"Why did you suddenly bring me into these people’s cult?" Then he sighed, he had also reached the same conclusion himself, but he did not feel good about it at all.
But Lian completely ignored him.

"Old man, just think for a moment, the Tear of Witness chose him, the sphere Of Witness chose him by itself, and your shrine responded to his Light without the ritual you had been preparing for him for several days."
"And as far as I saw, among everyone here who used Light, his Light was the purest."
The priest remained motionless and then shook his head.
"No."
"No... that’s impossible."
Disbelief could be seen in his eyes ... he had heard something that he would rather die than have it be true...
"I guess your god chose a barbarian as the Child of Light."

chapters.title: Chapter 525: The True Child Of Light
paragraphs: "This reaction is more like what I wanted to say myself." Kain pressed his lips together after seeing the old man’s reaction.
He himself was not happy with the reasoning and the conclusion either, but seeing an old man behave like this because of him was annoying.
But the priest could not hear him.
"The Child of Light cannot be an outsider." The man stared at the ground.
"He cannot have come from another world. The prophecy... the prophecy never said—"
His sentence remained unfinished, because he himself realized it...the prophecy had never said such a thing...or at least, it had never said such a thing as far as he knew.
His eyes showed disbelief.
"The Tear..." His voice became quieter.
"The Tear of Witness was supposed to be kept for him."
The two soldiers behind him looked at each other.
The priest continued, speaking more to himself than to the others.
"The sphere was the same. All the inheritances of the Witness... were supposed to be given to him when the Child of Light descended. No one except him should have been able to—"
He became silent again...his mind was clearly fighting against something he had believed his entire life.
"Well, I don’t know if I should help or let him deal with it himself." Kain said calmly.
Lian did not answer, in his opinion, the best thing was to wait and see what would happen.
"Proof." The priest finally took his eyes away from the sphere.
"Proof of what?" The Child of Light frowned.
"Prove it...if you really are what he says you are...prove it."
"How?"
"I will test you."
The priest moved the torn collar of his clothes aside with his good hand and pulled something out from under it, a broken necklace.
In the middle of its short chain, there was a round piece that at first looked like nothing more than old metal.
But when the man placed it in his palm, seven very small mirror pieces opened around it.
[Seven-Ray Seal.]
The priest placed it on a relatively flat piece of stone, his good hand was shaking too much for him to put enough Mana into it.
So without saying anything, he dragged the tip of his finger across the broken edge of his own armor.
His skin was cut and a drop of blood fell onto the center of the seal, and then all seven mirrors opened at the same time.
"Priest...in your condition—" One of the Region Three soldiers said in a low voice.
"Silence."
The man did not even look at him and looked directly at Kain.
"Do not activate any skill. Do not give any structure to your Light, only use raw Light."
"Alright." He took a calm breath and held his right hand above the seal, for a moment, nothing happened.
Then a very weak Light was released from his palm.
The first mirror lit up.
Click.
The second and third also lit up behind it.
The priest continued watching, his expression almost did not change.
The fourth one lit up.
And this caused a small line to appear between his eyebrows.
The fifth one lit up.
The man’s breath stopped for a moment.
One of the two Region Three soldiers unconsciously took one step closer.
The sixth one lit up!
The color slowly disappeared from the priest’s face, leaving no anger or doubt.
Only one mirror remained.
"I think this last one is a little stubborn." Kain looked at it.
Before he could finish his sentence, the seventh one lit up and Light passed through all seven mirrors, but what happened after that made even Kain become silent.

The Light did not break apart, no colors appeared around it, the seven mirrors were supposed to divide the Light into different colors, this was what happened when a normal Light Element user put Light into the artifact.
But that did not happen!
The beam that came from Kain remained white and pure after passing through all of them, and there was no impurity in it.
The priest did not breathe.
The point of white Light expanded and all seven mirrors automatically rotated..
Click.
The Light gathered in the center of the seal and for a moment a symbol appeared on the ground.
An eye with a drop under it, the same symbol they had seen on the shrine gate.
No one said anything.
The Region Three priest only stared for a few seconds, his lips slightly apart.
It was as if everything he had believed in throughout his life had suddenly changed from a stupid story into something standing a few steps in front of him.
His legs bent, and he slowly fell onto both knees..
"Oh." Kain made a strange face.
"Child of Light..." The priest lowered his head.
The two Region Three soldiers looked at him and almost at the same time, they also knelt down.
Kain really had nothing to say this time.
The priest lowered his head even more.
"We did not recognize you." His voice had become calm, unlike before.
"We raised our weapons against you, sent forces to capture you, and even tried to take back something that had been kept for you from the beginning."
His good hand clenched in shame.
"I ask for your forgiveness, Child of Light."
Kain looked at Lian.
For someone who usually almost always had something to say, his expression was very clear.
What exactly am I supposed to do with this?
Lian only raised his shoulder very slightly.
The Child narrowed his eyes, this was not helpful.
Another voice broke the silence.
Everyone turned toward the commander of Region Six, the man had remained silent until now but his expression had completely changed.
Of course, it was not the same hatred from before or anger, it was something much closer to fear.
"No."
His hand tightened around the handle of his weapon.
"This should not have happened."
The Region Three priest slowly raised his head.
The commander stared at Kain, but it was as if he no longer saw an outsider...he was seeing something much greater.
"Damn you..." His breathing became heavy.
"We are too late. We should not have let you open the shrine. We should not have let the Tear reach him and we definitely should not have let the sphere choose him."
"What are you talking about?" Kain frowned.
The commander did not answer him, he turned his head toward his three remaining warriors.
"Kill him."
One of the warriors did not move for a moment.
"Commander?"
"Kill him!" The man shouted this time and more blood came out from the wound in his side.
"If he stays alive, the prophecy will begin! Kill him right here. It does not matter what happens to us, it does not matter if none of us leave this city alive!"
The three warriors looked at each other for a moment, then their weapons were raised.
Kain gathered Light around his fingers to protect himself, but before he could move, Lian raised his right hand.
"Not necessary."
The commander gathered darkness around himself, and two warriors moved from the left and right.
The third one went directly toward Kain, the distance was about twenty meters.
But this time Lian was not looking at their bodies, he was seeing the Light, the white beams on the blades and the reflection of the sun from the edges of the armor.
The Light that came from the sun and fell across the commander’s face.
The Eclipse Core gave a small pulse and a small amount of energy was released from it, at that moment four lines of Light...became black.
The young Vorhelm only moved his index finger a few centimeters.
There was no explosion and there was not even any special sound.
Four very thin lines of Corrupted Light, so fast that normal eyes could barely follow their paths, passed through the space between them.
The commander reacted in time, a shield of darkness gathered in front of his body.
The first line reached the shadow and for a moment the surface of the shield even became thicker, but then a black point appeared at the center of contact.
The line simply passed through it, as if the structure of the darkness no longer existed at that point.
The thin line entered the commander’s chest and the other three lines reached the warriors almost at the same time.
One of the men still took two steps...then the sword fell from his hand.
The second one tried to gather Mana in his legs, but the energy in his paths became unstable, his knee bent and he fell onto the stone.
The third one put his hand on his throat and then he also fell.
There were no huge wounds on their bodies, this attack was not made to destroy buildings.
These lines made of Corrupted Light had eroded their vital organs and as a result, their dead bodies fell one after another.
The commander lasted a few seconds longer, his knees bent, but he held himself up with his sword.
Blood came down from his mouth, but his eyes fell on Lian, and it was as if Kain no longer mattered to him...as if he had seen something even more frightening...
The man’s eyes first moved in disbelief over the lines of Corrupted Light disappearing in the air.
Then his expression changed.
He had recognized something or at least remembered something.
"Corrupted Light..." The man whispered in a rough voice.
He paused and let out another breath, then those words came out of his mouth, more precisely, it was a title.
Something that even the Region Three priest became tense after hearing.
"The Dormant Calamity..."
Real fear could be seen on the face of the Region Six commander, a fear as if he had faced the end of the world...
Not fear of his own death, a much older fear.
It was as if what stood in front of him had, for a few moments, overlapped with something from his childhood stories or religious warnings.
Then the strength left his legs...his body fell onto the stone and became still.

sentences.text: "This reaction is more like what I wanted to say myself." Kain pressed his lips together after seeing the old man’s reaction.
He himself was not happy with the reasoning and the conclusion either, but seeing an old man behave like this because of him was annoying.
But the priest could not hear him.
"The Child of Light cannot be an outsider." The man stared at the ground.
"He cannot have come from another world.
The prophecy... the prophecy never said—"
His sentence remained unfinished, because he himself realized it...the prophecy had never said such a thing...or at least, it had never said such a thing as far as he knew.
His eyes showed disbelief.
"The Tear..." His voice became quieter.
"The Tear of Witness was supposed to be kept for him."
The two soldiers behind him looked at each other.
The priest continued, speaking more to himself than to the others.
"The sphere was the same.
All the inheritances of the Witness... were supposed to be given to him when the Child of Light descended.
No one except him should have been able to—"
He became silent again...his mind was clearly fighting against something he had believed his entire life.
"Well, I don’t know if I should help or let him deal with it himself." Kain said calmly.
Lian did not answer, in his opinion, the best thing was to wait and see what would happen.
"Proof." The priest finally took his eyes away from the sphere.
"Proof of what?" The Child of Light frowned.
"Prove it...if you really are what he says you are...prove it."
"How?"
"I will test you."
The priest moved the torn collar of his clothes aside with his good hand and pulled something out from under it, a broken necklace.
In the middle of its short chain, there was a round piece that at first looked like nothing more than old metal.
But when the man placed it in his palm, seven very small mirror pieces opened around it.
[Seven-Ray Seal.]
The priest placed it on a relatively flat piece of stone, his good hand was shaking too much for him to put enough Mana into it.
So without saying anything, he dragged the tip of his finger across the broken edge of his own armor.
His skin was cut and a drop of blood fell onto the center of the seal, and then all seven mirrors opened at the same time.
"Priest...in your condition—" One of the Region Three soldiers said in a low voice.
"Silence."
The man did not even look at him and looked directly at Kain.
"Do not activate any skill.
Do not give any structure to your Light, only use raw Light."
"Alright." He took a calm breath and held his right hand above the seal, for a moment, nothing happened.
Then a very weak Light was released from his palm.
The first mirror lit up.
Click.
The second and third also lit up behind it.
The priest continued watching, his expression almost did not change.
The fourth one lit up.
And this caused a small line to appear between his eyebrows.
The fifth one lit up.
The man’s breath stopped for a moment.
One of the two Region Three soldiers unconsciously took one step closer.
The sixth one lit up!
The color slowly disappeared from the priest’s face, leaving no anger or doubt.
Only one mirror remained.
"I think this last one is a little stubborn." Kain looked at it.
Before he could finish his sentence, the seventh one lit up and Light passed through all seven mirrors, but what happened after that made even Kain become silent.

The Light did not break apart, no colors appeared around it, the seven mirrors were supposed to divide the Light into different colors, this was what happened when a normal Light Element user put Light into the artifact.
But that did not happen!
The beam that came from Kain remained white and pure after passing through all of them, and there was no impurity in it.
The priest did not breathe.
The point of white Light expanded and all seven mirrors automatically rotated..
Click.
The Light gathered in the center of the seal and for a moment a symbol appeared on the ground.
An eye with a drop under it, the same symbol they had seen on the shrine gate.
No one said anything.
The Region Three priest only stared for a few seconds, his lips slightly apart.
It was as if everything he had believed in throughout his life had suddenly changed from a stupid story into something standing a few steps in front of him.
His legs bent, and he slowly fell onto both knees..
"Oh." Kain made a strange face.
"Child of Light..." The priest lowered his head.
The two Region Three soldiers looked at him and almost at the same time, they also knelt down.
Kain really had nothing to say this time.
The priest lowered his head even more.
"We did not recognize you." His voice had become calm, unlike before.
"We raised our weapons against you, sent forces to capture you, and even tried to take back something that had been kept for you from the beginning."
His good hand clenched in shame.
"I ask for your forgiveness, Child of Light."
Kain looked at Lian.
For someone who usually almost always had something to say, his expression was very clear.
What exactly am I supposed to do with this?
Lian only raised his shoulder very slightly.
The Child narrowed his eyes, this was not helpful.
Another voice broke the silence.
Everyone turned toward the commander of Region Six, the man had remained silent until now but his expression had completely changed.
Of course, it was not the same hatred from before or anger, it was something much closer to fear.

His hand tightened around the handle of his weapon.
"This should not have happened."

chapters.title: Chapter 526: The Seven Regions
paragraphs: Lian heard that title, the man was clearly calling him by it, as if he had realized some truth and that was why he called him this.
But why? Why did he call him this? Where did this title come from? And based on the priest’s reaction, it seemed to be related to the Child of Light as well.
What exactly was going on? It seemed there were many things they did not know about.
"Why did he suddenly become like this?" Kain also had not understood anything.
"I don’t know." This time the answer was completely honest, and Lian looked at the Region Three priest.
The man was still kneeling, but his head was no longer lowered, and the color of his face had also changed slightly.
"You know what he meant, don’t you?"
But the old man did not answer immediately.
"You know that title?"
The priest remained silent for at least a few more seconds, finally he sighed and started speaking.
"It’s from the prophecy of Region One."
"What prophecy?" Kain frowned.
"The one that announced your coming, Your Highness." The man kept his eyes on him.
"Then what is the rest of it?"
The priest remained silent.
"Why aren’t you talking anymore?"
"For the same reason all six other Regions want to destroy us." The old man pressed his lips together.
"All six Regions?" Lian gave him his full attention this time, why would six Regions want to destroy one Region?
"Yes."
"Why?"
The priest looked at Lian for a moment, very briefly, if it had been someone else, they might not have even noticed.
But Lian saw it, and that look gave him more information than the first answer, it was the same kind of look that the commander of Region Six had given him before his death.
A look full of fear and terror, as if he was the embodiment of doomsday or something like that.
"The prophecy is not only about the descent of the Child of Light." The man took a calm breath.
"When the Child of Light comes... he will not come alone."
Kain turned his head toward Lian and his friend also said nothing, but an unpleasant feeling appeared inside him.
"With me? Who is coming with me? And why does it sound like something bad?" He only knew one person who could come with him and always stay by his side, and that was his best friend.
"I cannot say more than this." The priest slowly shook his head.
"You can’t or you don’t want to?" Kain frowned even deeper.
The man looked directly at him, this time there was no hostility in his eyes, but there was a boundary that he was not willing to cross even for someone he considered the Child of Light.
"Both."
Lian also told him not to insist, at least for now, what they had learned was already big enough.
A few moments later, Kain looked at the priest who was still kneeling on both knees.
"One more thing."
"Yes, Child of Light." The man immediately lowered his head.
"Stand up first."
"But—"
"I really can’t talk to someone while they’re kneeling in front of me, I’ve already seen enough strange things today."
The man stood up hesitantly, his legs shaking slightly.
Lian noticed that if he did not lean against the broken wall beside him, he would probably fall down again.
One of the two Region Three soldiers stepped forward to help him, but the priest stopped him with a movement of his hand.
He himself sat beside a piece of a pillar and used his teeth to tear off part of his clothes, then tied it around his half-burned arm.
A few minutes ago he had been a prisoner in front of them, and now?
His behavior was more like someone who had finally been allowed to believe a piece of news that had always only been a distant promise after many years.
It seemed it no longer mattered to him that the Child of Light was an outsider.
"Now that things are calm and there is no one bothering us anymore, how about you start from the beginning? What is this Region One? Which Divine do they follow?" Lian finally spoke.
And after thinking for a moment, he added,
"And explain why the six Regions want to destroy your Region."
The man rested his head against the wall behind him and closed his eyes for a few seconds.
"We waited for decades...waiting for the signs."

"When Region One announced the prophecy, many people in Region Three celebrated. Some thought it meant the period of misery was over. The Child of Light would come, the sacred relics would return, and we could live outside the walls of the Region again."
His smile disappeared.
"Then the other Regions reacted."
"First, trade became smaller. Then several roads were closed. Caravans that had traveled for years without problems disappeared, they wanted to isolate us."
The fingers of his good hand closed over his knee.
"Then the killing of our priests began."
The two soldiers beside him lowered their eyes.

"Every time there was news about a relic belonging to the Divine of Light, someone else was already there before we could reach it. Sometimes Region Six. Sometimes forces from Region Two. Sometimes..." He paused. "People we could not even understand which Region they worked for."
"So you were basically surrounded." Kain looked at the bodies of the four Region Six soldiers.
"Not in the usual way."
"Because they can’t enter Region Three, right?" Lian asked.
The priest turned his head toward him.
"That’s right, you have probably realized by now why the seven Regions still exist after all these centuries."

"The Regions are not just cities, long before we started calling them Region One, Two, or Three, they were seven shelters, each one was built by one of the seven Divines for the people under their protection."
Lian already knew this to some degree, the seven Regions had survived for centuries against attacks from monsters and even Demons.
But now the full picture was becoming clearer.
"No one can enter a Region without the permission of that Region’s Lord."
"So instead of attacking your home, they took away everything outside it from you." Lian concluded.
"Yes."
"And they are waiting for you to become weaker."
"Yes."
"Or they want to finish the job before your descent, but why? What exactly is this prophecy that makes them want to destroy you this much?"
"This...I cannot tell you the prophecy without permission."
The young Vorhelm remained silent, what exactly did this prophecy say that it had been able to make six Regions turn against one Region?
What had caused the natives, when this world was already dealing with the apocalypse, to want to destroy one Region instead of working together?
He also understood why the natives of Region Three had been so harsh and cold, for decades they had been treated differently among humanity and had been rejected and isolated by their own race.
"And about which Divine Region One follows...the order we use today actually starts with Region One."
"They follow the Divine of Fate."
"The same crazy people who made the prophecy?" Kain said.
"I would not use that word in front of them." The priest gave him a short look.
"But isn’t it wrong?"
"It is not completely wrong, Region One is the smallest of all the Regions. As far as I know, today their population does not even reach a thousand people, maybe only a few hundred."
"That is all?"
"Those few hundred people caused the other six Regions to change the path of their next decades, they control the narratives, and all the Regions more or less follow their prophecies..."

"They almost never leave their Region. They do not have an army like Region Two, their trade is limited, and even we have very little information about what is inside their land. But when they announce a true prophecy...no one ignores it."
"Why? What made them have so much credibility?"

"They predicted the apocalypse, at that time no one believed them and everyone saw the result...after that they made dozens of other prophecies and all of them turned out to be true, to some extent, it is also because of them that humanity has not gone extinct yet."

The young Vorhelm remained silent, the Divine of Fate and its followers were the most mysterious among all seven Divines and their religions, even in the former Ruined Realms, there had not been much information about them.
The priest continued his explanation.
"Anyway, Region Two follows the Divine of War and Destruction."

"It is the most military Region among the seven Regions. Most of their children receive combat training from a young age. Power, competition, and victory are not just tools for them, they are part of their faith."
"They fight most of the wars against monsters?" Lian asked.
"For the past few centuries, yes. Whenever a very powerful monster gets close to the safe routes, Region Two is usually the first place to send a large force."
"So at least they have some use." Kain said.
"As long as they don’t decide that you are the problem." The priest gave him a short look.
"I understand." He stopped his smile.
The priest moved slightly.
"Region Three...is our Region." His expression became slightly softer for a moment.
"Followers of the Divine of Light and Life."
These two words together caught Lian’s attention, until today they had seen most of the relics of this Divine from the aspect of "Light", but apparently Life was also a major part of its domain.
Even in the former Ruined Realms, it was mostly called the Divine of Light.

"Most of our abilities are focused around Light, healing, purification, protection, and growth. Even the farming lands inside the Region are fed by old Mana networks. That is why famine and medicine were never our biggest problems."
"Of course, we also have very strong offensive abilities...but we are not the best in this field..."

chapters.title: Chapter 527: The Seven Divines
paragraphs: "Region Four follows the Divine of Chaos."
Lian immediately thought of the Wolfgrave, as well as the ruined civilization he had found around that area, he had encountered some remains related to the followers of that god there.
From what he had seen, he could only say that they definitely had a very deep and very different view of life.

"Region Four is stranger than the others. Even they themselves do not always agree on what Chaos means. Some of their sects believe Chaos means freedom of choice, while some say it means breaking anything that limits the future to a single path."
"As long as there is a second path, fate is not a command, huh?" Lian quietly whispered, as this sentence was suddenly remembered in his mind.
The priest looked directly at him.
"That is one of their slogans...Have you met them before?" he asked and then added.

"That is one of the oldest sentences connected to the Divine of Chaos. But Region Four does not have only one school. Some of their branches are almost harmless, some of them...it is better to never be alone with them."
Lian looked at Two, that wolf was the result of the work of one of those branches, he had no disagreement with this part.
They really could be crazy.
"Saying that I have met them would be wrong, I have only seen some things related to them, however, since they do not like Fate very much, what is their relationship with you?"

"Well...they did not care about us from the beginning and it is still the same, but they do not act against Fate either...with all their beliefs and teachings, they still do not have the courage to do that," the old priest answered.
"How ridiculous," Lian laughed a little, he did not expect those crazy people to not have the courage to oppose Fate despite everything they said.
"Anyway, Region Five follows the Divine of Eternity and Immortality."
"The name is too ambitious," Kain said.
"They themselves have not become immortal yet," the priest answered without changing his expression.
Kain almost laughed
"The oldest living families among the seven Regions are mostly there. They work on increasing lifespan, preserving the body, keeping the soul, transferring memories, and preventing decay."
"How long can they live?"
"For normal people, there is not much difference. But some of their elders...have lived for several hundred years, since the same year the world entered this era full of destruction and monsters."
Lian slightly raised his eyebrows, this information was more important than it seemed at first.
If there were people in the Ruined Realm who had lived for several centuries, they probably had information that could explain many things.
"Do they know more about the time before the Fall? Or the reason for what happened to this world?"

"A lot more, and why our world became like this? Well...that is information that perhaps their oldest people know, but I doubt anyone knows the real reason," the priest answered after a short silence.

"And do they give that information?" The young Vorhelm was not disappointed after hearing that perhaps no one knew about the Calamities, and it was still possible that they at least knew one or two things.
But perhaps in the end, the best way to learn more about the Calamities was Ezrak.
"Rarely, Region Five gives almost nothing valuable without getting something more valuable in return," the old man gave a bitter smile.
Lian kept this in his mind as well, perhaps he would have a chance to meet them in the future, and even if they did not know anything about the calamities, they might have other useful information.
"Region Six follows the Divine of Shadow and Darkness."
"I think this one could be guessed," Kain said.
"Infiltration, hiding, spying, assassination, gathering information, and moving through darkness. They are the best at all of these."
"So the reason your secret operation had an entire army as guests after three days is clear, you cannot hide anything from them, huh?" The Child of Light looked at the corpses.
"Almost no major operation outside the borders of Region Three can stay hidden from Region Six for long."
"They are annoying."
"That was the mildest description I have heard of them," the priest looked at him.
Only one remained.
"Region Seven follows the Divine of Soul and Dream."
The priest continued:
"Culturally, they are different from most Regions. Many of their teachings are built around the soul, sleep, memory, dreams, and mental communication, and they are also good at making artifacts."
"So they can enter your mind?" Kain frowned slightly.
"Some of them.
"Great."
"What about their army? They do not seem that strong."
"Their army cannot directly be compared to Region Two, but if you think that means attacking them is easy, you are wrong."
"Why?"
"Because some of Region Seven’s defenses are not walls at all."
Kain became silent.
The priest explained.

"You may think you passed through the gate. Walk for hours. Fight a guard. Even think you entered the center of the Region...and then wake up and realize that you had been lying asleep a few steps in front of the entrance the entire time."
"Okay... I do not like this one," the Child of Light sighed.

Lian was also thinking, he had previous information about this Divine as well, according to what they knew from the previous Ruined Realms, the followers of this god were considered some of the most harmless ones.
He did not know if they were the same in this world or not, but at least in the previous ones, if a small civilization of them existed, they were isolated and tried to hide as much as possible.
They were more defensive than aggressive, and because of that, dealing with them was not easy, and since nothing about them seemed especially dangerous, the Awakened also ignored them.
Of course, in the ruins related to this Divine, good artifacts and skill books for protection against mental attacks, and even skill books for mental attacks, had been obtained.
Methods of Soul Refining had also been discovered and developed through the remains of their civilizations.
Lian stayed silent for a while.

Until today, "the seven Regions" had been more of a geographical term to him, he knew they were special, the fact that unlike the previous Ruined Realms, seven civilizations had still managed to survive in this world showed how special they were.
But until now, he had never thought much about them, and now he could see that the reality was much more complicated.

Each Region was the heir of one of the seven Divines, with a different religion, different culture, different way of fighting, different technology and artifacts, and differences that apparently went back for centuries.
Now a prophecy had disturbed this entire fragile structure.
"But this prophecy is still bothering me," he looked at the priest again.
"What?"
"The Child of Light is chosen and sent by a god, you believe that you will be saved by this person, and even the apocalypse will end and your world will also be saved...right?"
"Yes, this is the belief of me and all the followers of the Divine of Light."

"Then why, from the view of the other Regions, even Region One, is this not a good thing? What exactly is said in this prophecy that made everyone look at the negative side? Is it related to the companion? But what is this companion supposed to do?"
This time, the priest did not answer immediately, the same silence appeared again whenever the prophecy was mentioned.
"Because what comes after the Child of Light...from their view, is not salvation, but it could be the end of the world...all worlds."

"If my guess is correct, the prophecy does not say anything about salvation, this is your belief, because you believe your god is on the right side, right?" Lian added again with the same expressionless face.
Kain looked at Lian, he did not know where this discussion was going, but he also had a bad feeling about this prophecy.
What did it mean that he was supposed to have some connection to the destruction of the worlds in this prophecy?
"We cannot talk about the prophecy...that prophecy is blasphemy and talking about it has been forbidden by the Lord," the priest did not answer again.
However, his words confirmed Lian’s reasoning, the prophecy did not say anything about the Child of Light coming to save the world, and that was why it was considered blasphemy.
But he did not like his own reasoning, what did it mean that both he and Kain might have something to do with the destruction of the worlds?
Where did this stupid prophecy even come from?
What is the origin of the followers of the Divine of Fate?
"Am I really going to become the reason the worlds are destroyed?" But he did not reach a conclusion.
It was possible that the prophecy had nothing to do with the destruction of the worlds, maybe all these natives had simply misunderstood it.
Several minutes of silence passed.
The priest now looked less like a prisoner and more like a very tired man who had finally allowed his body to feel the pain.
He rested his head against the pillar and.
"When I was a child, the first outer shrine I knew was lost."
Kain and Lian looked at him.
The man continued without anyone asking.
"My father served there. One night, news came that it had been attacked. No one came back."
The two Region Three soldiers lowered their eyes.
"When I reached the age to become a priest, no caravan left the Region without guards anymore. A few years later..." a bitter smile appeared on his face.
"Even guards were not enough."
"Every year, one less route, less trade, and more suffering."
"All this time, from when I was a child until now, we heard one thing; endure."
He paused.
"Preserve the remains, find the lost shrines, do not let the Light go out."
Then he raised his head and this time looked directly at Kain.
"Until the Child of Light comes."
Kain said nothing.
"Many people have heard this sentence their entire lives," the priest continued.
"Many died with it...my father was one of them. My teacher was one of them, many of the people who died here today also believed in the same thing."
His eyes moved toward the corpses of the people from Region Three for a moment.
"Endure."
He slowly let out his breath.
"But none of them saw this day."

This time even Kain could not use a joke to make the moment lighter, and his eyes stayed on the shrine as his thoughts returned to the Sphere Of Witness, the Tear it had absorbed, and even his Child of Light class.
For him, a few hours ago, this Sphere had been an incredible reward.
An Ancient-ranked artifact and a powerful tool, and that Tear was only something that had changed his talent and class and given him the chance to finally become a genius and prodigy.
That was all...

But for the man sitting in front of him, all of these things were something very different...even his own existence was the same, and proof that the expectations of several generations might not have been useless.
Kain slightly turned his face away, he did not feel comfortable, and for once, instead of hiding it behind a joke, he allowed the silence to remain.
Lian also said nothing, he had no idea about his friend’s inner struggles, but his mind was not idle either.
They now had several problems, first, Kain.
If what the priest said was true, he was no longer just one of Earth’s Awakened who had accidentally found an Ancient-ranked artifact.
The six Regions might simply send forces to kill him.
Second, the prophecy.
Region One knew something about Kain’s arrival, and apparently also knew about the person who would come with him, and there was a good chance that person was him.
Third...Region 3.
Going there could give them a huge amount of information.
But it could just as easily turn into willingly entering one of the strongest native fortresses.
Fourth...Lian himself.
He had obtained the Corrupted Sun and the Eclipse Core, fought a Level 50 Fallen, and seen short memories of a Demon.
The simple journey that had started only to see what was beyond the border of Base #9 had quickly gone out of control.
After some time in silence, the priest slightly straightened his body, the new respect in his eyes toward Kain was even a little strange to Lian.
"Anyway...Child of Light."
Kain immediately changed his expression, it was clear that he still did not like hearing this title.
"Now that we have found you, I cannot pretend this is only a chance meeting."
His eyes stopped on Lian for a moment, short but meaningful, and then returned to Kain.
"Do you want to come to Region Three?"
