chapters.title: Chapter 528: The Core Grows Stronger
paragraphs: "Do you want to come to Region Three?"
Kain did not answer immediately.
His eyes moved from the man’s face to Lian, with everything that had happened, making a decision was not easy.
Just an hour ago, the forces of Region Three had wanted to capture him.

The situation had changed too quickly, a few hours ago he was the "Tear Thief," and now the same people who had wanted to capture him alive were kneeling in front of him and calling him the Child of Light.
He put his hands on his waist.
"Let’s say we agree, how exactly are we going there? It took us six hours just to get here from the mountain pass, where exactly are the seven Regions? How many hours away are they from here?"
"It is two days away, and by sea," the priest answered without hesitation.
Kain slowly turned his head.

The black area that covered a large part of the city could still be seen in the distance, but it was no longer one solid area like a few hours ago and was slowly turning into vapor, even now a large part of it had already disappeared.
Parts of the black material had even gone down and revealed piles of stone and the burned ground beneath it.
And besides, he doubted that it was possible to sail through it.
"From...here?" he asked very quietly after that.
"No." The priest showed something like a smile.
Kain waited and the man continued.
"You’ll understand."
"That sentence was not reassuring at all."
"What should we do? Should we accept in the end or not?" He looked at his best friend again.
"From a security point of view, I have no problem with it, whenever I sleep I can leave this place, you haven’t forgotten, right? But if they capture you, you’ll be screwed," Lian answered calmly.
He could leave the Ruined Realm whenever he wanted.
"Ah...damn it, I completely forgot that you can freely travel in and out of the Ruined Realm...fuck."
"Anyway, I don’t think going there is a bad idea, we might be able to get answers to many questions there and find out what this prophecy is," the young Vorhelm added while ignoring his complaints.

Kain stayed silent for a few moments, it was true, they still had questions, and now that he knew he might be hunted by all six native Regions, it was not a bad idea to at least have one of them as support.
And in the end, they agreed to go there.
Lian looked at the huge body of the Eclipse Leviathan.
"I have something to do first."
"I thought we already took everything valuable from it." Kain followed the direction of his gaze.
"No."
He moved toward the body, something inside his body reacted a little more clearly with every step.
The Leviathan’s body was more than sixty meters long, and now that it was lying motionless on the broken dock, it looked even bigger.
A large part of the monster’s shell had been broken or fallen apart during the battle.
Under it, the thick gray skin of the sea monster was exposed, and the deep crack in its chest showed the empty space where the cores it had swallowed had been.
But his Eclipse Core pulsed again as he got closer to the body.
Thump.
[Eclipse Core-compatible remains detected.]
[Remaining active Essence can be extracted.]
[Start the absorption process?]
Lian only answered in his mind.
Yes.
One of the black veins that remained between the Leviathan’s dried flesh moved.
The vein separated from the tissue and rose from the creature’s body against gravity like a drop of thick ink, floating in the air.
A second vein came out from around the spine, and then a third.
Very soon, dozens of thin black veins came out from different parts of the sixty-meter-long Leviathan’s body, from the collapsed Mana paths, from under the armor plates, from the dried veins.
The two Region Three soldiers unconsciously took several steps back, and the priest also changed his expression, the scene he was seeing...looked demonic.
All the veins slowly moved toward Lian’s right hand, and when the first flow entered his palm, the Eclipse Core reacted.
This time there was no intense pain or memories of the Demon Of Eclipse, and the Essence directly entered a specific path and went into the Core.
The small black sphere inside it began to spin, and the veins inside it became brighter.
The Leviathan’s remaining Essence was compressed layer by layer inside the Core.
The process took almost a minute.
[Eclipse Essence successfully absorbed.]
[Eclipse Core stability increased.]
[Eclipse Energy storage capacity increased.]
[Eclipse Energy production increased.]
Lian felt the Core for a few moments, the difference from a few minutes ago was clear.
What he had just absorbed was Eclipse Essence, they were exactly the same veins that had been on the Sphere Of Witness, and he had built his first Core by absorbing them.
And now, by absorbing the ones inside the body of this monster, the Core had become larger, and its capacity to store Eclipse Energy had also increased.
And besides, the Core could produce more Eclipse Energy.
Lian kept his attention on the black sphere inside him for a moment.
This meant that if he encountered another creature in the future that possessed Eclipse Essence, killing it would not only give him normal resources, it could directly help his first Core grow.
And the largest amount of Eclipse Essence was in the hands of the Demon Of Eclipse.
Would the day ever come when he could find and hunt that Demon?
"Can you please tell me what the hell you just did? What was that damn demonic scene?" Kain asked after seeing the change in his expression.
Lian said nothing and Kain immediately understood and did not ask anything else.
First, his eyes moved over the huge body of the creature, despite removing the Core and Eclipse Essence, there was still a large amount of valuable material left.
Skin, bones, teeth, flesh, and the entire body of this Level 50 monster.
"Don’t you want anything from it?" He turned his head toward the Child of Light.
"From this?" Kain’s eyes stopped on the huge crack that had appeared between the Leviathan’s armor plates.
Under the monster’s natural armor, the thick gray skin was still intact.
Even after a battle where several Divine skills, the Midday Judgment, and Eclipse Energy had struck the creature’s body, a large part of it only had a few surface cuts.
He thought for a few moments and then said.
"Its skin."
"The skin?"
Kain nodded.
Lian nodded and the Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his right hand.
Ice came out from his forearm and turned into curved blades.
The Leviathan’s skin was so thick that an ordinary weapon would probably have a lot of trouble cutting it off, but the ice claw went into the flesh.
He carefully chose the path of the cut and removed one large and continuous piece for him.
A few minutes later, he removed the thick and heavy skin from the body, large enough to cover a large part of a room.
"Heavier than I thought." Kain touched it.
"Don’t worry, your storage space can’t complain."
"Fortunately."
The skin disappeared and the Child of Light placed it inside his storage space.
The young Vorhelm looked at the rest of the body again, this time his thoughts went directly to the Devouring Egg, he felt that the Egg would not be unhappy with this decision.
With one movement, he put the rest of the Leviathan’s body into his storage space.
The dock that had been sinking under the weight of the body only moments ago suddenly became empty.
When they returned to the priest, the man raised his hand without asking about the corpse.
A small object appeared in the palm of his hand.
Kain, who expected a map or something to help them find their way, stared at it for a few seconds.
It was a ship, or more accurately, a very small model of a ship, almost the size of a palm.
It had a thin white body, without sails or a mast, and very thin blue lines moved along both sides of it like flowing water.
"What is this?" Kain bent down to look at it

But his Eclipse Core pulsed again as he got closer to the body.
Thump.
[Eclipse Core-compatible remains detected.]
[Remaining active Essence can be extracted.]
[Start the absorption process?]
Lian only answered in his mind.
Yes.
One of the black veins that remained between the Leviathan’s dried flesh moved.
The vein separated from the tissue and rose from the creature’s body against gravity like a drop of thick ink, floating in the air.
A second vein came out from around the spine, and then a third.
Very soon, dozens of thin black veins came out from different parts of the sixty-meter-long Leviathan’s body, from the collapsed Mana paths, from under the armor plates, from the dried veins.
The two Region Three soldiers unconsciously took several steps back, and the priest also changed his expression, the scene he was seeing...looked demonic.
All the veins slowly moved toward Lian’s right hand, and when the first flow entered his palm, the Eclipse Core reacted.
This time there was no intense pain or memories of the Demon Of Eclipse, and the Essence directly entered a specific path and went into the Core.
The small black sphere inside it began to spin, and the veins inside it became brighter.
The Leviathan’s remaining Essence was compressed layer by layer inside the Core.
The process took almost a minute.
[Eclipse Essence successfully absorbed.]
[Eclipse Core stability increased.]
[Eclipse Energy storage capacity increased.]
[Eclipse Energy production increased.]
Lian felt the Core for a few moments, the difference from a few minutes ago was clear.
What he had just absorbed was Eclipse Essence, they were exactly the same veins that had been on the Sphere Of Witness, and he had built his first Core by absorbing them.
And now, by absorbing the ones inside the body of this monster, the Core had become larger, and its capacity to store Eclipse Energy had also increased.
And besides, the Core could produce more Eclipse Energy.
Lian kept his attention on the black sphere inside him for a moment.
This meant that if he encountered another creature in the future that possessed Eclipse Essence, killing it would not only give him normal resources, it could directly help his first Core grow.
And the largest amount of Eclipse Essence was in the hands of the Demon Of Eclipse.
Would the day ever come when he could find and hunt that Demon?
"Can you please tell me what the hell you just did?
What was that damn demonic scene?" Kain asked after seeing the change in his expression.
Lian said nothing and Kain immediately understood and did not ask anything else.
First, his eyes moved over the huge body of the creature, despite removing the Core and Eclipse Essence, there was still a large amount of valuable material left.
Skin, bones, teeth, flesh, and the entire body of this Level 50 monster.
"Don’t you want anything from it?" He turned his head toward the Child of Light.
"From this?" Kain’s eyes stopped on the huge crack that had appeared between the Leviathan’s armor plates.
Under the monster’s natural armor, the thick gray skin was still intact.
Even after a battle where several Divine skills, the Midday Judgment, and Eclipse Energy had struck the creature’s body, a large part of it only had a few surface cuts.
He thought for a few moments and then said.
"Its skin."
"The skin?"
Kain nodded.
Lian nodded and the Glacial Reaper Claw formed on his right hand.
Ice came out from his forearm and turned into curved blades.
The Leviathan’s skin was so thick that an ordinary weapon would probably have a lot of trouble cutting it off, but the ice claw went into the flesh.
He carefully chose the path of the cut and removed one large and continuous piece for him.
A few minutes later, he removed the thick and heavy skin from the body, large enough to cover a large part of a room.
"Heavier than I thought." Kain touched it.
"Don’t worry, your storage space can’t complain."
"Fortunately."
The skin disappeared and the Child of Light placed it inside his storage space.
The young Vorhelm looked at the rest of the body again, this time his thoughts went directly to the Devouring Egg, he felt that the Egg would not be unhappy with this decision.
With one movement, he put the rest of the Leviathan’s body into his storage space.
The dock that had been sinking under the weight of the body only moments ago suddenly became empty.
When they returned to the priest, the man raised his hand without asking about the corpse.
A small object appeared in the palm of his hand.
Kain, who expected a map or something to help them find their way, stared at it for a few seconds.
It was a ship, or more accurately, a very small model of a ship, almost the size of a palm.
It had a thin white body, without sails or a mast, and very thin blue lines moved along both sides of it like flowing water.
"What is this?" Kain bent down to look at it

chapters.title: Chapter 529: The Dream Voyager
paragraphs: The priest did not answer and threw the ship toward the empty space of the street.
The small object landed on the stone.
Click.
For a fraction of a second, nothing happened...then blue lines began to glow and white light came out from the entire body.
Kain unconsciously pulled his head back, and Lian also took a step back.
The ship began to grow, not by simply becoming bigger, but its real structure came out of the light layer by layer.
Its length went from the size of a palm to one meter in a single breath.
Three meters.
Five.
Ten.
The bottom of the ship opened into the air, the front part became longer, and white walls rose from both sides.
Lines of light on the surface of the body connected to each other in complex paths.
Twenty meters.
Thirty.
When its growth ended, a ship more than thirty meters long was standing in the middle of the ruined street of the city.
But what stopped Lian more than the change in its size was that it had not touched the ground.
The body remained floating about half a meter above the stone road.
"Here you go." The priest raised his healthy hand respectfully toward the deck.
Kain looked at the ship and then at Lian.
"I think this trip is getting stranger every hour."
He had no objection, even from close up, this thing did not look simple.
The Mana grooves on its body were so fine that some of them looked thinner than a strand of hair.
Before getting on, he turned his head toward Two.

The eight-eyed wolf was standing a few meters away, he had summoned him again so he could help scare these natives during the interrogation, but in the end, it was not needed, it was better for him to rest for the rest of the journey.
Two lowered his huge head slightly, as if he was saying goodbye.
His body turned into particles of light.
[Two has returned to the Colony House.]
Lian entered the ship after Kain, the two Region Three soldiers also followed them, and the priest was the last one.
The deck was simple compared to the size of the ship, there were no ropes, no sails, and not even a mast.
At the front, a half-transparent ring of light was floating in the air, and several Mana lines continued from it along the floor of the deck to the entire body.
Kain was still looking down and examining one of the grooves.
"What is this thing—"
The ship moved...for one moment it was still in the air, and the next...the ground of the city was ten meters below them.
"Damn it!" The Child of Light quickly grabbed the edge of the deck with his hand.
The ship quickly rose.
Twenty meters.
Fifty.
One hundred.
The wind hit their faces with force and pulled their clothes backward, the white and gray buildings of the City of Light below them became smaller.
The shrine stairs, the mirror towers, the black area that was collapsing, and the bodies of the soldiers from the two Regions, which were now only small spots from this height.
Kain moved to the wall and looked down, there was no fear on his face, instead...his excitement had almost become childish.
"It is really flying!"
Lian had one hand on the edge of the ship, the cold wind hit his face and pushed his hair backward.
Even he could not deny it...it was amazing.
The ship turned its front toward the mountain wall and the distance between them and the rocks quickly became smaller.
After a few seconds, Kain noticed that their direct path was leading exactly toward one of the highest parts of the mountain.
His eyes slowly moved toward the priest.
"I hope this thing knows what it’s doing."
"It does, Your Highness, don’t worry." The man was completely calm as he stood beside the ring of light.
The rocks came closer.
One hundred meters remained between them and the rocks...
Fifty meters.
Thirty meters.
Ten meters!
Kain tightened his fingers around the edge of the deck, and at the last moment, the front of the ship turned toward the sky.
Whoooosh!
A sudden pressure fell on their bodies, and the ship pulled up from the edge of the mountain at a sharp angle.
Gray rocks passed less than a few meters below the body.
Then there was nothing but the sky, thick clouds were in front of them, and the ship entered them without slowing down.
The world became white.

Cold moisture touched Lian’s face, he could not see more than a few meters, only the blue lines of the ship could be seen through the fog, and the sound of air passing around the body continued around them like a constant roar.
A few minutes later, they came out above the clouds.
Below them was a sea of clouds, the white clouds continued to the horizon, and the gray light of the sky spread across them.
The ship moved directly above it.
Kain walked from one side of the deck to the other, looked down, and then looked up.
"Okay. I admit it. This is probably the coolest thing I have ever seen."
"Your Sphere of Witness is going to get upset." Lian said.
Kain thought for a moment about the sphere he had stored inside his body.
"Second coolest thing."
Lian had not even had time to answer when the front of the ship went down.
"Why are we going down?" Kain was also surprised.
The angle became greater...much greater.
"Why are we going down this much?"
"It’s normal." The priest said calmly.
And at that moment, the ship fell, this time it was no longer like a controlled descent, instead, the body entered the clouds at high speed.
The wind pressure became so strong that Kain had to hold the wall with both hands.
Lian also pressed his palm firmly against the edge.
The clouds moved away and the scene below them suddenly became clear.
Blue and endless, it was a real sea, blue water continued to the horizon and shone under the light of the sky.
The ship was coming down toward the surface at a terrifying speed.
One hundred meters.
Fifty meters.
This time Kain said nothing, he only looked at the priest, the man was still calm.
Ten meters above the water, all the blue lines on the body lit up, and the shape of the lower part of the ship changed.
The body became wider, and the lines of light stretched from the front to the back, and then...SPLASH!
The ship landed on the water, two huge walls of water rose from both sides, and drops fell onto the deck like rain.
But its speed did not stop, the ship moved forward across the surface of the sea, and the water behind it turned into a white line of foam and waves.
The Child of Light did not say anything for a few seconds, as if he was trying to control his surprise.
Then, with a wet face and some of his hair stuck to his forehead, he looked at the priest.
"What the hell is this thing?!"
Lian was also waiting for an answer.
Even for him, creating something like this was far beyond something that could simply be called "useful.
The priest placed his hand on the control ring.
"The Dream Voyager, it is a transportation artifact."
"A transportation artifact that can fly?" Kain looked at the water below them again.
"For a short time, air travel uses several times more energy than moving on water.
"Usually, we only use the flying mode to cross mountains, valleys, or places where it is impossible to travel on the ground."
Lian looked at the water paths on the body, this limitation made sense.
If the vehicle could fly anywhere without a significant cost, building roads and using normal ships in this world would not make much sense.
"Of course, this ship can fly in every environment, it can even enter someone’s dreams, fly in the sky and on the seas, and move through deserts."
"Can we get one of these? Or is it something special?" Lian asked, this ship was an all-purpose vehicle, it was impossible not to be tempted by it.
"Under normal conditions, maybe, they are made to order, and as long as you pay the cost, they will make one for you." The priest let out a small sigh.
He paused.
"But their creators are from Region Seven, the followers of the Divine of Soul and Dream."
"And they have stopped trading with Region Three." Lian understood.
"For years." The man placed his hand on part of the wall.
"This one is old too. It has been repaired several times. If its main part is seriously damaged...I don’t think anyone in Region Three can fully repair it."
The young Vorhelm looked around the ship again, another question appeared in his mind.
"Do you know how they make things like this? Or is making artifacts like this considered the main specialty of Region Seven?"
The priest thought for a moment.
"I don’t know the exact method. But making artifacts is not only their work, the other Regions also have their own craftsmen."
Then he pointed at the floor of the ship with his hand.
"The difference with some of the craftsmen from Region Seven is their method of designing."
"What is the difference?" Kain came closer.
"Dreams."
"They can create the design of an artifact inside a dream, make a test version, destroy it, and try again from the beginning."
"Without using real materials?" Lian showed more interest.
"As long as it is only designing and testing, yes. Stronger craftsmen can even change the way they experience time inside some dreams."
"What does that mean?" Kain was genuinely interested this time.

"It means a craftsman may sleep at night and, from his own point of view, spend several weeks or even several months working on a design. Then, when he wakes up, he makes the version with the highest chance of success in the real world."
"That’s really cool." The Child of Light whispered.
Lian also slowly nodded, he agreed, even without direct combat power, such a profession had incredible value.
The ability to test hundreds of designs without wasting real materials, reducing mistakes, creating complex artifacts, and of course money.
Probably a lot of money.
He placed Region Seven one step higher on his list of places worth visiting someday.
After some time, the speed of the ship became stable.
The priest and one of the two soldiers went forward to control the route.
Kain stood beside the edge of the deck and only looked at the sea for a while.
For Lian, it was finally a chance to organize his panel, he sat beside the wall and opened his Status Panel.
The first thing that caught his attention was the reward from the Leviathan battle.
[Stat Points Received: 4,730.]
[Fragments Received: 9.]
Before the battle, he had 161 fragments.
Now.
[Fragments: 170.]
He lowered his eyes slightly, these numbers were not even the full reward from the battle.
Because Kain had directly participated in killing the Leviathan, his final share had unfortunately been cut in half.

chapters.title: Chapter 530 - 20,000 Stats Points!
paragraphs: Lian did not feel anything special about this.
If someone only looked at the final result, they might think that they had hunted down a Level 50 Fallen with fairly good speed.
The reality was very different.
Lian himself, with the Fallen Monster talent, created clear pressure on monsters and managed to suppress their power to some degree.
He had the World-Devourer Bastion, an Ancient armor that had saved his life many times.
He had a Core containing Essence belonging to a Demon-ranked being inside his body.
Two was with them, a Level 40 Fallen who was not even considered normal among Fallens.
One had helped to some degree, and more importantly, there was Kain.
Kain was not only a powerful Awakened himself, but the Sphere of Witness, an artifact belonging to one of the Seven Divines, had turned his attacks into something much more dangerous.
Midday Judgment and Light Echo alone had broken through a large part of the Leviathan’s final defense.
If a normal group of Awakeneds had entered the same battle instead of them, their first attack would probably have been the end of them.
Therefore, having the reward cut in half was fair.
He went to his Stats.
[Strength: 4,200.]
[Spirit: 2,900.]
[Resistance: 2,700.]
[Stat Points: 4,730.]
Lian thought for a few seconds and then started dividing them.
A familiar pressure formed inside his body.
This time, the change was not bigger than the increase before the battle, but reaching new levels in several Stats caused his body to become warm for a few seconds.
Power became denser in his muscles, his spiritual perception became clearer, and more Mana filled his pathways.
Then the final panel appeared.
[Remaining Stat Points: 1,086.]
He looked at the number twenty thousand for a few moments, he had expected his limit to be like this, so he was not too surprised.
"So I need to reach the second evolution sooner." Even so, this time he had reached his limit much earlier than he had expected.
The general rules about Stat limits were not a secret.
For someone with a five-star Class who had completed the first evolution, the limit at this stage was ten thousand.
After the second evolution, the capacity increased to fifty thousand, and the third evolution raised it to three hundred thousand.
Then there was a very large jump that many considered crazy.
The fourth evolution had a limit of five million.
That final number was so far beyond the reach of most Awakeneds that many did not even consider it a real "limit."
What did it matter how high the ceiling of a room was, when most people could not even climb halfway up its wall?
After passing the fifth evolution, common knowledge said that there was no longer a fixed limit for Stats.
But there was one small problem.
None of the Awakeneds who had actually passed all five evolutions had publicly confirmed this until now.
So maybe it was true.
Maybe it was not.
For now, Lian did not care, he had only just reached the twenty-thousand limit.
Five million was so far away that worrying about it would be stupid.

More importantly, the Stat limit did not mean the end of growth, not even close, even though he could no longer add Stats, he could at least raise his body and Soul to their peak through other methods.
Body Refinement.
And
Soul Refinement.
Both were very common among Awakeneds.
Warriors were more interested in Body Refinement.
Mages, healers, and those who had Soul or mental skills usually invested many resources into Soul Refinement.
The basic method was not complicated and the difficult part was the resources, both of these paths required absorbing very special resources in a very specific way.
In a sense, they had to bathe in the related resources.
And increasing the Strength Stat was not the same thing as Body Refinement.

Strength increased the output, the raw power of the muscles, striking power, lifting, pushing and pulling power, gripping and crushing power, the explosive acceleration of the body, and the force transferred from the legs to the waist and then to the arms, the power of jumping, and even the ability to maintain physical force when hitting something.
But if the body was not a suitable container for that power, a higher output did not always mean better performance.
Body Refinement changed the quality of the container itself, denser bones, stronger tendons and ligaments, muscles that could withstand more pressure without tearing.

Internal organs that were more resistant to impact and acceleration, better tissue recovery, more durable Mana channels inside the body, and most importantly, a body that could transfer its existing power better without damaging itself.
If the Strength Stat showed how much power the engine could produce, Body Refinement showed how much that power the frame, axles, and body could withstand.
Lian already had a big advantage in this area.
The Fallen Monster talent had greatly strengthened the structure of his body, bones, and tissues after the first evolution.
But this did not mean the end of the path.
Suitable Refinement resources could push even that monster-like body one step further.
Spirit also had a similar difference from Soul Refinement, increasing Spirit raised Soul defense, made perception more accurate, and increased the speed of processing information and concentration.
It improved mental clarity, reasoning ability, resistance against mental pressure, and control over skills.
The higher Spirit became, the easier it also became to control complex Mana structures.
Soul Refinement?

It changed the quality of the Soul itself, its stability, density, resistance against Soul damage, resistance against erosion, corruption, and direct attacks on one’s existence, faster recovery after Soul exhaustion.

It increased the ability to endure long-term use of skills whose pressure was transferred to the mind and Soul, and even created a better connection between the mind, Soul, and the individual’s skills.
In a way, they worked as complements to each other instead of being separate.
He took his eyes away from the panel.
So the twenty-thousand limit was only one of the walls.
He still had 1,086 Stat Points that he could use after his next evolution, and until then, there were still many other ways to become stronger.
[Fragments: 170.]
For some time, Lian had almost ignored two skills, not because they were useless, but because compared to his new abilities, they had fallen too far behind.
Grave Fang — Normal.
And
False Presence — Normal.
Grave Fang had been used many times to briefly capture a target or restrict a limb, but its Normal rank now had too many limitations against stronger enemies.
False Presence could only create a fake presence, which was enough against weaker enemies, but now that his enemies were this strong, it was ridiculous.
He focused on Grave Fang first.
[Direct upgrade to Divine rank detected with the use of 93 Fragments.]
[Do you wish to continue?]
Yes.
[Eternal Grave Maw.]
[Rank: Divine.]
[The user can create a maximum of ten Maws at the same time in visible locations.]
[The Maws can restrain physical targets and Mana and Soul structures.]
[The closing and restraining power increases based on the Spirit and Mana consumed.]
[After fully closing, the flow of Mana in the trapped area will be put under pressure.]
[Targets with a large difference in power can break the Maws.]

[Remaining Fragments: 77.]
[False Presence.]
[Direct upgrade with the use of all remaining Fragments detected.]
He continued anyway.
[Myriad Presence Mirage.]
[Rank: Divine.]
[The user can create several moving fake presences.]
[Each presence can perfectly imitate the user’s Mana signature, presence pressure, voice, and movement pattern.]
[The presences can move independently within the control range of the skill.]
[Current simultaneous control limit: 10 presences.]
[The combined intensity of the fake presences cannot exceed the capacity of the user’s real presence.]
[The presences are fake and cannot cause physical damage.]
[Five presences can transfer their perception to the original owner.]
[The user can also create up to one thousand fake presences, but they will only be mirages and illusions and have no abilities, and they will not even have the signatures related to the user.]
[Fragments: 0.]
Lian remained silent for a few seconds.
Five moving presences could work extremely well, especially since they were now completely identical to him and there was no difference between them.
As long as the enemy did not touch them, identifying them would be impossible, and they could be used as a surprise element or to deceive enemies.
Creating one thousand fake presences could also work very well for confusing enemies.
Then he wanted to look at One’s status, but the notification appeared first.
[The first evolution process of the special member One has been completed.]
[Do you want to see the result?]

sentences.text: Lian did not feel anything special about this.
If someone only looked at the final result, they might think that they had hunted down a Level 50 Fallen with fairly good speed.
The reality was very different.
Lian himself, with the Fallen Monster talent, created clear pressure on monsters and managed to suppress their power to some degree.
He had the World-Devourer Bastion, an Ancient armor that had saved his life many times.
He had a Core containing Essence belonging to a Demon-ranked being inside his body.
Two was with them, a Level 40 Fallen who was not even considered normal among Fallens.
One had helped to some degree, and more importantly, there was Kain.
Kain was not only a powerful Awakened himself, but the Sphere of Witness, an artifact belonging to one of the Seven Divines, had turned his attacks into something much more dangerous.
Midday Judgment and Light Echo alone had broken through a large part of the Leviathan’s final defense.
If a normal group of Awakeneds had entered the same battle instead of them, their first attack would probably have been the end of them.
Therefore, having the reward cut in half was fair.
He went to his Stats.
[Strength: 4,200.]

[Resistance: 2,700.]

Lian thought for a few seconds and then started dividing them.
A familiar pressure formed inside his body.

Power became denser in his muscles, his spiritual perception became clearer, and more Mana filled his pathways.

[Remaining Stat Points: 1,086.]
He looked at the number twenty thousand for a few moments, he had expected his limit to be like this, so he was not too surprised.
"So I need to reach the second evolution sooner." Even so, this time he had reached his limit much earlier than he had expected.
The general rules about Stat limits were not a secret.
For someone with a five-star Class who had completed the first evolution, the limit at this stage was ten thousand.
After the second evolution, the capacity increased to fifty thousand, and the third evolution raised it to three hundred thousand.
Then there was a very large jump that many considered crazy.
The fourth evolution had a limit of five million.
That final number was so far beyond the reach of most Awakeneds that many did not even consider it a real "limit."
What did it matter how high the ceiling of a room was, when most people could not even climb halfway up its wall?
After passing the fifth evolution, common knowledge said that there was no longer a fixed limit for Stats.
But there was one small problem.
None of the Awakeneds who had actually passed all five evolutions had publicly confirmed this until now.
So maybe it was true.
Maybe it was not.
For now, Lian did not care, he had only just reached the twenty-thousand limit.
Five million was so far away that worrying about it would be stupid.

More importantly, the Stat limit did not mean the end of growth, not even close, even though he could no longer add Stats, he could at least raise his body and Soul to their peak through other methods.
Body Refinement.
And
Soul Refinement.
Both were very common among Awakeneds.
Warriors were more interested in Body Refinement.
Mages, healers, and those who had Soul or mental skills usually invested many resources into Soul Refinement.
The basic method was not complicated and the difficult part was the resources, both of these paths required absorbing very special resources in a very specific way.
In a sense, they had to bathe in the related resources.
And increasing the Strength Stat was not the same thing as Body Refinement.

Strength increased the output, the raw power of the muscles, striking power, lifting, pushing and pulling power, gripping and crushing power, the explosive acceleration of the body, and the force transferred from the legs to the waist and then to the arms, the power of jumping, and even the ability to maintain physical force when hitting something.
But if the body was not a suitable container for that power, a higher output did not always mean better performance.
Body Refinement changed the quality of the container itself, denser bones, stronger tendons and ligaments, muscles that could withstand more pressure without tearing.

Internal organs that were more resistant to impact and acceleration, better tissue recovery, more durable Mana channels inside the body, and most importantly, a body that could transfer its existing power better without damaging itself.
If the Strength Stat showed how much power the engine could produce, Body Refinement showed how much that power the frame, axles, and body could withstand.
Lian already had a big advantage in this area.
The Fallen Monster talent had greatly strengthened the structure of his body, bones, and tissues after the first evolution.
But this did not mean the end of the path.
Suitable Refinement resources could push even that monster-like body one step further.
Spirit also had a similar difference from Soul Refinement, increasing Spirit raised Soul defense, made perception more accurate, and increased the speed of processing information and concentration.
It improved mental clarity, reasoning ability, resistance against mental pressure, and control over skills.
The higher Spirit became, the easier it also became to control complex Mana structures.
Soul Refinement?

It increased the ability to endure long-term use of skills whose pressure was transferred to the mind and Soul, and even created a better connection between the mind, Soul, and the individual’s skills.
In a way, they worked as complements to each other instead of being separate.

chapters.title: Chapter 531: The Ant Of Ruins
paragraphs: [The first evolution process of the special member has been completed.]
[One.]
[Level: 20.]
[First Evolution: Complete.]
The corner of Lian’s lips rose slightly.
Finally.
But the message was not finished.
[An abnormal phenomenon has been detected.]
Lian paid more attention.
[The original species belonged to the Normal rank.]
[Under normal conditions, the evolution of a Normal monster does not cause an increase in its original rank.]
This was not new to him, evolution and rank were two separate things.
A Normal monster could evolve, its body could change, it could gain new skills, its growth limit could increase, but it would still remain Normal.
Changing from Normal to Fallen was not something that happened just by going through "one evolution."
Rank advancement was a much rarer phenomenon, in fact, it was extremely unusual and extremely rare for it to happen.
But the next notification showed the reason for this exception.
[The special member link of the Colony Sovereign has been detected.]
[Evolution saturation has exceeded the required limit.]
[The quality of the consumed resources is much higher than the basic requirement.]
[Last absorbed Core: Fallen — Level 50.]
[Rank advancement conditions have been met.]
[Rank increased.]
[Normal ← Fallen.]
He looked at the text for a few seconds, this part was much more important than the change in One’s appearance.
Until now, the Colony Sovereign had mostly meant a way for him to create a colony, create links, create special members, and borrow part of their power.

But if this same link had been able to change the evolution path of one of his special members enough to cause a rank advancement, then did this mean that one day all five special members of his colony could become Supreme?
Even thinking about it was crazy, having five Supreme monsters as his subordinates!
Supremes were monsters that were almost described as god-like.

He had already faced powerful beings such as Calamities, but it should not be forgotten that these Calamities did not have combat power themselves, they were conceptual beings that had the power to start the apocalypse in worlds.
They themselves did not have combat power, at least Black Silence was not like that, and they even needed an Anchor and a Vessel, and those two things were already major limitations for them.
But Supremes were not like that, they themselves had the power to destroy a world, he really wanted to know where the world these monsters and apocalyptic concepts came from was.
And did a hierarchy exist there?
If so, where did Supremes and Calamities stand in that hierarchy?
And what about the being that the Calamities called Father?
In any case, this was not something he had an answer for right now, and One’s rank advancement was not free either.
If One had only absorbed the minimum Cores required, this probably would not have happened.
His saturation had remained at a high level for a long time, he had consumed far more resources than necessary.
And his last Core also belonged to a Level 50 Fallen with Corrupted Light.
The Colony Sovereign had made the path possible, but the giant ant had filled that path with its resources.
[Evolved Species: Ant Of Ruin.]
[New Talent acquired.]
[Heir of Ruin — Rank S.]
[Compatibility with forces of destruction and collapse has greatly increased.]
[Ability to use Ruin Energy.]
[Ability to destroy structures, objects, and living beings and completely collapse them from the inside using Ruin Energy.]
[Ability to use Ruin Energy directly in attacks like an Element.]
Lian was satisfied.
More than satisfied.
This path fit One perfectly.
Two was a monster that could break the normal logic of battle and could use the Eight Disasters and provide incredible help in changing the situation.
But One now?
He could directly act like a heavy fighter and destroy anything in his path with all his power.
And if he was not mistaken, Ruin Energy should be something similar to Destruction power.
Kain noticed the expression on his face.
"What happened?"
"One finished his evolution."
"Bring him out." The Child of Light immediately moved away from the edge of the deck.
Lian looked at the floor of the ship and then at his friend.
"You want him to put a hole in the ship?"
Kain remained silent for a few seconds.
"How big did he become?"
"I haven’t seen him yet."
"Then he might not put a hole in it."
"He might."
"Fine. But summon him as soon as we arrive." Kain turned forward with an unhappy expression.
This time Lian did not object, he also wanted to see the result and had no doubt that it would be far beyond his expectations.
It took almost three days to reach their destination, they spent this time enjoying the journey.
Of course, they also encountered sea monsters several times, but Lian and Kain both dealt with them easily.
"We have arrived."
Both of them went to the front of the deck, but there was still nothing but the sea in front of them, blue water continued to the horizon and no land could be seen.
"Arrived where?" Kain looked at the priest.
"There." The man pointed toward the horizon.
At first, Lian saw nothing.
Then he noticed a very thin line of light, as the ship got closer, the line became larger, and ten minutes later it became clear that it was not a line at all...it was a curtain.
A wall of light that started from the surface of the sea and went so high that its end disappeared into the sky.
The light on its surface moved like a curtain in the wind.
The ship did not slow down.
"We’re not going to hit that, right?" Kain looked at it for a few seconds.
The priest did not even turn around.
"No."
"Good."
The distance became smaller.
One hundred meters.
Fifty.
The Child of Light unconsciously placed one hand on the wall, and the ship entered the light directly.
For one second, the world disappeared.
There was no sound and not even wind, the sound of the moving water could no longer be heard either.
Then the colors returned.
Lian remained truly silent for a few seconds, the sea on the other side of the curtain was not the same sea, the water was clearer.
The sky above them, unlike the dead sky that always covered a large part of the Ruined Realm, was bright blue, and groups of white clouds moved calmly across it.
Land could be seen on the horizon, it was completely green.
Farming terraces rose along the gentle slopes, trees grew in neat rows beside water channels.
White towers could be seen between the buildings, and wide waterways came from inside the city toward the sea.
Small ships moved across the water, and birds flew in the sky.
Kain looked at the scene without saying anything, Lian did the same.
What caught his attention more than the towers was the smoke.
A thin column of gray smoke rose from among the buildings near the coast, then a very weak smell reached them with the wind.
Bread.
People were moving along the coast.
Workers were carrying goods.
Fishermen were collecting their nets.
Several children were running on a small pier.
The sound of conversations, laughter, and cart wheels could be heard.
Seeing life in a world that was supposed to be destroyed was truly strange.
This Region had not only survived, it was living, it had no difference from a prosperous and happy civilization, at least from their point of view.
The priest gave them a short look, he probably knew their reaction.
"Welcome to Region Three."
The ship moved toward the main port.
At a close distance, the city was larger than what they had seen from the sea.
White and cream-colored buildings with several floors had been built along the coastal slope.
Most of the roofs were bright and curved, and narrow water channels passed through the streets.
Tall towers stood in different parts of the city, but they did not have the dead and heavy feeling of the Silent Light city.
When the Dream Voyager entered the port, several guards were already standing near the docking area.
The ship’s own seal and the priest’s presence were probably enough to show their identity, but the ordinary people still did not know what had happened.
The ship could not become smaller until everyone got off, a narrow bridge of light formed from the deck to the dock.
The priest went down first.
Several people immediately came toward him, the expressions on their faces changed when they saw his injuries.
The two remaining soldiers went down after him.
A murmur spread through the crowd and everyone wondered where the others were.
Then Kain stepped onto the bridge, and Lian was right behind him.
The moment Kain’s foot touched the white stone of the dock, a very faint light came out of his chest.
He stopped himself.
"I didn’t do anything."
A white point came out of his body.
The Sphere Of Witness appeared beside his shoulder and silently glowed.
For two seconds, nothing happened...then the sound of something falling onto stone was heard.
Clack.
An old priest several dozen meters away had dropped the container he was carrying.
A woman covered her mouth with her hand, and a young boy standing beside some fish boxes stared at the sphere with his mouth open.
"The Sphere Of Witness..." someone whispered.
"Impossible." Someone else answered.
The murmur moved through the port like a wave.
"Is that really it?"
"Did we...really get the Divine of Light’s artifact back?"
"But...who is he?"
"Why does he have the Divine’s artifact? Why doesn’t the priest have it?"
The priest looked at the crowd, as if he had expected their reactions, he did not even try to hide anything and announced loudly.
"The Child of Light has finally appeared!"
For a moment, a suffocating silence covered the entire crowd, as if they could not easily understand those words.
An old woman fell to her knees.
A man beside her was still standing and only stared.
Someone cried.
Several people brought their hands together in front of their chests.
Some did not move at all.
And some clearly did not believe it.
An old man sitting on a box beside the dock leaned forward, narrowed his eyes, and then said in a voice that was quiet to himself but reached Kain.
"That kid? Impossible!"
The corner of Lian’s mouth rose slightly, he had expected that not everyone would immediately believe it.
But the priest ignored everyone and turned toward the guards.
"Open the way."
The respect in the guards’ behavior toward Kain was now obvious, but fear and confusion were also mixed with it.
A huge piece of news had entered the port, and the people still did not know what they should do with it, had their savior really appeared?
They had not even entered the main part of the city when Kain stopped, on the left side of the port, there was a relatively open square between the coastal warehouses.
His eyes moved toward Lian.
"At least now there is no ship to put a hole in."
Lian knew what he meant, and he also no longer intended to wait.
It was time to summon One.

chapters.title: Chapter 532: Six Regions Want to Kill Kain
paragraphs: After moving away from the crowd, Kain returned the Sphere Of Witness into his soul, he had no idea why this thing had suddenly come out.
But as far as he knew, this artifact had a consciousness of its own and it was possible for it to show such behavior.
He looked around and, after seeing that there were no longer ordinary people around them, he looked at Lian.
"Now is the time to summon it!"
"Here?" Lian raised an eyebrow, they were following the priest, and it was a little crazy to suddenly do something like this.
"It doesn’t matter, they can wait for a few minutes, besides, I want them to be a little more afraid of us after seeing the Godly Emperor Of All Ants."
"I can understand your intention, but what is that stupid title you gave my ant?"
Kain ignored him and simply waited for One to be summoned.
Lian also said nothing more and summoned the Ant Of Ruin.

Particles of Light gathered in the middle of the square.
Several guards immediately put their hands on their weapons.
A huge creature formed from the particles.
Its body was more than ten meters long and its shoulders were several meters high.
Six long and powerful legs came out from both sides of its body, each one covered with thick black plates that looked more like the armor of a war monster than the body of an insect.
Every step it took seemed as if it could shake the ground.
Its sharp claws were buried in the stone, and it was clear that they would leave deep marks on the ground when it moved.
Its main body was made of several huge sections, and its entire surface was covered with black armor plates.
Deep cracks could be seen on some of the plates, and through those cracks, thick black energy flowed through the creature like blood through veins.
Ruin Energy.
Its head alone was almost as large as a human.
Two long and thick antennae came out from the top of its head and slowly moved through the air, as if they were checking everything around it.
But the most terrifying part of its body was its jaws.
Two huge jaws came out from both sides of its mouth, and each one had several rows of black and sharp teeth.
When the jaws slowly came together, a metallic sound spread through the air.
Several large black plates like the broken blades of a huge armor were placed on its back.
An aura of Ruin Energy moved around its body, the stones near its feet cracked and broke apart without even being touched.
Even the Mana in the air became unstable near it.
This was no longer a giant ant.
Its appearance looked more like a creature that had stepped out of the apocalypse, as if Ruin itself had taken form, grown six legs, and stepped forward to devour what remained of the world.
Two pack animals tied to a cart several dozen meters away pulled back in fear.
One of them neighed and pulled at its reins, and the guards half-drew their weapons.
"W-What... what kind of monster is that?"
The guard’s voice was shaking, and his fingers were trembling so badly that the spear in his hand was shaking.
Another one instinctively took several steps back.
"Just... just don’t let it look at us..."
At that moment, One’s huge head turned toward them, its gaze fixed on the guards.
The color drained from their faces.
One of them held his breath and his knees began to shake.
"D-Don’t... move..."
His voice could barely be heard.
"Just... don’t move..."
The guards who were supposed to protect the priest were so terrified that they almost fell to the ground.
"Calm down! It is with them!" The priest immediately raised his hand.
Kain paid no attention to the guards and walked around One a few times.
The head.
The legs.
The armor.
The jaws.
He was truly silent for a few seconds, and then he stopped.
"Okay... the name I gave him really isn’t good."
He paused for a moment, as if he was thinking about what name he should use for him from now on.
"I got it! From now on, I should call him The Eternal Abyssal Sovereign Of Ants!"
Lian completely ignored his friend and looked at One, and the ant also turned its antennae toward its master.
Lian completely ignored his friend and looked at One.
The ant immediately turned its antennae toward its master as well.
A feeling of satisfaction and happiness was sent to Lian through the bond.
There was no pride in One’s feelings.
There was only sincere and pure happiness and satisfaction.
One felt that now he could help his master again.
He no longer had to just watch him from far away.
Now he could once again stand beside his master in every battle, just like before.
This was all he wanted.
The only thing he wanted was to stay beside his master so he could protect him under any circumstances.
He only...
didn’t want to be thrown away.

He could understand all the feelings of his Colony member through the bond.
"One, you are the first member of my Colony." He said in a calm voice.
"You are the one who stayed beside me during the worst and most dangerous days of my life, when everyone had given up on me, you still stood beside me."
"I will never forget how you always tried to protect me."
Lian remembered how One had tried to save him in the Special Area.

Even when the Black Silence had taken control of his body, One had still stayed beside him, at that time, everyone had come to the conclusion that he was dead and they wanted to actually destroy his body.
But One? He still only wanted to save him.
In many other situations as well, this ant had always stood beside him.
"I will never forget your help." Young Vorhelm smiled slightly.
"And you will always remain the most precious member of my Colony to me." Then he looked seriously into the ant’s eyes.
"So never think again that I am going to throw you away, okay?"
One stayed silent for a moment, then he suddenly opened his huge mouth and stuck out his tongue.
Lick!
Lian’s entire body became wet in an instant.
A warm feeling and satisfaction were sent through the bond again, he simply declared that he would stay beside his master forever and continue serving him.
Lian looked at his wet clothes and face and laughed.
"Heh, bad boy."
Then he placed his hand on One’s head again and began to stroke the ant with a smile.
"For now, go back."
One turned into particles of Light without resisting.
Entering the center of the city with a huge Fallen, especially on the same day that half of the port had believed that Kain was someone from the prophecy, probably would not help calm things down.
One of the port officials, who was wearing a formal white and gray uniform, stepped forward.
"Your accommodation will be prepared. The Lord is still in a meeting, but as soon as he has free time, he will meet with you."
The guest accommodation was located in a higher part of the city.
On the way, Lian had more time to see the Region closely, the water canals really passed through the streets.
Some houses had small gardens.
People still stopped when Kain passed by, the news had moved faster than they had.
On every street, more people knew about it, but the reactions were still different.
Respect.
Curiosity.
Crying.
Disbelief.
And looks that saw Kain not as a young man, but as something they had heard about for years.
The Child of Light became quieter the farther he went.
When they finally entered the accommodation, the first thing he did was throw himself onto one of the chairs.
The priest also sat on the chair opposite him.
"Who exactly is this Lord we are waiting for?" Lian looked at the old man and asked.
"Lord Orlian Veyra. The current ruler of Region Three." The priest answered.
"Something like a king?"
"Not exactly."
"Old families have influence, and the Priest Council also has influence over many decisions, but the Lord is the highest executive authority in the Region."
"He is also in charge of the main defense of the Region. He has the central seal of the shelter, and some of the old arrays can only be activated with his permission."
"So he basically has a lot of power." Kain added.
"A lot, but not absolute power."
The priest paused for a moment.

"In normal matters, the council and the families can stand against him. But war, official relations with other Regions, opening closed archives, high-rank artifacts of our Divine, and old agreements... he has the final say there."
"How is this Lord chosen?" Young Vorhelm asked with interest, he wanted to see whether the ruling system here was a democracy or a dictatorship.
"The candidates are trained from childhood, but the final choice is made by the Divine of Light."
"Oh? How does it choose? Is there some kind of ritual, or does it simply announce it directly?" He became even more curious, was it possible that these natives had a way to speak with the gods?
"It is some kind of trial, all the candidates take part in it, and the winner is chosen as the Lord."
Lian sighed, what a shame.
After the old man explained a few things to them, he left, apparently he had to go and give his report.
It was expected.
Just a few days ago, a large part of Region Three’s forces had been killed in Silent Light.
The forces of Region Six had attacked their operation.
The ancient shrine had been opened, and the Sphere Of Witness had found a new owner after centuries.
The Child of Light, if the priest’s test was correct, had really appeared.
And that Child of Light was a foreigner.
Each of these pieces of news alone was enough to keep the leaders of a Region inside a meeting room for hours.
And before leaving, the priest told them one more thing, it probably would not take long before the other six Regions learned about the appearance of the Child of Light.
They might have already learned something even now, but Region Three would do everything it could to buy as much time as possible.
And this was not good news at all, at least Lian might be able to hide his identity, but Kain would definitely become the target of all six Regions sooner or later.
Time passed.
Near sunset, a pale golden color settled over the white towers of the Region.
From the balcony of the accommodation, a large part of the city could be seen, lights turned on one after another, and the green fields farther away were quiet under the last light of the day.
The water canals reflected the light of the sky, and the sounds of life could still be heard from the streets.
For a while, neither of them said anything.
Kain stood beside the railing, his elbows resting on the stone and his eyes fixed on the city.
"We were just passing the border of Base #9 for fun, and now we are involved in something like this." He then spoke calmly.
"It was your decision." Lian was sitting on a chair inside the room.
Kain turned around.
"You came too."
"I said it was your decision, not that I stopped you."
"Sometimes I think being your best friend must be some kind of disease, how are you this relaxed? We are going to be hunted by six civilizations!"
"Please don’t include me in that, you are the one who is going to be hunted, I still have many things to deal with and I don’t have time to deal with this one." Lian corrected him.
Kain was about to answer.
Knock. Knock.
The sound of someone knocking on the door came, and both of them turned their eyes toward it.
The door did not open.
The priest’s voice came from behind it, and this time his tone was more formal than before.
"Child of Light and his companion, Lord Orlian is ready to meet you."
( Ant Visualization )

chapters.title: Chapter 533: The Prophecy
paragraphs: "Lord Orlian is ready to see you." The priest’s voice came from behind the door.
Kain stood beside the balcony for a few seconds, looking at the bright city below.
Then he let out a short sigh and stepped away from the railing.
"Finally."
The door opened.
The priest who had accompanied them from Silent Light this time wore clean clothes.
He lowered his head respectfully.
"This way, Child of Light and your respected companion."
Kain frowned for a moment, he still was not used to that title, it would probably take some time.
Lian also stood up and followed them.
The main headquarters of the ruler of Region Three was not built at the highest part of the city.
He had expected the building where the ruler of one of the Seven Regions lived to be something like a huge castle, but the building in front of them looked more like a military temple.
White stone with tall pillars and narrow windows where the evening light entered through them.
There was very little gold in the architecture, and even that small amount was mostly used in the Mana grooves of the walls and religious symbols instead of decoration.
There was no giant statue of the Lord, and no expensive carpet covered the entire path.
But this simplicity made the building look older and heavier.
Guards stood on both sides of the path.
There were not many of them, but the pressure of their presence was different from the ordinary soldiers at the port.
The main doors of the hall opened for them.
Light entered through the tall windows, and more interestingly, even though it was already evening, there was still natural light inside.
The hall was more than forty meters long, and its floor was made of a bright stone with very thin golden lines flowing inside it.
At the end of the hall, there was no high platform, only a few steps and a stone chair with a short back.
A man was standing in front of it.
His hair was white with a slight golden color and reached close to his neck.
His face looked around forty-something, not young, but not old either.
His clothes were simpler than what the two of them had probably expected.
A white robe with faint golden lines, there was no crown on his head, but his presence made it clear that no one needed a crown to understand his position.
Lord Orlian Veyra.
On his right stood a young girl.
Her light golden hair reached her shoulders, and unlike her father’s formal clothes, she wore a shorter and more practical robe.
A small sun symbol was placed on her collar, and her hands were behind her back.
She did not look older than nineteen or twenty, her eyes first fell on Kain and then on Lian.
And unlike the curious looks of the people at the port, hers was colder, there was no clear hostility, but there was no warmth either.
Orlian stepped forward.
His eyes stayed on the Sphere of Witness inside Kain for a few seconds, as if he knew it was there even without seeing it.
"Three generations of my family have been waiting for this meeting."
His voice was calm, but it spread across the entire hall without needing to become louder.
"It was strange that when it finally happened, you were younger than everyone had imagined and that you are a foreigner."
"Today is the second time someone has been disappointed about where I was born."
Kain looked at him for a few seconds and then let out a short sigh.
The corner of Orlian’s mouth rose slightly.
"Not disappointed...just surprised, anyway, it is a pleasure to meet you, Child of Light."
His eyes moved away from Kain for a moment and stopped on Lian, staying there slightly longer than normal.
Lian noticed it, and this was not the first time.
From the moment they had entered the hall, the ruler of Region Three had looked at him several times, not with simple curiosity, as if he was examining something.
He said nothing.
"Elara."
Orlian moved his hand slightly.
The young girl lowered her head.
"Elara Veyra."
"My youngest daughter."
"Welcome, Child of Light."
Elara kept her eyes on Kain, her voice was respectful, but when her eyes moved to Lian for a moment, she only lowered her head slightly.
"And you."
"Thank you."
The young Vorhelm nodded.
Orlian invited them to come closer.
The priest accompanying them gave a short report and then, with the Lord’s permission, left the hall with the guards.
The first few minutes were mostly spent explaining what had happened in Silent Light.

Orlian had already received the main report, but he also heard the details about the presence of Region Six, the opening of the sanctuary, the Eclipse Leviathan, and the number of deaths directly from them.
When Kain explained that the Sphere of Witness had accepted the bond with him by itself, Orlian did not ask any more questions.
He did not ask for any test and did not bring another seal, for him, the matter was already settled, and he seemed to believe it.
The Lord treated both of them with respect, but perhaps because of the difference in age or power, he still did not show them the same extreme respect that the priest had shown them.
But toward Lian, besides respect, there was a kind of caution and perhaps even fear in his behavior...?
It could be felt as if he was afraid of Lian.
In the end, Kain asked the same question that was the main reason for this meeting.
"So can I finally find out what is written in that prophecy?"
Orlian looked at him, the small smile from before disappeared from his face.
For a few seconds, no one spoke, and then the Lord slightly turned his head toward the doors.
"Everyone out."
The guards moved without asking questions, the two huge doors closed.
The sound of them closing echoed through the hall.
When Orlian started speaking, his tone no longer sounded like a ruler explaining politics.
It had become quieter and heavier, like someone saying words he had heard many times by heart and knew that every one of them had been preserved through generations.
"This is how the prophecy begins."
Light moved across the golden lines on the floor.
"When the Tear recognizes its owner and the Witness awakens after a long silence, the Child of Light will descend."
"Six shelters will rise in fear of the Third, because the Light will not walk alone."
"Beside him, the Dormant Calamity will walk; nameless in the Father’s records and without chains in the threads of fate."
Even Lian could not simply let the sentence pass through his mind.
Nameless in the Father’s records.
There was something unpleasant about this phrase, especially the word Father, it reminded him of that same Father who commanded all five Calamities.
But what did this sentence mean now?
Orlian had not finished yet.
"The Calamity will not come with one face; what exists within the souls of monsters will echo within him after their fall."
The young Vorhelm’s fingers curled very slightly, he had a very strange feeling that this sentence was referring to his three Innate Skills.
"When the heart becomes complete and the Dormant Calamity stands at the edge of the end, universe will either break free from his chains..."
His tone stopped for a moment and then continued more quietly.
"...or no living will see the next dawn."

From the moment they had entered the hall, the ruler of Region Three had looked at him several times, not with simple curiosity, as if he was examining something.
He said nothing.
"Elara."
Orlian moved his hand slightly.
The young girl lowered her head.
"Elara Veyra."
"My youngest daughter."
"Welcome, Child of Light."
Elara kept her eyes on Kain, her voice was respectful, but when her eyes moved to Lian for a moment, she only lowered her head slightly.
"And you."
"Thank you."
The young Vorhelm nodded.
Orlian invited them to come closer.
The priest accompanying them gave a short report and then, with the Lord’s permission, left the hall with the guards.
The first few minutes were mostly spent explaining what had happened in Silent Light.

Orlian had already received the main report, but he also heard the details about the presence of Region Six, the opening of the sanctuary, the Eclipse Leviathan, and the number of deaths directly from them.
When Kain explained that the Sphere of Witness had accepted the bond with him by itself, Orlian did not ask any more questions.
He did not ask for any test and did not bring another seal, for him, the matter was already settled, and he seemed to believe it.
The Lord treated both of them with respect, but perhaps because of the difference in age or power, he still did not show them the same extreme respect that the priest had shown them.
But toward Lian, besides respect, there was a kind of caution and perhaps even fear in his behavior...?
It could be felt as if he was afraid of Lian.
In the end, Kain asked the same question that was the main reason for this meeting.
"So can I finally find out what is written in that prophecy?"
Orlian looked at him, the small smile from before disappeared from his face.
For a few seconds, no one spoke, and then the Lord slightly turned his head toward the doors.
"Everyone out."
The guards moved without asking questions, the two huge doors closed.
The sound of them closing echoed through the hall.
When Orlian started speaking, his tone no longer sounded like a ruler explaining politics.
It had become quieter and heavier, like someone saying words he had heard many times by heart and knew that every one of them had been preserved through generations.
"This is how the prophecy begins."
Light moved across the golden lines on the floor.
"When the Tear recognizes its owner and the Witness awakens after a long silence, the Child of Light will descend."
"Six shelters will rise in fear of the Third, because the Light will not walk alone."
"Beside him, the Dormant Calamity will walk; nameless in the Father’s records and without chains in the threads of fate."
Even Lian could not simply let the sentence pass through his mind.
Nameless in the Father’s records.
There was something unpleasant about this phrase, especially the word Father, it reminded him of that same Father who commanded all five Calamities.
But what did this sentence mean now?
Orlian had not finished yet.
"The Calamity will not come with one face; what exists within the souls of monsters will echo within him after their fall."
The young Vorhelm’s fingers curled very slightly, he had a very strange feeling that this sentence was referring to his three Innate Skills.
"When the heart becomes complete and the Dormant Calamity stands at the edge of the end, universe will either break free from his chains..."
His tone stopped for a moment and then continued more quietly.
"...or no living will see the next dawn."

chapters.title: Chapter 534: The Dormant Calamity
paragraphs: The atmosphere in the hall became heavy, and no one spoke immediately.
Kain’s eyes remained fixed on the floor, Lian could understand what phrase his mind was stuck on.
The Dormant Calamity.
But his own mind was somewhere else.

Nameless in the Father’s records, without chains in the threads of fate, the power of monsters, and for a moment, when he heard the part about the heart becoming complete, the Ruin Heart came to his mind.
Other than that heart, what other heart needed to become complete?
He had a very bad feeling that this prophecy was actually talking about all of his secrets, or was it just paranoia?
Although he strongly doubted it was only that.

Lian stopped himself there, he still did not have enough information, but in any case, he had a very bad feeling about Region One and immediately placed their threat level at the highest possible level.
"What exactly is the Dormant Calamity?"
Kain finally raised his head.
"That is one of the things even we do not agree about."
Orlian had no answer to this question.
"That helped a lot."
The Child of Light frowned.
"Prophecies are not written with explanations."
This time Elara answered, her tone was calm, but the same coldness as before was still there.
Kain looked at her.
"You seem to be a big fan of this prophecy."
"I am not a fan of it.
I take it seriously."
The girl said without changing her expression, and her eyes rested on Lian for a moment.
Lian said nothing, this time he was sure, the girl did not have a problem with him as a person, she had a problem with what he might represent.
After a few moments, Orlian turned his eyes toward his daughter.
"Elara."
The girl stood straight.
"Yes?"
"Prepare the Child of Light for the ceremony."
"What ceremony?"
Kain frowned almost immediately.
"The Return of Light Ceremony, the people need to know that the Child of Light has finally arrived."
Elara gave him all of her attention.
"Can we just make an announcement?"
"No."
"Very well.
At least are you coming?"
Kain looked at Lian.
He wanted to say something, but the Lord spoke for him.
"I still have some things to discuss with your friend."
The Child of Light nodded, and then left with the girl.
The atmosphere changed at that exact moment.
Orlian was no longer smiling.
The calm expression of a ruler was still there, but the small amount of warmth that had been visible in his behavior when Kain was present had disappeared.
Lian remained standing there.
The Lord only looked at him for several seconds, the silence lasted long enough to make it clear that it was intentional.
Then he said.
"No matter where I am in this region, I know this smell."
"What smell?"
Lian’s eyebrows slightly came together.
The ruler of Region Three looked directly into his eyes.
"Why do you smell like the Demon Of Eclipse?"
For a fraction of a second, the young Vorhelm’s mind stopped on that sentence.
Not because Orlian knew the name of the Demon Of Eclipse, that was normal, Silent Light was part of the history of Region Three.
But a smell?
Someone could not recognize the smell of a Demon just by reading a book.
"You know the Demon Of Eclipse?"
Orlian did not answer immediately, he turned back toward the window and looked at his own city for several seconds.
When he spoke again, his voice was slightly lower.
"I am the only human who survived that day."
Lian’s eyes remained fixed on his face, someone had actually managed to survive a Demon?
"When Silent Light fell, I was still a child."
Several priests realized that the city’s defense was going to break, so they picked up the child and moved through the tunnels beneath the sanctuary.
The first one died before leaving the city, the second one died several hours later, the Eclipse Energy destroyed the structures of their bodies from the inside.
The third priest took him to the only teleportation artifact they had left, something that could only take one person away from that city.
And he died right there, but the child was saved.
Orlian pulled his eyes away from the window.
"What remained on their clothes, on their skin, and even inside their blood...that smell can never be forgotten."
He was talking about the Eclipse Essence of that Demon.
Now his eyes were on Lian again.
"So I will ask again, Why do you smell like that Demon?"
He stayed silent for a few seconds, there was no reason to create a complete lie.
In fact, the truth was part of the best cover.
"When I helped Kain free the Sphere Of Witness, we realized that Eclipse Essence was trapped inside its structure."
Orlian showed no reaction.
But Lian continued.
"The Sphere could not become fully active until that corruption was removed.
I separated the black part from it, maybe that is why I smell like it."
Everything was true, he simply did not tell the rest.
The Lord looked at him for a long time, as if he was trying to see through him, as if he was trying to see inside him.
In the end, he calmly said.
"I see."
It seemed that he had not been able to find any lie in his words.
The young Vorhelm gave a small mocking smile inside his heart, because he had not lied, he had simply not told him everything.
The conversation naturally returned to the Demon Of Eclipse.
"That was one of the main reasons your world fell?" Lian asked.
Orlian let out a very short sigh.

"Yes, more precisely, the reason our world fell was because of very special creatures like that Demon Of Eclipse, for a long time, we did not have a name for them, until we learned that they were called Demons."
"Many people who live in this region today, when they hear the word Demon, only think about power.
Because they have never seen one up close."
"Power is not the worst part about them, they were not very different from us humans except for a few small physical differences, and in terms of intelligence, they were even above us."
"If the Seven Divines had not built the shelters, I do not think even one human civilization would have survived in this world today."
He paused for a moment.
"It was not only humans, there were other intelligent races too, some of them no longer exist today."
Lian slowly nodded, he knew about Demons very well, and the Awakened Federation had managed to discover a lot of information about them during the past 250 years.
There had also been many traces of Demons in the former Ruined Realms, and sometimes even important information about them was found.
For example, the Federation had discovered that there were exactly 72 Demons, and their number was not infinite.
Of course, their actual number should be lower now because Awakened had managed to hunt down several of them over the years.

He did not know why, but fortunately, Demons did not work together as a group, because otherwise, even a few dozen creatures with the power of the Demon Of Eclipse would have been more than enough to destroy a world.
Silence remained for a few moments.
Then Lian asked his main question.
"One more thing, before that Region Six commander died, he thought I was the Dormant Calamity."
Orlian’s expression changed slightly.
"I want to know why."
The Lord did not answer directly, he walked toward the table beside the hall and ran his finger over one of the reports placed on it.
"In the report the priest wrote for me, you fought a Leviathan that used Corrupted Light."
"That is right."
"Light that had been changed by Eclipse Essence."
"Yes."
Orlian now looked directly at him.
"And after that monster died, my priest saw you use the same type of Corrupted Light and kill the Region Six commander and his people."
Lian slowly nodded.
Now he understood.
The Lord repeated part of the prophecy.
"The Calamity will not come with one face, what exists within the souls of monsters will echo within him after their fall."
The air became heavy for a moment, and Orlian asked.
"Do you know how many interpretations there are for this sentence?"
"No."
"More than it is worth counting."
The man stood beside the table.
"Some say it means that the Dormant Calamity has several forms.Some say it means several souls or several different bodies."
He paused.
"But one of the oldest interpretations is that the Dormant Calamity can use the power of the monsters that it defeated along, in some form, for itself."
