chapters.title: Chapter 535: The Secret of the Seven Crystals
paragraphs: For a moment, everything stopped in Lian’s mind, he now understood, he now fucking understood how that commander had identified him as the same Dormant Calamity before his death.
The Region Six commander had seen that after the Leviathan died, he had been able to use the power of that monster.
For someone who knew that interpretation of the prophecy, the conclusion was not very strange, but this part was not really important.
There was something else.
Region One.

If the prophecy was real, if it had predicted the Tear of Witness, the Sphere of Witness, and the Child of Light more than ten years before Kain was born...and they had even been able to predict him...
What did they know about him?
Did they know about the Innate Skill Glutton?
What about Butcher?
Did they know that he could have Cores like monsters?
And did they even know about the nature of the Ruin Heart?
He felt his fingers become tense for a moment.
No.
The conclusion was too early.
It was possible that they only had a few vague sentences and generations had built interpretations around them.
But even this possibility made Region One dangerous, because they might know things they should not know.
They had practically revealed all of his biggest secrets through that prophecy, fortunately, it was a prophecy and every sentence could have thousands of interpretations.
But that did not make the situation much better, it could still be a disaster for him.
Orlian was looking at him.
"If the report is correct, which it seems to be, then I guess the last interpretation is correct, right?"
Lian raised his head and looked at the Lord, this man might now be someone who had understood one of his secrets, that he could use the power of monsters.
But he could not do anything, this man at least had the power of an Awakened who had gone through three evolutions, and if he wanted to make a more exact guess, he should not be far from Level 80.
"So it is true...don’t worry, you are our guest, and although I don’t know why, our god has chosen you and your friend as our future leaders, your secret will be safe with me."
"Thank you."
He did not know how much he could trust him, but the situation was not so bad that he could not control everything.

"I will try to hide anything related to you as much as possible, the main problem is not the Child of Light for the six Regions, they are worried about the appearance of his companion...and it is not even said that they will appear together."
Orlian answered calmly.
"This way, I will owe you too much."
Lian smiled.
"This is not only for you, it is also for us, if they find out that the Dormant Calamity has appeared, we will definitely become the target of a full-scale attack from all of them..."
"Even if they want to launch a full-scale attack, isn’t this place safe?"
"It should be safe, until today no one has been able to destroy the defenses of the Regions, but Region One worries me too much, I feel like they may have a way."
"I understand."
The young Vorhelm thought for a moment and then asked.
"How much do you think they know about the complete truth of the prophecy?"

"The original version came from there, what we have is the version that was given to Region 3, so they may have more information than us, but I would not worry too much, if they knew your face, they would already be looking for you."
He nodded, he was growing at an incredible speed and it should not take too long before no one could be a threat to him anymore.
Even so, he really wanted to know what the interpretation of the sentence "When the heart becomes complete and the Dormant Calamity stands at the edge of the end" would be.
He could understand that the meaning of the heart becoming complete was the completion of the five slots of the Ruin Heart.
But what interpretation did standing at the edge of the end have?
"As long as the Child of Light is here, you are also a guest of Region Three, so I hope you enjoy your time here as much as possible."
Orlian did not ask any more questions and instead said.
"Thank you for your hospitality, but I am not going to stay for long."
Lian nodded.
The Lord gave him a short look.
But he did not ask why.
He only moved his hand toward the door.
"Then you should not spend the rest of your time inside a hall."
The door opened.
This time, another young woman entered the hall, she was a few years older than Elara and looked around twenty-six.
Her golden hair was longer and tied simply behind her head.
Unlike her younger sister, her clothes looked less religious, white and gold, but suitable for movement.
A natural smile was on her face.
Cassia Veyra.
"My eldest daughter."
"I heard our city found some interesting guests today, welcome."
Cassia respectfully lowered her head toward Lian.
Her tone was completely different from Elara’s, warmer.
"Cassia, until the ceremony is over, show our guest around the city."
Orlian gestured toward his daughter.
"With pleasure."
She answered without hesitation.
Lian exchanged a short look between the father and daughter.
Apparently, not every member of this family was going to think the end of the world was near just because they saw him, unlike Elara.
Outside the hall, Cassia walked beside him for a few steps.
"Did my sister treat you coldly?"
She asked after a few seconds.
"You got straight to the point."
He gave her a short look.
Cassia laughed.
"I could tell from your reaction to me."
"Yes."
"It is not personal."
"I am still not sure about that part."
"Elara takes the prophecy very seriously."
Cassia gave another short laugh.
"I am also starting to take it seriously."
Lian answered.
She looked at him with curiosity for a few moments.
"Even so, you don’t look very worried."
"Worrying does not change anything."
"That answer sounds a lot like my father."
The tour of the city was interesting, unlike what Lian had expected.
Not because of the large buildings, but because Region 3 really had the structure of a living society.
The herb market was full of the strong smells of roots and interesting flowers, each of them had different properties.
In the healer section, several entire buildings were dedicated to treating physical injuries, poison, and Soul injuries.
Water channels passed through very old paths, and in several places, faint light rose from their floors.
Cassia explained.
"The water network has remained since before the Fall, a large part of the city was built on that old design."
After that, they passed a group of children wearing the same white clothes and practicing Light control in a large courtyard.
Some could only create a small point of light.
Some could move it between their fingers, and one of them directly shined his light on his friend’s face and made the other one angrily chase after him.
With the clothes they were wearing, they looked like young priests, or at least people who would soon become priests.
"The Priest Preparatory School, from this age they learn the teachings and traditions, and after the age of 16, they are taught how to use Light."
Cassia said with a smile.
When they reached the central part of the city, the streets became wider, the buildings moved farther away, and a huge square appeared in front of them.
Lian first noticed the channels, twelve water paths entered the square from different parts of the city.
But there were also strands of Light among them, they came out from underground, from the walls, and from the towers, and all of them reached the center of the square.
He took a few more steps forward and stopped.
A huge crystal was floating in the center of the square, it was more than thirty meters tall and had a semi-transparent structure, and white-golden light rose from deep inside it.
Bright lines slowly moved inside it, almost like watching the flow of blood inside a huge creature.
There was no base underneath it.
The crystal floated several meters above the central stone platform.

Strands of Light came out from it, one group went toward the border towers, another part went toward the farming lands, paths went toward the water channels, and much stronger strands went toward the huge defensive barrier surrounding the entire Region.
"The Heart of the Region."
Cassia said with clear pride.
Lian did not answer, something about the shape of the crystal looked familiar, he knew this thing, every Awakened knew it.
This was that crystal, at least one of the Seven Crystals and the final goal of all Awakened in the Ruined Realm, to collect them.
The reason?
It was simple, collecting all seven Crystals and destroying them would cleanse and completely close the Ruined Realm, and the monsters would no longer be able to enter their world through them.
"The Divine Gift of the Divine Of Light and Life to our ancestors, and the reason Region 3 is still alive after all these centuries."
She added.
Lian stayed silent, so the seven Crystals that all Awakened were searching for were the main source of the shelters’ defenses.
He looked more carefully at the strands of Light, the reason even the Demons had not been able to take these regions.
The reason for the defensive barrier, the source of the city network, was this thing.
To take this Crystal, Region 3 would have to lose the heart of its own defense.
And if all seven were needed?
All the Regions.
"Does every one of the seven Regions have one of these?"
He only asked, he already knew the answer, but he had to make sure.
Cassia answered without the slightest doubt.
"Of course, the appearance and properties of every heart are different, because each one is connected to one of the Seven Divines.
But every shelter has a heart."
That was enough.
But the information he had now could change the Federation’s relationship with all seven Regions forever.
And there was an even worse question.
How much did the Federation know about this truth?
He knew there were rumors and guesses saying that the Seven Crystals were inside the seven Regions.
And now, from his point of view, the guess had been confirmed, but were the Federation and the other forces also certain?
"Maybe I can use this."
He thought for a moment, a simple idea came to his mind that maybe with its help, he could destroy all six other Regions.
And this way, only Region Three and the followers of the Divine Of Light would remain and all the enemies would be eliminated.
Several hours later, Lian returned to their accommodation and had not even entered the room when he heard Kain’s voice.
"If you say one word, I will kill you."

"So it is true...don’t worry, you are our guest, and although I don’t know why, our god has chosen you and your friend as our future leaders, your secret will be safe with me."
"Thank you."
He did not know how much he could trust him, but the situation was not so bad that he could not control everything.

"I will try to hide anything related to you as much as possible, the main problem is not the Child of Light for the six Regions, they are worried about the appearance of his companion...and it is not even said that they will appear together."
Orlian answered calmly.
"This way, I will owe you too much."
Lian smiled.
"This is not only for you, it is also for us, if they find out that the Dormant Calamity has appeared, we will definitely become the target of a full-scale attack from all of them..."
"Even if they want to launch a full-scale attack, isn’t this place safe?"
"It should be safe, until today no one has been able to destroy the defenses of the Regions, but Region One worries me too much, I feel like they may have a way."
"I understand."
The young Vorhelm thought for a moment and then asked.
"How much do you think they know about the complete truth of the prophecy?"

"The original version came from there, what we have is the version that was given to Region 3, so they may have more information than us, but I would not worry too much, if they knew your face, they would already be looking for you."
He nodded, he was growing at an incredible speed and it should not take too long before no one could be a threat to him anymore.
Even so, he really wanted to know what the interpretation of the sentence "When the heart becomes complete and the Dormant Calamity stands at the edge of the end" would be.
He could understand that the meaning of the heart becoming complete was the completion of the five slots of the Ruin Heart.
But what interpretation did standing at the edge of the end have?
"As long as the Child of Light is here, you are also a guest of Region Three, so I hope you enjoy your time here as much as possible."
Orlian did not ask any more questions and instead said.
"Thank you for your hospitality, but I am not going to stay for long."
Lian nodded.
The Lord gave him a short look.
But he did not ask why.
He only moved his hand toward the door.
"Then you should not spend the rest of your time inside a hall."
The door opened.
This time, another young woman entered the hall, she was a few years older than Elara and looked around twenty-six.
Her golden hair was longer and tied simply behind her head.
Unlike her younger sister, her clothes looked less religious, white and gold, but suitable for movement.
A natural smile was on her face.
Cassia Veyra.
"My eldest daughter."
"I heard our city found some interesting guests today, welcome."
Cassia respectfully lowered her head toward Lian.
Her tone was completely different from Elara’s, warmer.
"Cassia, until the ceremony is over, show our guest around the city."
Orlian gestured toward his daughter.
"With pleasure."
She answered without hesitation.
Lian exchanged a short look between the father and daughter.
Apparently, not every member of this family was going to think the end of the world was near just because they saw him, unlike Elara.
Outside the hall, Cassia walked beside him for a few steps.
"Did my sister treat you coldly?"
She asked after a few seconds.
"You got straight to the point."
He gave her a short look.
Cassia laughed.
"I could tell from your reaction to me."
"Yes."
"It is not personal."
"I am still not sure about that part."
"Elara takes the prophecy very seriously."
Cassia gave another short laugh.
"I am also starting to take it seriously."
Lian answered.
She looked at him with curiosity for a few moments.
"Even so, you don’t look very worried."
"Worrying does not change anything."
"That answer sounds a lot like my father."
The tour of the city was interesting, unlike what Lian had expected.
Not because of the large buildings, but because Region 3 really had the structure of a living society.
The herb market was full of the strong smells of roots and interesting flowers, each of them had different properties.
In the healer section, several entire buildings were dedicated to treating physical injuries, poison, and Soul injuries.
Water channels passed through very old paths, and in several places, faint light rose from their floors.
Cassia explained.
"The water network has remained since before the Fall, a large part of the city was built on that old design."
After that, they passed a group of children wearing the same white clothes and practicing Light control in a large courtyard.
Some could only create a small point of light.
Some could move it between their fingers, and one of them directly shined his light on his friend’s face and made the other one angrily chase after him.
With the clothes they were wearing, they looked like young priests, or at least people who would soon become priests.
"The Priest Preparatory School, from this age they learn the teachings and traditions, and after the age of 16, they are taught how to use Light."
Cassia said with a smile.
When they reached the central part of the city, the streets became wider, the buildings moved farther away, and a huge square appeared in front of them.
Lian first noticed the channels, twelve water paths entered the square from different parts of the city.
But there were also strands of Light among them, they came out from underground, from the walls, and from the towers, and all of them reached the center of the square.
He took a few more steps forward and stopped.
A huge crystal was floating in the center of the square, it was more than thirty meters tall and had a semi-transparent structure, and white-golden light rose from deep inside it.
Bright lines slowly moved inside it, almost like watching the flow of blood inside a huge creature.
There was no base underneath it.
The crystal floated several meters above the central stone platform.

Strands of Light came out from it, one group went toward the border towers, another part went toward the farming lands, paths went toward the water channels, and much stronger strands went toward the huge defensive barrier surrounding the entire Region.
"The Heart of the Region."
Cassia said with clear pride.
Lian did not answer, something about the shape of the crystal looked familiar, he knew this thing, every Awakened knew it.
This was that crystal, at least one of the Seven Crystals and the final goal of all Awakened in the Ruined Realm, to collect them.
The reason?
It was simple, collecting all seven Crystals and destroying them would cleanse and completely close the Ruined Realm, and the monsters would no longer be able to enter their world through them.
"The Divine Gift of the Divine Of Light and Life to our ancestors, and the reason Region 3 is still alive after all these centuries."
She added.
Lian stayed silent, so the seven Crystals that all Awakened were searching for were the main source of the shelters’ defenses.
He looked more carefully at the strands of Light, the reason even the Demons had not been able to take these regions.
The reason for the defensive barrier, the source of the city network, was this thing.
To take this Crystal, Region 3 would have to lose the heart of its own defense.
And if all seven were needed?
All the Regions.
"Does every one of the seven Regions have one of these?"
He only asked, he already knew the answer, but he had to make sure.
Cassia answered without the slightest doubt.
"Of course, the appearance and properties of every heart are different, because each one is connected to one of the Seven Divines.
But every shelter has a heart."
That was enough.
But the information he had now could change the Federation’s relationship with all seven Regions forever.
And there was an even worse question.
How much did the Federation know about this truth?
He knew there were rumors and guesses saying that the Seven Crystals were inside the seven Regions.
And now, from his point of view, the guess had been confirmed, but were the Federation and the other forces also certain?
"Maybe I can use this."
He thought for a moment, a simple idea came to his mind that maybe with its help, he could destroy all six other Regions.
And this way, only Region Three and the followers of the Divine Of Light would remain and all the enemies would be eliminated.
Several hours later, Lian returned to their accommodation and had not even entered the room when he heard Kain’s voice.
"If you say one word, I will kill you."

chapters.title: Chapter 536: The Invitation From the Pendragon Family
paragraphs: Lian opened the door and for a few seconds, he only looked at the scene in front of him.
Kain was wearing a formal white and gold outfit.
A long robe decorated with a sun symbol on the shoulders, with a bright belt around his waist..
Elara was standing beside him, and from her expression, it was clear that this outfit was completely suitable for the ceremony.
Cassia entered behind he and looked at Kain, then smiled.
"Don’t say anything." Kain immediately pointed his finger at Lian.
He entered the room.
"I didn’t say anything."
"Your face is talking again."
"The clothes are completely suitable for the status of the Child of Light." Elara said without looking at the young Vorhelm.
"Do you see what I’m dealing with?"
"It was your choice to come."
This time, Kain paused and then his expression became more serious.
"Actually, that’s what I wanted to talk about."
Lian looked at him.
Cassia and Elara both became silent.

"I want to stay here for a while, until now, most of the things I learned about Light were either things I understood by myself, or things I learned through training and fighting, even after changing my class and becoming the Child of Light, I’m still doing half of the things through trial and error."
He moved the Light between his fingers.

"There are people here who have kept hundreds of years of knowledge about Light, not just shooting it, but controlling it, increasing its density, bending it, reflecting it, healing with it, using Light inside arrays... they even have methods that I didn’t know were possible."
Kain turned off the Light.
"If I return now, I’m an idiot."
"Then stay." Lian said without hesitation.
"That’s it?"
"You have a good reason, and you won’t find a better place than this."
He himself, if he found a place where he could directly get information about the Monster Class, he would probably make the same decision.
"What about you?" Kain asked.
This time, the young Vorhelm did not answer for a few seconds, he remembered an invitation that had been sitting in the corner of his mind for some time.
The Pendragon Family and their Heir Selection Ceremony, and most importantly, Seris.
The girl herself had invited him.
It had not been long since the last time Lian had seen her.
However, when he thought about returning now, he realized that something more than the ceremony itself made him want to go.
He wanted to see Seris.
The thought was so simple that it felt strange to him, he could not remember ever missing someone before.
He paused on this feeling for a few moments, it was not unpleasant, and it was not something he wanted to deny.
It was just an unfamiliar feeling.
"I have to go back."
"Do you have something important to do?" Kain looked at him suspiciously.
Lian only nodded and avoided giving any more explanation.
The decision was made.
Kain would stay in Region Three for a while and learn how far the talent of the Child of Light could really go.
"Take care of yourself." The young Vorhelm said to him before leaving.
Kain nodded.
"Of course."
"And if one day you realize that being the Child of Light is turning into a golden prison, tell me before it is too late."
Elara, who was standing a few steps away, looked at Lian with clear dissatisfaction.
Cassia, however, could not completely hide her smile.
The Child of Light thought for a moment and then asked with a smile.
"Will you come with One and Two to save me?"
"If you stop giving them stupid names, definitely."
"Good. Then I can relax."
"No one intends to imprison the Child of Light." Elara finally said.
Kain gave her a short look and said sarcastically.
"Good. Then we will never have to find out how many hits that giant ant needs to break the doors here."
Lian decided that before the argument really started, it was a good time to leave.
[Do you want to return to your own world?]
He chose Yes, and the space around his body changed, the white and gold image of the room slowly stretched.
Then everything disappeared.
Silence.
Lian blinked several times and looked around, he had returned to the dormitory room.
The first thing he saw after that was his phone, it was not turned off and still had charge, it had only been left on the table and its screen was full of notifications.
When he picked it up, the number of messages was more than he expected.
News.
Personal messages.
Academy notifications.
Several missed calls.
But one of the messages immediately caught his attention.
Sender:
Aurelia Pendragon (Aurelia Pendragon).

With one look, he understood that it was the official invitation to the ceremony and it had been sent to him last week, fortunately, the date of the ceremony was two days later and he had not missed it.
The invitation was short but formal, Lian’s name was registered as one of the direct guests of the family.
Seris had personally invited him before, and now the official invitation had also arrived.
He looked at the screen for a few seconds.
Only two.
An image of Seris appeared in his mind, her silver hair and that cold look, the serious tone she used even when she said something normal, as if she was giving an order.
And again, that same feeling of missing her, he missed her, it would not be wrong to say that the girl had been beside him since the first day of his adventures in the Ruined Realm.
Then he opened the news page, his smile quickly disappeared, the first headline was about a new Rift, then a second and a third.
Lian quickly went through several news reports, the number of Rifts had increased during the past few weeks.
Not the normal yearly increase, but a kind of sudden jump.
One report showed a map of the Earth, with new red points spread across several regions of the world.
Two major European cities had fallen.
In one of them, several Rifts had opened almost at the same time, and the local forces had been forced to evacuate a large part of the city before support arrived.
The second city was in a worse situation, parts of it were still under the control of monsters.
Three major cities in Asia had also gone out of control, one after a high-level Rift and two because of several events happening at the same time.
And in Africa, another city had fallen.
He opened one of the images, burned buildings, Federation temporary walls, and columns of smoke could be seen.
People were leaving the area by buses and cars, and people were sitting on the ground beside ambulances.
Part of the city was marked in red on the map.
He only looked at it for a while and remembered Gareth’s words, the increase in Rifts and the increasing pressure on the Federation and the Guilds.
What had still looked more like a worrying trend than a crisis at that time was no longer just a possibility, it was happening.
And if the speed continued to increase like this, the six cities would not be the last cases.
Lian opened several more news reports, armies were being moved and the Federation had divided emergency forces between the continents.
Several Hunter bases had canceled their general missions to keep forces ready to respond to the Rifts.
While he had been searching for answers in the Ruined Realm, the situation in his own world had become worse.
Lian closed the news and returned to the message list, several messages were related to the Academy, two were from people he knew, and then a name made his finger stop.
His uncle.
The message only had one sentence.
"I’m glad you came back safely, it seems their plan failed."
Lian remained completely still for a few seconds, his eyes fixed on one word.
"Their plan."
Not:
"What happened?"
Not:
"I heard the Special Area was dangerous."
He slowly sat on the edge of the bed and his mind returned to the last day of the Special Area.
And all the things his brother, Darian, had said above him when he thought Lian was dead, at that time, it had only been a guess that his stepmothers might have sent this boy to kill him.
And now, considering his uncle’s message, he could say that his guess had been completely correct.
Lian read the message again.
Once.
Twice.
There was no other explanation, it was possible that his uncle had learned the truth after everything was over.

But the way the message was written... it did not seem like that, it sounded more like someone who had been waiting for the result from the beginning, and there was also his previous message that seemed like he wanted to warn him.
He opened the number and his finger stayed on the call button for a few moments.
There was no time for guessing anymore, it was time to ask directly about this.
His finger moved down and the call was connected, and fortunately, it did not take long for him to get an answer.
"It has been a while, my dear nephew."

chapters.title: Chapter 537: The Patriarch Is Coming Back
paragraphs: For a few seconds, neither of them said anything.
"It has been a while, my dear nephew, how have you been? You finally decided to call me." His uncle, Damian, spoke in a calm tone.
Lian went directly to the thing that had made him call.
"You said their plan failed, what plan?"
The other side of the line became silent, not long enough to be strange, but enough for him to understand that his uncle had not prepared the answer beforehand.
Damian was deciding how much to tell him.

"Your stepmothers have been getting too active lately, more than what can be called normal family competition, I heard that you faced Darian" It was clear that he probably knew about a large part of what had happened.
"The Special Area incident probably wasn’t their last attempt. If I were you, from now on I would check even the things that seem completely random twice."
"Is there a reason for that? Or is it the same old jealousy?"
For years, the competition between his father’s wives had not been considered strange.
The Vorhelm Family was large enough for every branch to have its own supporters, even a small success could change the weight of a faction.
But trying to kill someone? This was no longer normal competition, especially when it reached the point where all of them decided to work together to remove one person.
This showed that they either knew something, or something was about to happen that was a very big threat to them.
"I don’t think it’s only jealousy." Damian’s voice returned after a few seconds.
"Then?"
Lian raised his head slightly.
"These days, there is almost only one piece of news going around the entire family, the return of the Patriarch."
"My father is back?" Even so, even if that was the case, he could not understand what this had to do with anything... wait, unless...?
"No, but he will return soon."
Lian said nothing for a few moments.
His father had been out of the family’s direct reach for a long time.
Neither his absence was something new, nor was it unusual for most of the family’s daily affairs to continue without him.
But his "return" was usually not without a reason, and he had a guess about what the reason for his return would be.
His uncle continued.
"And the thing that has everyone worried is not only his return. It is the decision he is going to make after he returns."
Lian leaned back against the chair, at first, several possibilities appeared in his mind.
A war?
Resource distribution?
A change in the council?
But none of them explained why several of his stepmothers would suddenly go as far as physically removing him, and because of that, he rejected all of them.
Only one answer remained.
"He wants to choose the heir." Lian whispered quietly.
"Exactly." The other side of the line confirmed.
He looked at the ceiling.
Of course.
If the Vorhelm Patriarch was finally going to choose his official successor, all the internal balance of the family would change.
Every wife, every child, every branch, and every council member who had invested in one of the candidates for years would suddenly have something real to lose.
"And what has made them the most nervous is that your name has risen too much during the past few months."
This time, Lian laughed, it was a short laugh that came more from how pointless the situation was.
"So that’s why Darian wanted to kill me? Because my father might remember after all these years that he has another son?"
"Lian."
Damian’s tone made him become silent.
"I can’t prove exactly who gave Darian what order.
He chose his words carefully.
"I can’t even say with certainty that their final goal was definitely your death, or that they would have accepted something less."
"But?"
Lian slightly narrowed his eyes.
"But Darian entering the Special Area was not a coincidence, he was not supposed to be there, but he entered at the last moment, which means he had a goal, and that goal was you."
The young Vorhelm already knew this part, besides, something his uncle did not know was that he had heard that bastard’s words with his own ears.
Damian let out a short breath.
"I’ll stop their attempts as much as I can. But I can’t stay beside you every hour, and you are no longer the boy who stays inside the family estate all day."
His voice became more serious.
"They will do anything they can to make sure you are not chosen, the more likely you become to be chosen, the harsher their methods will become."
Lian remained silent for a few moments, he was neither afraid nor did he care, the fact that several people in his family wanted to remove him was more annoying than frightening.

But his uncle was also right, these women were worried that if he was chosen as the heir, he would definitely take revenge on them, and that was why they would do anything to make sure he was not chosen.
Even if they had to use harsher methods.
"I’ll be careful."
A few seconds of silence formed between them, his uncle was not completely relieved by this, he was also trying to protect his nephew, but it was not enough.
Besides, he had noticed that these women had been too quiet lately and had done nothing, but this only gave him a worse feeling.
His brother’s wives would definitely show their poison again somewhere.
Lian moved the phone from one hand to the other and then asked the question that had been in his mind since he saw the invitation.
"Are the Vorhelms sending a delegation to the Pendragon ceremony?"
"Of course, it’s not a small ceremony, a delegation from the family is going."
"Who is leading it?"
"Your older brother."
"So I’ll see my brother again."
It was a normal sentence, but apparently something in it made his uncle pause.
"Wait."
Lian felt that the subject was about to go in a direction he would not like.
"What?"
"You’re going too?"
"Yeah."
This time, the silence was longer.
He moved the phone slightly away from his ear and looked at the screen to make sure the call had not ended.
It was still connected.
"Uncle?"
"I’m thinking."
"Hmm? What are you thinking about? Which part of me going needs thinking about?"
"Now that I think about it..." But Damian continued after a few moments.
"What?"
"There was also something strange between you and that Pendragon girl at Diana’s birthday ceremony."
Lian did not even need to ask which girl he meant.
"What was strange? We only fought, that’s all."
His uncle really thought for a few seconds and then asked with a simplicity that made the sentence even worse.
"Are you two lovers?
Lian coughed several times heavily at that exact moment.
"Cough cough! Where did that come from?!"

In love?

Her voice when she personally invited him to the ceremony.

He missed her.

Lian went directly to the thing that had made him call.
"You said their plan failed, what plan?"
The other side of the line became silent, not long enough to be strange, but enough for him to understand that his uncle had not prepared the answer beforehand.
Damian was deciding how much to tell him.

This was no longer normal competition, especially when it reached the point where all of them decided to work together to remove one person.

"My father is back?" Even so, even if that was the case, he could not understand what this had to do with anything... wait, unless...?
"No, but he will return soon."
Lian said nothing for a few moments.
His father had been out of the family’s direct reach for a long time.

Resource distribution?
A change in the council?

Of course.

This time, Lian laughed, it was a short laugh that came more from how pointless the situation was.

Because my father might remember after all these years that he has another son?"
"Lian."
Damian’s tone made him become silent.
"I can’t prove exactly who gave Darian what order.
He chose his words carefully.

His voice became more serious.
"They will do anything they can to make sure you are not chosen, the more likely you become to be chosen, the harsher their methods will become."
Lian remained silent for a few moments, he was neither afraid nor did he care, the fact that several people in his family wanted to remove him was more annoying than frightening.

But his uncle was also right, these women were worried that if he was chosen as the heir, he would definitely take revenge on them, and that was why they would do anything to make sure he was not chosen.
Even if they had to use harsher methods.

chapters.title: Chapter 538: Not Everyone Wants to Be Strong
paragraphs: The training field that usually had the sound of weapons clashing and Mana explosions coming from it now had only three people.
The large cafe near the central square was half-empty.
Even some of the educational buildings had closed the doors to their side sections.
Lian put his hands inside his pockets.
Hearing so many normal sounds and seeing so much empty space was calming.
He followed the stone path beside the Academy’s gardens, letting his mind stay empty for a while.
Until a familiar face several dozen meters away caught his attention, a girl was sitting alone on a bench beside the path.
Her head was slightly lowered and a small book was beside her.
At first glance, Lian only felt that he had seen her somewhere.
Then he got closer and recognized her.
Claire.
It had been a long time since he had seen her, Claire was the healer of their group in the border city.
Before that incident, most of what the young Vorhelm remembered about her was her relatively calm behavior, great caution, and good healing skills that had helped the group many times.
Then two of their group members died and everything changed for the girl.
The incident had affected every member of the group, but not in the same way, some became angry, some trained more, and some tried to become stronger faster.
But Claire had pulled away, and there had been no news about her for a long time.
Lian slightly changed his path and walked toward the bench, the girl was so lost in thought that she did not notice his presence until he sat beside the bench.
She was slightly startled and turned her head.
She looked at him for a few moments and then the tension on her face slowly disappeared, a small smile appeared.
"I didn’t expect to see you like this."
"I didn’t expect to see you here after all this time either." Lian leaned against the back of the bench and gave her a short look.
She looked better than the last time he had seen her.
"When did you come back?"
"About a week ago."
"Welcome back." He said quietly.
"Thank you." The girl’s smile became a little wider too, as if seeing an old friend after all this time made her happy.
Then silence formed, but it was not the uncomfortable kind.
Both of them looked at the path in front of them and a gentle breeze moved through the small trees in the garden.
One of the three students training in the field farther away used a skill incorrectly and the sound of something hitting the ground could be heard.
Neither of them cared.
Several minutes passed.
"Everyone has been talking about you these days." This time Claire was the one who spoke, and after a short pause, she continued.
"Almost everyone who is still here." There was a small smile on her face.
"Your rankings, the competition, what happened in the Ruined Realm, even the professors talk about you."
Then she tilted her head slightly.
"I think I should have realized back then that you would become famous one day."
Lian said nothing, the girl looked at him for a few seconds and then her smile slowly disappeared and her fingers locked together.
"All of you continued after that incident."
Her voice had become quieter.
"You. Cassian, Marcus, Selina, Liana..."
Her thumb moved across the back of her other hand, a small movement that showed that her body was nervous.
"But I couldn’t."
Lian did not interrupt her.
Claire took a slow breath.
"For a long time, I thought maybe the problem was me. That I should never have come with you.
A pause.
"I wasn’t like you."
"I was weak."
A moment later, she corrected her own sentence.
"No... more than weak, I was scared."
She gave a short and bitter smile.
"You know what the stupid part is? I never wanted to become an Awakened." The wind moved a few strands of hair beside her face.
"Almost everyone wishes to successfully Awaken, families celebrate for their children, everyone talks about getting a good Class and a good Talent."
She raised her eyes.
"But from the beginning, I only wanted to stay away from these things."
Her voice trembled very slightly for a moment.
"From monsters, from the Ruined Realm, and from waking up every day knowing that someone beside you might not come back."
She looked at the ground again.
"Then I became an Awakened."
This time she laughed, but it was not a happy laugh.
"A lot of people thought I was lucky."
Lian said nothing for a few seconds, prepared advice would not help, telling her "You are strong" would not change anything.
Claire herself knew that she had healing abilities, that was not the problem.
He had no idea how he should comfort her, their views were different, he had always wanted to become an Awakened but his first two Awakening processes had failed.
But this girl was different, she had never wanted to become an Awakened.
Because of that, he could not simply tell her that he understood.
In the end, he said.
"Being afraid of something that can really kill you is not weakness."
She raised her eyes.
"If you are never afraid, either you don’t understand what is standing in front of you or you are an idiot, I mean, it’s normal to be afraid of monsters, they are really ugly and scary."
"Your way of comforting people is strange." Claire smiled again and even laughed quietly.
"I’m trying." Lian continued after a moment.

"But if you want to come back, this time come back because you want to, don’t come back because everyone else continued, not because you think you have fallen behind, not because someone expects you to act like everyone else."
Lian leaned his shoulder against the back of the bench.
"If you really don’t want to enter the Ruined Realm, don’t."
"Are you serious?" Claire looked at him for a while.
"Yes."
"I thought you would tell me that I have to face my fear."
"You don’t have to fight everything you are afraid of, you only have to make sure your fear isn’t the one making the decision for you." The young Vorhelm added.
Another silence formed.
This time Claire thought for longer and then slowly nodded.
"I think that was what I had been trying to understand all this time."
"Are you better now?"
She slowly pressed her lips together and then nodded.
"A lot."
She paused for a moment.
"Of course, I didn’t just sit at home during this time, Professor Aldric made a plan for me."
That name made Lian pay more attention.
"First, simple Mana control exercises, then only healing people who were injured during training, after some time he allowed me to stay beside the training field, and then monster simulations."
Lian could guess the path.
A gradual return, not throwing someone who had been hurt by battle directly into another major event.
Aldric, despite his strict appearance, knew exactly what he was doing.
The girl slowly breathed out.
"The first time, I couldn’t even stay until the end, the second time was better, the third time was the same... I think maybe I can return." Her eyes stayed on her hands for a moment.
"Good, I guess it won’t take long until you succeed." This time Lian answered without thinking much.
The girl’s expression softened, this time she said nothing, there was no need.
A few minutes later, the atmosphere of the conversation became lighter.
"How are the others? Cassian, Marcus, Selina, Liana."
"They’re all fine, they are probably in the Ruined Realm right now."
"Have they improved a lot?" Claire nodded and asked a few moments later.
"Compared to the last time you saw them, probably a lot, all of them have passed their first evolution."
It took a few seconds for the reaction to come.
"All of them?"
"Yeah."
She slowly breathed out, and for a moment, something appeared in her eyes that he recognized.
The feeling of being left behind.
"And they were all waiting for you to come back." But before that thought could grow, he continued.
"Really?" Claire became still.
"Yeah."
"Even after all this time?"
"You weren’t removed from the group, you just went away for a while to get yourself together." The young Vorhelm looked at her.
The girl lowered her eyes, this time her silence was different and a few seconds later she asked.
"What about you?"
"What about me?"
"What have you been doing these days?"
"Exploring and trying not to die in the middle of the way."
Claire stared at him for a few moments and then started laughing, perhaps it was the first completely natural laugh Lian had heard from her since that incident.
He also gave a very small smile, at least this meeting had not ended badly.
The following days passed more quietly.
Lian saw Claire several more times.
The first time, the girl was standing beside the training field and only watching two students fight.
When one of them was injured, her body became tense for a few seconds, but she did not move away from the field.
The second time, she entered the treatment area herself.
Her hands were still shaking a little at first, but when the healing Mana started to flow, the shaking became less.
The third time, she entered a simple simulation with a training group for a few minutes.
It was still not a real mission, there were still no real monsters, but she was no longer running away from getting close to the training field.
That was enough.
At least for now.
And anyway, the day came when he had to leave.
The capital’s large transportation center was crowded from the early hours of the morning.
The huge building had several separate halls, and each hall was assigned to a group of intercontinental portals.
Normal travelers were rarely seen in this section.
The cost of direct transportation through a portal was still not low enough to replace airplanes and trains for everyone.
And his destination was on another continent.

chapters.title: Chapter 539: The Patriarch Wants To See Me ( PS Bonus - )
paragraphs: Lian presented the official invitation along with his identity at the reception desk, the place he wanted to go required some kind of visa and entry permission, and this invitation could be used as one.
The employee checked the destination.
"Verendal, right?"
"Yeah."
"Direct transfer is active."
The amount appeared on the screen.
He paid the cost in dollars without any special reaction, and a few minutes later, he was standing in front of one of the transfer gates.
The surface of the portal moved like a layer of liquid glass, and the sign turned green.
He entered and felt a short pressure across his entire body, for a moment, there was neither ground nor air, then his shoes were on stone again.
The air was different and colder, with the smell of old rain and wet stone in it.
Lian left the transfer hall, and Europe was in front of him.
Verendal did not look like the new cities that had been built, it did not look like the old cities that had also gained new parts.

The first thing that caught his attention was the age of the city, which could be seen to some degree by looking at the dark stone streets, buildings with stone exteriors that were hundreds of years old, and tall windows.
Dark sloped roofs rose above the buildings, and in some places, narrow towers rose from between them.
Several bell towers could still be seen among the buildings, although modern communication systems had been installed on some of them.
The Pendragon Family had not destroyed the city to make it modern.
They had placed technology inside the old architecture.
Electric lights were placed on walls that were perhaps four hundred years old.
Modern cars passed by buildings that had survived several wars and several historical periods.
But the real difference between Verendal and Medes was not the architecture, it was ownership.
Medes was not the city of the Vorhelm Family.
The Vorhelms were one of the greatest powers established there, and their huge family properties were located in a separate part of the city.
Of course, because the Vorhelms were the strongest power established in that city, it had caused the whole world to consider the city as belonging to them.
But Verendal? The entire city was the territory of the Pendragon Family.
The land, old walls, training centers, military bases, main properties, security forces, and even many old businesses were directly or indirectly connected to the family.
This was not a place where the family lived, the city itself was the family’s home.
And not everyone was allowed to enter it, everyone needed a visa or the same entry permission to enter.
The transfer center where Lian had appeared was outside the main security ring.
On the way to the checkpoint, the crowd around the ceremony became more noticeable.
Luxury cars passed through the private road one after another.
Some were simple, while some were so luxurious that they looked more like a display of power than a way of transportation.
Guards wearing the clothes of different families could be seen around the entrance.
And different flags were on the cars, with small symbols of those flags on the chest parts of the guards’ clothes.
Lian recognized some of them, in fact, he was able to see three of the six great families from a distance.
Stormheart.
Valemont.
Several cars under them had stopped there, and their guards were checking their entry permits.
In another part of the road were Ravencrest and finally Eisenwald.
The six great families that were known as the most powerful families in the world and had existed for more than 250 years.
Pendragon, Vorhelm, Stormheart, Valemont, Grendalz, and Blackthorn.
All of them had sent representatives, and this was still only the great families.
The flags of dozens of smaller families, associations, organizations, and other powerful groups could also be seen.
The ceremony that was being held was not only a family event, it was an opportunity for some of the most powerful people of the new and old generations to gather in one place.
At this ceremony, the next leader of one of the most powerful organizations in the world would be announced, a family whose decisions could affect the course of the entire world.
Many came only to flatter them and show respect, while other forces of the same level only sent delegations to maintain diplomatic relations.
Lian continued along his path, and an unwanted comparison formed in his mind.
The structure of the Pendragons was different from his own family, power here was much more concentrated.
There was a patriarch and a matriarch, both of them were at the highest level of decision-making.
There was a small council of elders, but unlike the Vorhelms, power was not divided between dozens of almost equally powerful factions.

But the Vorhelm Family was different, the council, family branches, the patriarch’s wives, old factions, and at the top of them all, the patriarch who was currently not directly present, all had a role in decision-making.
That alone was enough for a decision like choosing the heir to bring the entire family into a quiet chaos.
The Pendragons at least looked more organized from the outside, whether they were really like that or not was another matter.
The main checkpoint did not look like an ordinary city gate.
Two tall stone walls stood on both sides, and several control paths had been created between them.
Each path was covered by checking mechanisms and several guards, forces were also stationed on the towers around them.
Even on a normal day, Verendal was not a city open to tourists.
Family members, affiliated forces, approved workers, official guests, and merchants with special permits, only these groups were allowed to enter.
Today? The security had been increased several times.
The young Vorhelm entered the line for official guests, and it did not take long before he reached the checking section.
The guard was a middle-aged man wearing the family’s official clothes.
"Name and affiliation." he asked without raising his voice.
"Lian Vorhelm."
For a fraction of a second, the guard’s gaze became more focused, he recognized the name.
Lian presented his identity card and official invitation, and the man placed the invitation on the checking screen.
A short light passed over it.
[Identity confirmed.]
[Official Invitation: Pendragon Family.]
[Issuer: Aurelia Pendragon.]
The guard returned the card, and this time his behavior became slightly more formal.
"Entry confirmed, Mr. Vorhelm."
He stepped aside.
"Welcome to Verendal."
The inner gate opened, and he entered the Dragon City.
Inside the main ring, the crowd was even larger, guests were moving in small groups.
Family staff were guiding the guests to different accommodations.
Some streets had been closed for official delegations to pass through, and security forces could be seen at almost every main intersection.
He took out his phone and wrote a message to Aurelia Pendragon.
"I arrived. I am inside Verendal now."
Send.
He lowered the phone, he did not expect an answer right away, Aurelia was probably one of the busiest people in the family during the days before the ceremony.
Lian continued along his path and decided to look around the city.
But five minutes passed and there was no message.
Ten minutes, and still no answer.
He checked his phone again, the message had been delivered and had even been seen, but there was no reply.
He put it back into his pocket, it was not a problem.
He could go to the accommodation that had been prepared for the guests first, but he had only gone a few hundred meters farther along the main street when something changed.
The people moving in front of him moved slightly to the side, not because of him, but because they recognized a group coming from the other side of the street.
Six people were coming toward Lian, all of them wearing the same dark clothes with a small Pendragon symbol on their chests.
Their behavior was different from the guards at the entrance, their steps were coordinated and the distance between them was clear, none of them looked around.
The young Vorhelm did not slow down, but he opened his perception toward them.
The pressure of their presence was enough immediately, all six of them had gone through at least two evolutions, and some had probably gone even further.
It was too many people for welcoming a young guest.
The group came directly toward him, and stopped several meters away, the man standing in the center took one step forward.
There was no hostility on his face, there was even formal respect in his behavior.
"Mr. Lian Vorhelm?"
Lian’s gaze briefly moved over the five people behind him.
"That’s me."
The man lowered his head slightly.
"Our patriarch has asked to speak with you before you attend any other event."
Lian said nothing for a few seconds.
The Pendragon Patriarch.
He had not even seen Seris yet.
Aurelia had not even replied to his message.
And now, before he could even reach the accommodation, the highest-ranking man of the Pendragon Family wanted to see him.
Could something have happened?

chapters.title: Chapter 540: Face to Face with a Celestial
paragraphs: "Please guide me."
The man in front of Lian lowered his head slightly and, without any extra explanation, turned toward the eastern part of the street.
The other five moved almost at the same time.
Not close enough to surround him and not far enough for their presence to be meaningless.
Their formation was too organized for them to simply be a group guiding a guest.
Pav said nothing about it.
If the Pendragon Patriarch really wanted to take him somewhere, it was probably not strange for his family to send six Awakened who had gone through at least two Evolutions.
The more important question was, why?
He had been in Verendal for less than half an hour.
He still had not seen Seris, Aurelia had not even answered his message.
And now, before all of them, one of the most powerful living men in the world wanted to speak with him personally.
Lian walked a few steps behind the commander.
Whatever it was, he was not worried, he doubted that his life was in danger, it was more likely that the man was curious to know who his daughter had spent so much time with.
As they moved away from the public part of Verendal, the crowd around the ceremony slowly disappeared as well.
There were fewer flags of the great families.
Official cars no longer passed beside them, and the guests who had been seen at almost every intersection only a few minutes ago were replaced by Pendragon forces.
The buildings also changed and were older and larger.

And unlike the outer part of the city where historical architecture was mixed with modern equipment, here the family seemed to have allowed even fewer things to change the original shape of the buildings.
Walls made of light gray stone, tall arches, and dragon statues were placed on the walls and in the gardens.
Trees whose trunks were so thick that it was clear some of them had been standing there long before several generations of the family had been born.
Almost ten minutes later, the group stopped in front of another wall, the wall was not as tall as Verendal’s outer wall and did not have many towers.
But with only one look, he noticed the difference, the difference was the guards here.
Four people stood on both sides of the gate, none of them wore heavy armor and their weapons were not hidden either.
But the presence of all four was heavier than all the forces he had seen beside the outer gate, these four had also gone through at least two Evolutions.
The commander of the group walked forward, showed something to one of the guards, and a few seconds later, the stone gate opened without a sound.
The man turned back to Lian.
"From here on, the Patriarch is waiting for you alone."
Lian gave a short look at the six people who had come with him.
None of them moved forward.
"I understand."
He passed through the gate.
The inside was almost the opposite of what he expected from the "heart of the property of one of the six great families."
There were huge palaces, buildings that were hundreds of years old, wide gardens, and fountains flowing among stone dragon statues.
But there was no excessive gold, precious stones on the walls, or pointless display of wealth.
The main feeling of the place was its age, everything seemed to have a reason for being there.
On one of the walls, old marks from impacts remained, and no one had tried to cover them with new stone.
A huge dragon statue stood in the central square, part of one of its wings was broken.
Even on the path, in some places, new stones had been placed among pieces that were several centuries old.
A servant was waiting at the end of the path, without needing an introduction, he lowered his head.
"Mr. Vorhelm. This way."
Lian followed him, they passed through two hallways, a small courtyard, and then the second floor of one of the main buildings.
The servant stopped in front of a wooden door.
"The Patriarch is waiting for you inside."
He placed his hand on the handle and the door opened.
The room looked more like a private library than the official meeting place of a Patriarch, and at the end of the room, there was a huge window through which a large part of Verendal could be seen.
A man was standing beside that same window, he had a white cup in his right hand.
He was wearing only simple dark clothes with a small Pendragon dragon symbol on his chest, and his silver hair covered both sides of his temples.
His face looked around fifty years old.
His body was tall and fit, but there was no exaggerated attempt to show physical strength in his appearance.
Hearing the door close, the man turned around, and gray eyes fell on Lian.
And at that exact moment, his body reacted before his mind, his body froze in place.
It was as if it was no longer even his body and it did not dare to listen to his consciousness, no matter how hard he tried, his body did not move at all.
His instinct also simply told him that trying was useless, if the man in front of him decided to kill him right now, he would die.
That was it.
The strangest part? His body did not even have any desire to resist, as if it had already accepted the result.
And no aura was coming from the man’s body at all, it was like standing in front of a completely ordinary human.
The man slightly raised his cup and a friendly smile appeared on his face.
"I finally get to see you in person, come in, I’m not going to interrogate you or hurt you."
After hearing the man’s words, the impossible pressure suddenly disappeared from him and his body could finally move again.
"This was not the start I expected." Lian walked a few steps forward, the speed of his steps did not change.
The man’s smile became deeper and his eyes moved to Lian’s posture for a moment.
"Don’t worry, if I wanted to kill you, I wouldn’t need to send six people after you, you would have died the moment you stepped into this city."
"That sentence usually doesn’t make people less worried."
There was silence for a moment, he knew those words were not a lie, the man in front of him had gone through five Evolutions.
He was a man who stood at the top of the world’s power, so powerful that it could not be described, their mere breath was enough to turn an entire mountain range into ash.
Their footsteps alone could cause earthquakes, and their gaze could make oceans evaporate.
A Celestial was standing in front of him!
Rhaenar Pendragon!
The man laughed... he really laughed.
"Good."
He placed his cup on the table.
"At least you’re not so afraid that you can’t speak in front of me."
He pointed toward the chair.
"Sit."
Lian sat down and the man sat across from him as well.
"Tea?" And without waiting for an answer, he placed a cup in front of him.
For a few seconds, the only sound in the room was the sound of tea being poured.
"Was your trip good?"
"To this city?"
"In general."
"It could have been more peaceful."
"When I read the reports about you, I also come to the conclusion that you are somehow a magnet for danger."
Lian looked at him and Rhaenar smiled.
"You thought I would summon you without knowing who you are?"
"Of course not."
"Good."
The man took a sip of his tea.
"The academy, your sister’s birthday event, the events in the Special Area, your growth over the past few months, and even the final exams, I’ve heard about all of it."
"Then I don’t need to explain much about myself." The young Vorhelm did not touch his cup.
"No."
Rhaenar casually raised his shoulder slightly.
"Most of the things I could learn by asking, I’ve already read about."
"Then can I ask why I’m here?" Lian thought for a moment.
This time, the Patriarch looked at him for a few seconds.
"Because reports don’t answer questions, people do."

He understood what he meant, this man had not been looking for information from the beginning, he was watching him, the way he sat, his answers, and the things he chose to say and the things he intentionally did not say.
Rhaenar picked up his cup again.
"One year ago, no one knew the name Lian Vorhelm, and anyone who did know you called you a loser."
He calmly drank his tea.
"Now, for some people, the question is whether your father will put your name at the top of the heir list when he returns."
"Our family news spreads quickly." Lian did not change his expression.
"When the name Vorhelm is on it, it is no longer family news."
It was logical.
Choosing the heir of one of the six great families did not only affect the people of that family.
Business partners, alliances, enemies, associations, and even the Federation’s decisions, everyone had to include it in their calculations.
The man looked at him for a few more moments and then calmly said.
"But there is one thing about you that does not match the reports."
"Which part?"
"I still haven’t figured it out." The man smiled.
Lian was silent for a moment.
It was a simple sentence.
But coming from someone like Rhaenar, it was not that simple.
The man continued.
"None of the things I read explain why someone who was a loser changed this much in such a short time."
His gaze slowly moved across Lian’s face.
"But I’m not in a hurry to figure it out." Then he added in a completely normal tone.
"Maybe that’s what made my daughter interested in you."
The young Vorhelm paused for a few seconds, the subject had finally appeared.
The Patriarch placed his cup on the table, the soft sound of porcelain touching wood spread through the room, and then he calmly said in the same tone.
"Stay away from Seris."
He looked at him for a few seconds, there was no change in the man’s mood, as if he had only suggested closing the window.
As if he was only stating something simple.
"The reason?"
The man’s eyebrows rose slightly.
"I thought you would first ask what would happen if I didn’t."
"If you intended to threaten me, you would probably say it directly."
The man’s smile became slightly deeper and he leaned back against the chair.
"Alright, you want a reason? In the next few weeks, the Vorhelm Family may enter one of the biggest succession conflicts of the recent generation."

"Your stepmothers, your brothers, the family branches, the council members, the supporters of each faction... and at the head of all of them, that madman who is finally going to return after all these years and choose one name."
Lian was now certain that Damian was not the only one who knew what was going to happen.
Probably almost all the great powers of the world were watching.
Rhaenar continued.
"You are in the middle of that chaos.
It doesn’t matter if you chose to enter it or not, you should know that the Vorhelms will never leave you alone, no matter how much you want to stay away from them, it is impossible."
"I know."
"No, I think you’re only starting to understand, and Seris is not an ordinary member of the Pendragon Family either."
"Tomorrow, part of our new generation will stand before the First Dragon’s Crest, most of the important people gathered here expect Seris to receive the highest crest."
He picked up his cup again.
"And then the official heir of the next generation of the family will be announced, and the result is already clear."
"I have no problem with danger, the children of this family grow up with danger from childhood."
He paused for a moment.
"But it is different when my daughter decides to enter a war herself, or when she is pulled into the middle of it because of another person."
"I don’t want my daughter to become involved with you crazy Vorhelms." Then he added in a much quieter tone that only he could hear, "I don’t want what happened to my sister... to happen to her."
Lian thought for a few seconds, from the view of a father, and even more, from the view of the Patriarch of a family, this concern was completely reasonable.
If he entered the Vorhelm succession war, anyone close to him would become a possible point of pressure.
And if that person was the future heir of the Pendragon Family, the situation would go beyond an internal family conflict and could become much bigger.
This man wanted his daughter to focus on nothing except becoming stronger and did not want her to waste time, especially because of a Vorhelm.
"That makes sense."
Rhaenar looked at him for a moment, probably expecting a different continuation.
And that continuation came.
"But the choice is not mine or yours, has Seris herself said that she wants to stay away from me?"
"No."
"Then my answer is no too."
This time, the silence lasted a little longer.
Lian held the man’s gaze, he was aware of his danger, even more than enough, his body was still instinctively recording every movement Rhaenar made.

But the man’s power was not the subject of the discussion, he was not afraid of anyone, he was not even afraid of his own father, and it should be understood that the entire world was afraid of that man.
If Seris herself ever said that she no longer wanted to see him, the decision would be simple.
But her father? Even if he was one of the most powerful humans in the world, he still could not make that decision for her.
Rhaenar remained still for a few seconds and then laughed, the sound of his laughter was louder this time than before.
"It has been years since someone said no to me this easily."
"Your request was not exactly easy either." the young Vorhelm added.
"True."
The Patriarch was still smiling and there was no anger on his face.
No pressure filled the room either, and strangely, this very thing made his authority even more noticeable.
Someone who truly stood in his position did not need to use his power to remind the young man in front of him who he was.
They both already knew.
Rhaenar looked at his tea for a moment and then asked another question.
"Do you love her?"
