On one of the walls, old marks from impacts remained, and no one had tried to cover them with new stone.
A huge dragon statue stood in the central square, part of one of its wings was broken.
Even on the path, in some places, new stones had been placed among pieces that were several centuries old.
A servant was waiting at the end of the path, without needing an introduction, he lowered his head.
"Mr.
Vorhelm.
This way."
Lian followed him, they passed through two hallways, a small courtyard, and then the second floor of one of the main buildings.
The servant stopped in front of a wooden door.
"The Patriarch is waiting for you inside."
He placed his hand on the handle and the door opened.
The room looked more like a private library than the official meeting place of a Patriarch, and at the end of the room, there was a huge window through which a large part of Verendal could be seen.
A man was standing beside that same window, he had a white cup in his right hand.
He was wearing only simple dark clothes with a small Pendragon dragon symbol on his chest, and his silver hair covered both sides of his temples.
His face looked around fifty years old.
His body was tall and fit, but there was no exaggerated attempt to show physical strength in his appearance.
Hearing the door close, the man turned around, and gray eyes fell on Lian.
And at that exact moment, his body reacted before his mind, his body froze in place.
It was as if it was no longer even his body and it did not dare to listen to his consciousness, no matter how hard he tried, his body did not move at all.
His instinct also simply told him that trying was useless, if the man in front of him decided to kill him right now, he would die.
That was it.
The strangest part?
His body did not even have any desire to resist, as if it had already accepted the result.
And no aura was coming from the man’s body at all, it was like standing in front of a completely ordinary human.
The man slightly raised his cup and a friendly smile appeared on his face.
"I finally get to see you in person, come in, I’m not going to interrogate you or hurt you."
After hearing the man’s words, the impossible pressure suddenly disappeared from him and his body could finally move again.
"This was not the start I expected." Lian walked a few steps forward, the speed of his steps did not change.
The man’s smile became deeper and his eyes moved to Lian’s posture for a moment.
"Don’t worry, if I wanted to kill you, I wouldn’t need to send six people after you, you would have died the moment you stepped into this city."
"That sentence usually doesn’t make people less worried."
There was silence for a moment, he knew those words were not a lie, the man in front of him had gone through five Evolutions.
He was a man who stood at the top of the world’s power, so powerful that it could not be described, their mere breath was enough to turn an entire mountain range into ash.
Their footsteps alone could cause earthquakes, and their gaze could make oceans evaporate.
A Celestial was standing in front of him!
Rhaenar Pendragon!
The man laughed... he really laughed.
"Good."
He placed his cup on the table.
"At least you’re not so afraid that you can’t speak in front of me."
He pointed toward the chair.
"Sit."
Lian sat down and the man sat across from him as well.
"Tea?" And without waiting for an answer, he placed a cup in front of him.
For a few seconds, the only sound in the room was the sound of tea being poured.
"Was your trip good?"
"To this city?"
"In general."
"It could have been more peaceful."
"When I read the reports about you, I also come to the conclusion that you are somehow a magnet for danger."
Lian looked at him and Rhaenar smiled.
"You thought I would summon you without knowing who you are?"
"Of course not."
"Good."
The man took a sip of his tea.
"The academy, your sister’s birthday event, the events in the Special Area, your growth over the past few months, and even the final exams, I’ve heard about all of it."
"Then I don’t need to explain much about myself." The young Vorhelm did not touch his cup.
"No."
Rhaenar casually raised his shoulder slightly.
"Most of the things I could learn by asking, I’ve already read about."
"Then can I ask why I’m here?" Lian thought for a moment.
This time, the Patriarch looked at him for a few seconds.
"Because reports don’t answer questions, people do."

He understood what he meant, this man had not been looking for information from the beginning, he was watching him, the way he sat, his answers, and the things he chose to say and the things he intentionally did not say.
Rhaenar picked up his cup again.
"One year ago, no one knew the name Lian Vorhelm, and anyone who did know you called you a loser."
He calmly drank his tea.
"Now, for some people, the question is whether your father will put your name at the top of the heir list when he returns."
"Our family news spreads quickly." Lian did not change his expression.
"When the name Vorhelm is on it, it is no longer family news."
It was logical.
Choosing the heir of one of the six great families did not only affect the people of that family.
Business partners, alliances, enemies, associations, and even the Federation’s decisions, everyone had to include it in their calculations.
The man looked at him for a few more moments and then calmly said.
"But there is one thing about you that does not match the reports."
"Which part?"
"I still haven’t figured it out." The man smiled.
Lian was silent for a moment.
It was a simple sentence.
But coming from someone like Rhaenar, it was not that simple.
The man continued.
"None of the things I read explain why someone who was a loser changed this much in such a short time."
His gaze slowly moved across Lian’s face.
"But I’m not in a hurry to figure it out." Then he added in a completely normal tone.
"Maybe that’s what made my daughter interested in you."
The young Vorhelm paused for a few seconds, the subject had finally appeared.
The Patriarch placed his cup on the table, the soft sound of porcelain touching wood spread through the room, and then he calmly said in the same tone.
"Stay away from Seris."
He looked at him for a few seconds, there was no change in the man’s mood, as if he had only suggested closing the window.
As if he was only stating something simple.
"The reason?"
The man’s eyebrows rose slightly.
"I thought you would first ask what would happen if I didn’t."
"If you intended to threaten me, you would probably say it directly."
The man’s smile became slightly deeper and he leaned back against the chair.
"Alright, you want a reason?
In the next few weeks, the Vorhelm Family may enter one of the biggest succession conflicts of the recent generation."

"Your stepmothers, your brothers, the family branches, the council members, the supporters of each faction... and at the head of all of them, that madman who is finally going to return after all these years and choose one name."
Lian was now certain that Damian was not the only one who knew what was going to happen.
Probably almost all the great powers of the world were watching.
Rhaenar continued.
"You are in the middle of that chaos.
It doesn’t matter if you chose to enter it or not, you should know that the Vorhelms will never leave you alone, no matter how much you want to stay away from them, it is impossible."
"I know."
"No, I think you’re only starting to understand, and Seris is not an ordinary member of the Pendragon Family either."
"Tomorrow, part of our new generation will stand before the First Dragon’s Crest, most of the important people gathered here expect Seris to receive the highest crest."
He picked up his cup again.
"And then the official heir of the next generation of the family will be announced, and the result is already clear."
"I have no problem with danger, the children of this family grow up with danger from childhood."
He paused for a moment.
"But it is different when my daughter decides to enter a war herself, or when she is pulled into the middle of it because of another person."
"I don’t want my daughter to become involved with you crazy Vorhelms." Then he added in a much quieter tone that only he could hear, "I don’t want what happened to my sister... to happen to her."
Lian thought for a few seconds, from the view of a father, and even more, from the view of the Patriarch of a family, this concern was completely reasonable.
If he entered the Vorhelm succession war, anyone close to him would become a possible point of pressure.
And if that person was the future heir of the Pendragon Family, the situation would go beyond an internal family conflict and could become much bigger.
This man wanted his daughter to focus on nothing except becoming stronger and did not want her to waste time, especially because of a Vorhelm.
"That makes sense."
Rhaenar looked at him for a moment, probably expecting a different continuation.
And that continuation came.
"But the choice is not mine or yours, has Seris herself said that she wants to stay away from me?"
"No."
"Then my answer is no too."
This time, the silence lasted a little longer.
Lian held the man’s gaze, he was aware of his danger, even more than enough, his body was still instinctively recording every movement Rhaenar made.

But the man’s power was not the subject of the discussion, he was not afraid of anyone, he was not even afraid of his own father, and it should be understood that the entire world was afraid of that man.
If Seris herself ever said that she no longer wanted to see him, the decision would be simple.
But her father?
Even if he was one of the most powerful humans in the world, he still could not make that decision for her.
Rhaenar remained still for a few seconds and then laughed, the sound of his laughter was louder this time than before.
"It has been years since someone said no to me this easily."
"Your request was not exactly easy either." the young Vorhelm added.
"True."
The Patriarch was still smiling and there was no anger on his face.
No pressure filled the room either, and strangely, this very thing made his authority even more noticeable.
Someone who truly stood in his position did not need to use his power to remind the young man in front of him who he was.
They both already knew.
Rhaenar looked at his tea for a moment and then asked another question.
"Do you love her?"

chapters.title: Chapter 541: The Future Son-in-Law
paragraphs: Lian did not answer right away, he did not know why everyone seemed so interested in asking him this question, this was not a question he could answer that easily.
Love was not something that could be accepted or rejected based on a passing desire.
In the end, he only said.
"If you mean whether I can sit here right now and say that I love her and that I know exactly what I feel, no."
He was silent for a moment, now that he had started, leaving it unfinished would be worse.
"But seeing her is important to me." His face was calm, and there was no sign of worry or fear.
He had no problem saying this, and he was not embarrassed about saying it either.
Rhaenar did not laugh, he did not joke either, and his expression became a little more serious.
"That was a good answer."
"I wasn’t expecting a compliment." Lian looked at him.
"It wasn’t a compliment, but from a boy your age, I expected to hear a more stupid answer."
"That sounded a lot like a compliment too."
"Don’t get too hopeful."
The young Vorhelm smiled and finally reached for his cup and took a sip, the tea was good.
At least this part of the meeting was simple.
Rhaenar said nothing for a while, then put his cup on the table and locked his fingers together.
"Don’t misunderstand one thing, my problem is not that I think you are not good enough for Seris."
This sentence was unexpected.
"If that were the case, I probably wouldn’t have arranged this meeting at all."
His gaze became deeper for a moment, that unpleasant feeling passed through the back of Lian’s neck again, he felt as if this man was looking inside him.
"My problem is that you might become someone who can no longer be ignored very soon...if Seris gets what we expect tomorrow, she will become the future of the Pendragon Family."
"And if your father chooses you, you might become the future of the Vorhelm Family too."
Two names, two families from the six great powers, and that was when Lian saw the matter from another angle.
Rhaenar said.
"From that moment, a possible relationship between the two of you will no longer be only about two people."
His voice was still calm.
"Several families would do anything to stop two great powers from getting too close to each other, and they would cross lines that you cannot even imagine."
"No one wants to see a union between the Vorhelm and Pendragon Families, even I have no interest in having any connection with those crazy people."

"I have no problem with you, you don’t seem arrogant, stupid, or stubborn like them, but the problem is that you have the Vorhelm name, and that alone is enough for the entire Pendragon Family to stand against this union."
"This is what I asked you to stay away from."
"I understand." Lian said, he understood, if his relationship with Seris was going to move forward, there would be very big obstacles.
He did not care at all about the opinions of the Vorhelms, they had no right to interfere in his life.
But could he say the same about Seris and her family? For that girl, the Pendragons might be very important.
In the end, all of this was only about possibilities for the future, who knew? Maybe their relationship would never go beyond that of two normal friends.
"But you’re not going to do it, and you still don’t want to change your mind." The Patriarch said sarcastically.
"No, my mind cannot be changed."
"I changed my mind, you really are a Vorhelm, stubborn just like them."
A few seconds later, the Patriarch stood up, this movement itself meant the meeting was over.
Lian also stood up.
Rhaenar walked toward the window and put his hands behind his back, looking at his city for a moment.
"I won’t ask you to stay away from her anymore."
The young Vorhelm raised an eyebrow slightly.
"You changed your mind pretty quickly."
"I didn’t change it, I just understood that my request wouldn’t make you do it, I shouldn’t have expected a Vorhelm to be reasonable."
That was reasonable.
"Then I’ll say something else."
This time when he turned around, the smile had almost completely disappeared, and for a moment, it felt as if the whole world was about to fall apart.
"If you ever decide to truly enter my daughter’s life, don’t change your mind halfway."
Lian held his gaze.
Rhaenar continued.
"I have no problem with Seris’s enemies, she can kill her own enemies...she probably even enjoys doing it."
"But I have a problem with someone who gains her trust and then breaks it, no matter what else I am, I am still that girl’s father."
There was no direct threat, there was no need for one.
"I don’t leave people halfway." Lian answered calmly.
The Patriarch looked at him for a few seconds, and then his smile returned, the same calm and almost friendly expression from the beginning of the meeting.
"We’ll see."
The young Vorhelm lowered his head slightly, not enough to be a bow, only the respect that was necessary.
"Then, for now."
"Enjoy the ceremony."
He walked toward the door, opened it, and left.
A few seconds of silence filled the room, Rhaenar picked up his cup, there was still some tea inside.
He took a sip.
Then a quiet laugh came from the dark corner of the library.
"Well, Your Highness?"
He did not even turn his head.
Aurelia Pendragon stepped out from the shadow of one of the tall bookshelves, her usual happy smile on her face.
"Are you satisfied with your future son-in-law?"
"It is still not clear whether he will become my son-in-law or not."
She came closer.
"That wasn’t an answer to my question."
This time Rhaenar looked at her, and Aurelia made her smile even wider.
"You like him, don’t you?"
A few seconds of silence filled the room, the Patriarch did not deny it, and instead looked toward the window again.
"I wouldn’t mind if the jewel that the Vorhelms ignored for years eventually came to our side."
"So you admit that he is a jewel." She laughed.
"That doesn’t mean he is worthy of my daughter."
"Ah."
Aurelia placed a hand over her chest in a dramatic way.
"We finally reached the strict father part."
"Since when have you become so interested in this matter?" Rhaenar gave her a short look.
"Since Seris, for the first time in her life, tolerated a man...let me correct that, a living creature, without having to endure it."
He stayed silent, and Aurelia came closer to the window.
"I think the part about whether he is worthy of Seris or not should be her decision."
"I thought you would support my decision, not a Vorhelm."
"I do, that is why I don’t want your daughter to lose a good choice because of her father’s pride."
Rhaenar let out a short sigh.
"And I really doubt you will find a better husband for Seris than that boy."
"You sound very sure.
"Seris seems to be the same."
This time the Patriarch looked directly at her, and she smiled.
"She just hasn’t realized it herself yet."
A few seconds later, he turned his head toward the city again, from the height of the central building, almost all of Verendal was beneath him.
Thousands of guests, six great families, representatives of twelve ancient associations, and the new generation that would stand before one of the oldest relics of the Pendragon Family tomorrow.
He whispered very quietly.
"We’ll see."
Aurelia tilted her head slightly, the man’s expression revealed nothing, it was not clear what exactly he was thinking.

But one thing could be understood from the calmness in his eyes, he had not made a final decision about Lian yet, and it seemed that he was sure he would have more chances to get to know him very soon.
Lian had not left the central part of the estate yet.
A long stone hallway was in front of him, and the evening light fell across the floor through the tall windows.
His steps were calm.
But his mind was still going over the meeting from a few minutes ago.
Rhaenar was different from what he had imagined.
He expected a cold man, maybe arrogant, maybe someone whose absolute power for decades had made him forget how to speak normally with someone weaker than himself.
But what he had seen was almost the opposite.
The man joked, laughed, drank tea, and even when Lian directly stood against his request, he did not raise his voice or change his expression.
And that made the man even more dangerous.
Control.
That word was the best description.
That man had control over everything, as if there was nothing in the world that could ruin his mood.
As if he had become indifferent to everything.
During the entire meeting, Lian had not even been able to sense a noticeable leak of the man’s Mana.
Someone who had completed five Evolutions.
Rhaenar only needed to breathe for him to turn into a pile of ash and completely disappear from existence.
This was the power of a Celestial.
But the man had sat in front of him like an ordinary human and talked to him.
The young Vorhelm walked down the stairs, if the peak of human power was something like Rhaenar, he was still very far from it.
And this distance was not the kind that would disappear with two more Levels or a few thousand Stat Points.
Strangely, this thought did not upset him, on the contrary, having something that he still had to reach was not bad, he wanted to reach that level of power more than before.
Today, more than any other day, he understood how weak and limited he still was, as if he were a prisoner inside a much larger prison.
Power had made him think he was free, but he was wrong, he was still a prisoner, only becoming stronger would allow him to break free from all his chains.
So he had to become stronger.
"And you’re still alive!" A cheerful voice came from behind him.
"Miss Aurelia." Lian did not even feel the need to turn around.
Aurelia reached him a few seconds later, with the same usual smile and the same energy that seemed to never run out.
"Did you enjoy meeting the strongest Pendragon?"
He stopped and looked at her.
"I would appreciate it if you told me next time before I arrive that I’m going to meet your family’s leader directly."
She raised both hands.
"Sorry, but I really didn’t expect it either." Her face did not show even a moment of guilt.
Lian looked at her for a few seconds, he did not know why, but he felt that the woman was not telling him the whole truth.
Still, there was no point in arguing about it, something else was more important to him.
"Anyway, where is Seris?"
The change in Aurelia’s smile was so fast that he immediately regretted asking the question so directly.

chapters.title: Chapter 542: The Demon Of End
paragraphs: "Since you returned from the Special Area, she has gone into isolation."
"She still hasn’t come out?" Lian walked beside her.
"No."
"Training?"
"More like preparing."
He thought for a few moments, it was almost predictable.
Seris was not the kind of person who would rest the night before the most important ceremony of her generation because "she was already ready."
She was probably using all the resources the family had prepared for her while in isolation.
Increasing her stats as much as possible with the help of those resources and reaching the best possible condition before the ceremony.
And that was not even mentioning that girl had also gone through the first Evolution just like him.
Lian became curious for a moment, with Seris’s talent, resources, and background, what did her first Evolution look like?
One had changed from a Normal monster into a Fallen.
He himself had also upgraded his main Innate Skills after the Evolution, and with their help, he had managed to increase all his stats as much as possible during one month.
Seris’s Evolution path? It was impossible to predict, but he had no doubt that girl would become even more monstrous than before.
"You will definitely see her tomorrow." Aurelia added.
Their path went through one of the old gardens of the estate.
Tall trees cast shadows on both sides of them, and between them, there were dragon statues of different sizes and shapes.
Aurelia walked silently for a few steps before asking.
"By the way, how much do you know about the Dragon Mark Ceremony?"
"More or less." Lian answered and raised his head slightly.
"The new generation is introduced, those who have made important achievements in exploring the new Ruined Realm are rewarded, and then you announce the official heir."
She nodded.
"That’s right."
She paused.
"But the main ceremony is a little older and more complicated than what is usually said outside the family."
Lian looked at her, and Aurelia pointed at one of the dragon statues.
"Do you know why our family is called Pendragon?"
"As far as I know, the founders of the family hunted a dragon."
"That’s right, but not a normal dragon, more exactly, a Demon."
Lian gave her his full attention, and Aurelia continued.
"The name of that Demon was Demon Of End, our ancestors fought it."
Her tone was simple, but the sentence itself was not simple.
"It wasn’t a short battle either, many of the founders of the early branches of the family died there, but in the end, they killed it."
Lian said nothing for a few moments.
Killing a Demon.
He now understood better than many humans what that sentence meant.
The memory of the Demon Of Eclipse was still in his mind, he knew very well how powerful a Demon could be.
And as far as he knew, some Demons were even stronger.
Even today, hunting a Demon Rank being required forces at the highest level of the world.
But the ancestors of the Pendragon Family had managed to kill one.

"After the death of the Demon Of End, our ancestors obtained many spoils from its body, but the most important thing was a special artifact. Something that later became the foundation of one of the family’s most important traditions."
"The Dragon Mark, right?" Lian guessed the answer.
"That’s right, it is a kind of blessing artifact, of course, the word blessing isn’t exactly accurate, but it’s the closest simple explanation."
"What does it do?"
"It reacts to members of the family, almost every twenty-five years, after a new Ruined Realm opens, the family chooses the most important people of the new generation."
Not every young member, only those who were truly worthy of standing before that artifact.
Talent, achievements, future potential, performance in the new Ruined Realm, position among the generation, all of these were considered when choosing the people for the artifact.
Aurelia added.
"Then they stand before the Dragon Mark and read the family’s traditional oath."
Lian listened.
"The artifact reacts to each person’s blood, potential, abilities, growth path, and compatibility, and gives them a Dragon Mark, but not all marks are the same."
Some were simple, some were rare, and some were greatly different from the others in terms of quality.
And there was no guarantee that two geniuses with almost the same level of power would receive similar Dragon Marks.
The artifact measured something beyond their current power, in fact, even after all these years, no one still knew what the true basis of that artifact’s decision was when giving its blessings.
"For many generations, the person who received the highest Dragon Mark was almost always chosen as the heir."
"But this time you already chose Seris." Lian immediately noticed the difference.
"Yes." Aurelia said without even a moment of hesitation, the smile on her face was different this time and showed more pride.
"Even without the Dragon Mark, Seris is the jewel of this family."
Her tone was completely certain.
"No one really doubts that she will receive the highest mark of this generation tomorrow."
The family’s confidence in that girl was truly on another level.
The young Vorhelm became curious for a moment about what reaction he would cause if he himself stood before such an artifact.
Of course, he did not have Pendragon blood, so probably nothing or..., he put the thought aside right there and after a few more steps, he asked.
"I have never read this part in the books."
"Which part?"
"The Demon Of End, the fact that the Mark came from its spoils, is it okay for you to tell me this?"
"Yes." Aurelia said very easily.
"Isn’t it confidential?"
"The details are."
The woman put her hands behind her back.
"But the general truth is not. Important members of the six great families, some of the twelve ancient associations, and many high-rank Awakened know about it."
Lian nodded, it made sense.
If a battle on that scale had happened and several important founders had died in it, hiding the entire event for several centuries would have been almost impossible.
She continued in a happier tone.

"Of course, the ceremony isn’t only for the Dragon Mark, and the six great families, the twelve ancient associations, allied families, companies, unions, political representatives, and anyone else worth inviting come for their own reasons.
"So half of the ceremony happens in closed rooms." Lian added after thinking for a moment, it was easy to guess what she meant.
Aurelia smiled.
"Bravo."
Trade contracts.
The division or exchange of resources from the new Ruined Realm.
Hunting alliances, joint investments.
Agreements about exploration areas and political relations, these were the reasons many forces came.
"And of course, marriage." Aurelia added.
The young Vorhelm turned his eyes slightly toward her, the woman’s smile had become far too innocent...this part was not random.
"Our current Patriarch also started the path toward marrying his current wife at almost this same ceremony."
Her eyes stayed on Lian from the corner, she was clearly watching his reaction.
He thought for a few moments.
"I didn’t expect even the Pendragon heir to marry through an arranged marriage."
"Why?"
"I thought someone in that position would need it less."
Then he paused himself.
No.
If he looked at it more carefully, it was the opposite.
"But it makes sense."
"Oh?" The woman became curious about what reasoning he had reached.
Lian looked at the path ahead.
"When an heir is chosen, they still don’t have all the power of the Patriarch, they have the name, they have the position, but they still need to gather part of the family behind them."
A large foreign family could provide things that would take years to build.
Influence, money, connections, political support, and even indirect military support if needed.
He continued.
"If the Pendragon heir marries someone from one of the other six great families, your family’s internal power doesn’t decrease, but your influence outside the family becomes several times greater."
The woman’s smile became wider.
"For you, marrying into another great power isn’t a weakness, it’s an investment."
"Bravo." Aurelia slowly clapped twice.
Lian ignored her.
"So your family doesn’t only have no problem with the heir having a political marriage, you actually support it."
"Exactly, almost all the heirs of the last few generations either directly married into another great power, or the family used their marriage to build an important alliance." She nodded.
He thought about the Vorhelms in his mind, they almost had the opposite philosophy.
Political marriage also existed in his own family, but the Vorhelms hated dependence.
The family preferred its internal factions to be strong enough that the heir would not need to rely on an outside power to secure their position.

chapters.title: Chapter 543: The Dragon Mark Ceremony
paragraphs: Every foreign alliance was also carefully controlled so that another family could not gain too much influence inside the Vorhelm structure.
The Pendragons?
They seemed to see outside alliances not as a threat, but as a tool to expand their influence.
Two great families with completely different philosophies, it was impossible to say which one was right and which one was wrong.
It made sense to think that the Pendragons had the right idea, but the Vorhelms were not behind them in terms of power, and their family name had much more reputation.
"That is why you support your heirs’ marriages." Lian said.
"It has almost become a tradition." Aurelia nodded.
Then they walked silently for a few steps.
"But Seris is different, before this, many of the elders even thought it would be better if she never married."
"Why?" He was a little surprised.
"Because she is the jewel of the family."
The answer was simple, but there was logic behind it, and Aurelia explained.
"We never wanted to marry Seris into another family and then have them act as if the greatest talent of our generation now belonged to them too."
"And of course, that girl herself never showed any interest."
This part matched more with what Lian knew about Seris, for that girl, fighting and becoming stronger seemed to be the most important reason for her life.
"We all thought the only thing that girl wanted was to reach the top."
He said nothing, he could completely believe such an image of her.
Aurelia gave a mischievous smile.
"But who would have thought that girl..." But she left the sentence unfinished.
Lian waited for a few steps, but no continuation came.
"What about that girl?"
"Forget it."
"You started it yourself."
"I made a mistake." Aurelia laughed casually.
"Anyway, tomorrow she will probably receive many marriage proposals again."
She shook her head with regret.
"Many people still think they have a chance, but Seris? From what I know about her? She’ll tear all of them apart." She did not even need to think about it.
They walked a few more steps, and then the woman added very quietly without looking at him.
"Except one."
At that exact moment, she stopped without giving any further explanation.
An independent building stood in front of them, a two-story house with an old stone exterior, tall windows, and a small garden around it.
"We’re here." Aurelia said with the same completely innocent expression.
Lian only looked at her for a few seconds, the woman knew exactly what she had done.
She had stopped the sentence exactly where she thought it was most likely to make him think about it, unfortunately, this woman had misunderstood him a little.
Such things could not occupy any part of his mind, and he could understand what she meant in advance.
Aurelia held out the small piece that served as the building’s entry permission toward him.
"As long as you’re a guest of the family, this place is yours, I’ll see you tomorrow."
She turned around and walked away along the path with the same light steps.

"This family is really strange." Lian watched her back for a few seconds and then said quietly, he had thought only the Vorhelms had problems with their intelligence level, but it seemed that was not the case.
Inside, the accommodation was more like a complete house than what he expected from a guesthouse.
The first floor had a small living room with a kitchen, a study room, and a bathroom.
The upper floor also had several bedrooms and a balcony facing the eastern part of Verendal.
Lian sat on the edge of the bed, it had been a long day.
In the morning, he was in the capital and a few hours later, he was in Verendal and had managed to meet a Celestial, Rhaenar Pendragon.
He rested his head slightly against the wall, that man was interesting to him, more than he had expected.
Not because he was powerful, the existence of other powerful people was nothing strange to him, what had caught his attention was his personality.
That man’s personality was completely different from his father’s.
After some time, he stood up and walked to the window.
Night was slowly falling over the city, the lights had turned on and guards were moving along the walls.
Different groups of forces were moving through the main streets.
The great guests of the world were already within a few kilometers of him, the six great families, the twelve ancient associations, and probably many of the strongest people in the world.
The Pendragon Patriarch was also nearby, yet a small feeling would not leave him, he did not know why, but he had a bad feeling.
He felt that the next day was not going to go peacefully.
He looked at the quiet streets for a few seconds, maybe after spending so much time in the Ruined Realm, his mind had become too used to danger.
Maybe the prophecy of Region One was still keeping his mind busy for no reason, or maybe everything he had heard today had made him analyze things too much.
But this did not make him lower his guard, his instinct had not been wrong even once during all this time, so if he had a bad feeling, something was definitely going to happen.
He slowly breathed out.
In any case, this was Verendal, the home of the Pendragons, one of the most protected private territories on Earth.
Almost all the great powers of humanity were here for the ceremony.
And one of the few humans who had completed all five Evolutions lived nearby.
In such a place, what bad thing could exactly happen?
He had no answer.
The next morning, the sound of the first bell spread across all of Verendal before the sun had fully risen.
Daaang.
A few seconds later, the second bell answered from another part of the city, then the third, and soon the different towers woke up one after another.
Lian opened his eyes, the morning light had entered the room through the curtains, he got out of bed and walked to the window.
The city was different from the night before.
Pendragon flags had been lowered from all the towers, and the main streets were decorated with dragon symbols.
Official carriages had been moving toward the center of the city since the early hours.
Family members in formal clothes could be seen in the streets, and the security forces were twice as many as the night before.
He changed his clothes and left the accommodation.
The moment he stepped onto the stone path outside, one of the tallest towers in the central part of Verendal lit up with golden light.
A calm light that moved from the base of the tower to its highest point.
Then a sound spread through the city.
It was so close to the roar of a huge dragon that several birds flew up from the nearby rooftops for a moment.
But Lian did not see any creature in the sky, it was only an old echo.
A few seconds later, the official voice of the city’s public network was broadcast through the different towers.
"To all members of the family, guests, and representatives of allied powers—"
The dragon flag opened in the morning wind.
"The Dragon Mark Ceremony will now begin."

chapters.title: Chapter 544: The Dragon Mark Ceremony II
paragraphs: The sound of Verendal’s bells was still in the morning air when Lian moved toward the central part of the city with the flow of guests.

Unlike the previous night, the old streets were no longer quiet, white and gold flags of the Pendragon Family hung from balconies and stone towers, and official groups went toward the ceremony one after another through separate paths.
And among all of them, there were a considerable number of presences that made it clear even without releasing Mana that their owners were not ordinary people.
He kept his hands inside the pockets of the dark formal clothes he had chosen for the ceremony and moved forward without hurry.
The bad feeling he had last night had still not completely disappeared, but there was nothing to prove it either.
So for now, it was only a feeling that made him keep his guard up.
The ceremony location was in the central part of Verendal.
As he got closer, the buildings around them gradually moved farther away, and a huge square revealed itself.
Lian slowed his steps for a moment, the place was neither a closed hall nor a simple public square, but something between an ancient amphitheater and a ritual altar.

Semi-circular rows of seats rose several levels, and thousands of stone and modern seats had been placed among the old architecture. Each section was marked with the symbol of the power it had been assigned to.

The six great families, representatives of the twelve ancient associations, members of the Federation, allied families, and companies and unions that had enough influence to receive a direct invitation from the Pendragons.

But his gaze quickly passed over all of them, the center of the square was more important, a circular altar with a diameter of more than twenty meters was located at the lowest point of the amphitheater.
Six metal and stone rings, one inside another, had been built into its floor.
And right in the center, something was floating.

It was about three meters tall, with a black and irregular surface, and at first glance, it looked more like a huge scale separated from the body of some unnatural creature than something made by humans.
Golden veins flowed across its black surface, similar to veins moving under dark skin.
He did not need to guess, that thing was the Dragon Mark.
Lian stared at it for a few seconds, Aurelia’s words from the night before returned to his mind.
Demon Of End, a Demon Rank dragon and a creature that the ancestors of the Pendragons had killed at a heavy cost.
And this was the most important spoil that remained from that battle.

Still, in a way, it was also a little unfortunate, if he could obtain the Essence of that Demon, he could form another Core.
But he doubted that he could find such a thing.

"If you keep staring at that thing like this for a few more seconds, they might think you are planning to steal it."
Lian turned his head, a tall man was standing a few meters away.
A calm face that, despite the clear family resemblance, did not have the usual harshness of many members of the Vorhelm Family.
Several people with the Vorhelm Family symbol stood behind him.

Cassius came forward.
There was no hug and no overly friendly display, and only when he reached Lian did he place his right hand on his shoulder and look him up and down for a few seconds.
Then he gave a faint smile.
"I’m glad to see you again."
"Me too, if there is one of my brothers that I’m happy to see, it’s you, my older brother."
"Uncle Damian said I might see you here too, and I’m glad it turned out that way."
Cassius took his hand off his shoulder.
"I’m glad to see you’re healthy too, these days, every time I hear news about you, before I continue reading, I have to make sure you’re still alive."
"Well, I guess people have been saying that a lot lately too." Lian looked at the Vorhelms behind his brother and said quietly.
"So Uncle talked to you too." Cassius understood what he meant.
"Yes."
A few seconds of silence formed between them.
His older brother then turned his head slightly toward the section reserved for the Vorhelm delegation, and they both slowly moved in that direction.
"Did he tell you about Father?"

"It’s natural, but if you’re worried that I will enter the game because of Father’s seat, you don’t need to be."
"I know." Lian said calmly.
"Good. At least one of my brothers still believes what I say." He laughed, and a sign of relief appeared in his eyes.
This was not a new matter between them, Cassius had made it clear a long time ago that he had no interest in the position of Patriarch of the Vorhelm Family.
It was not that he had no ambition, he did, but his ambition was in a different direction.
His own power, his own path, and a position that did not require blood to be spilled between the family’s factions for him.
This was also one of the reasons why Lian’s relationship with him had never really become bad, of course, they had distance between them, there was a large age difference.
They had not even spent many years together, but they were not enemies either, more accurately, their relationship was neutral.
They were neither enemies nor friends, they did not hurt each other and they did not help each other.
What was more interesting was that this man was the oldest child of the Patriarch and, in the eyes of many, the most likely heir, but he himself had no interest in that position.
Cassius reached the Vorhelm delegation’s section, and before they separated, he lowered his voice.
"By the way, if you need anything, you can contact me directly."
Lian looked at his older brother for a few moments, he was not someone who used long emotional words, and perhaps that was why the sentence carried more weight.
"Okay."
Lian did not sit in the Vorhelm section, his invitation had assigned him another seat, and to his surprise, it was in a row very close to the front.
From this section, almost the entire altar could be seen.
The six great families were placed in six separate sections, with the Pendragons in the closest section to the main stage.
A little farther away was Blackthorn, a dark flag with branches that looked like thorns on it.
(In the previous few Chapters, I accidentally wrote Eisenwald, but Blackthorn is one of the six great families, unfortunately, I accidentally used a name from my other novel.)
Then there were Stormheart and the Vorhelms on the other side, followed by Grandalz and finally Valemont.
All six main families of the world had brought representatives or important members of their families.
And this was without even considering the twelve ancient associations that filled several levels of the seats across from them.
Lian moved his gaze across the Pendragon section, and several people caught his attention almost immediately.
Some were curious, some neutral, and a few were clearly cold.
He did not need to guess the reason, Seris’s personal invitation had not remained as private as he had thought.
One of the young men did not even try to hide his displeasure when their eyes met for a few seconds.
He had short silver hair and a strong face, his body showed even under his formal clothes that he had spent most of his life on the training field, and he looked at him with clear hostility.
The young Vorhelm did not know him yet, but he would probably hear his name very soon.
Another bell rang, this one was different from the morning bells, shorter and heavier, and it was heard only once.
All conversations in the square slowly became silent, and two people appeared on the main stage, Rhaenar Pendragon was the same man Lian had seen the day before.
He was wearing more formal clothes, but he still had the same calm behavior as before.
Even so, thousands of people became silent just because he entered.
Beside him stood a woman Lian had never seen until today, and even among all the powerful people present, it was difficult to ignore her.
Isolde Pendragon.
The Matriarch of the family.

chapters.title: Chapter 545: The Dragon Mark Ceremony III
paragraphs: Her very long golden hair fell down her back over her white clothes and reached almost to her waist, the beauty of her face was not the kind that made her look delicate or harmless.
On the contrary, the calmness of her face, the sharp lines of her gaze, and the way she stood made her look more like something complete and dangerous.
Her formal white clothes were decorated with thin black and gold lines.
She did not wear a large crown, only a thin golden piece among her hair, but just as Rhaenar did not need a crown to show his position, Isolde did not need one either.
If Rhaenar was a mountain that did not hide its own weight but did not need to move either, Isolde was more like a blade that was still inside its sheath.
Beauty was the first thing that caught the eye, power was what could be felt behind it a few moments later.
Lian did not keep his gaze on her for too long.
Even so, among thousands of people, Isolde looked directly toward his section for a moment.
It was only one second, and then her gaze moved away.
He said nothing, but he was almost certain that yesterday’s conversation with Rhaenar was no longer only between him and Seris’s father.
It seemed that the Matriarch of the family also knew about the conversation, and God knew how she felt about her possible son-in-law.
Rhaenar walked to the edge of the main stage.
"Twenty-five years ago, the generation before you stood before this same Mark."
There was no long introduction.
"Some of them are not here today."
Several faces in the Pendragon section became more serious for a moment.
"Some became commanders, some are responsible for our territories, and some are the fathers and mothers of those whose names we will hear today."
His gaze moved across the younger generation of the family.
"The new Ruined Realm has opened, and now it is your turn."
That was all.
He took one step back and sat on one of the two thrones with his wife, short and organized applause spread across the field, and then the ceremony entered its first part.
The young members of the Pendragon family were introduced one after another.
Not all of them were geniuses, some were introduced because of their fast growth, some for saving members of their groups, and some for finding important routes in the new Ruined Realm.
Some were introduced for successfully leading operations where not even one person had died.
Names were called, achievements were announced, the people went onto the stage, received their recognition, and returned.
Lian did not remember every detail, but he paid enough attention to better understand the structure of the new generation of the Pendragons.
Then the ceremony host paused and the atmosphere in the field became quieter.
"And now, the five outstanding members of the current generation of the Pendragon Family."
This time, even many of the powerful guests paid more attention.
The first name. Tristan Pendragon.
A young man who was even younger than most of the people who had been introduced.
He had light brown hair and a younger-looking face, but the presence of his Mana did not match his appearance.

The short report of the ceremony focused more on his fast growth and two rescue operations in the new Ruined Realm, in one of those operations he had rescued another group from being surrounded by several monsters.
Lian gave him a short look, he was definitely someone the Pendragons were counting on for the future.
The second person, Lysandra Pendragon.
A girl with dark hair tied behind her head, her behavior was so organized that even when she stepped forward to receive her recognition, she did not make any unnecessary movement.
Her achievements were more related to command than raw power.
Several difficult exploration operations, almost no deaths, and fast decision-making.
The third name was enough to make the young man who had given Lian several cold looks since the beginning of the ceremony stand up.
Caelen Pendragon.
One of the strongest direct fighters of the new generation, with the highest number of recorded hunts among people his age in the past few months.
Very strong performance in long battles, an aggressive fighting style, and from the way he walked, it was clear that he did not dislike the attention he was receiving.
As he passed, his short gaze stopped on Lian again, and his hostility was even clearer this time.
This time, Lian did not even bother to react, all of their achievements looked pale and ordinary in his eyes.
The fourth person, Lucien Pendragon.
When he entered, the reaction of the field was a little different, there was more respect and more controlled applause.
Lucien was older than the previous three and it was clear that his position among the new generation was already established.
He had a calm face and silver hair, movements without hurry, and almost everything could be seen in the report of his achievements.
Power, command, exploration, several important hunts, and before another name appeared, many people considered him the most natural choice for the heir.
Then the four of them stood in their assigned places.
The fifth place remained empty, no one asked why, almost everyone knew what name was left.
The ceremony host waited for a few seconds and then said.
"And the final member—"
The weak noise of the crowd itself became silent.
"Seris Pendragon."
Before Lian saw her, he noticed the different silence in the field.
Then the gate of the inner section opened and Seris walked out, her clothes were different from all the formal clothes of the women he had seen today.
No long and heavy dress that limited her movement, no excessive decorations.

A combination of white and black with very few golden lines, a design that belonged to the formal clothes of the family but was still made for someone who needed to be able to move and even fight in it.
Her hair had been arranged, but not in a way that changed her personality, her face had the same cold calmness as always, the same gaze and the same controlled steps.
But Lian noticed another change during those first few steps.

She had become stronger, he could not put a number on it from such a long distance, but the presence of this girl had become so powerful and destructive, that it was clear she still did not know how to control it.
During the time she had been in isolation, it was clear that she had not only returned to her previous peak, but had gone beyond it.
Seris first stood before Rhaenar and Isolde’s stage, lowered her head respectfully, and then turned toward the crowd.
The applause was louder than for the previous four, even many of the guests outside the family were watching her carefully.
The Jewel of the Pendragon Family.
A name he had heard many times during these past few months.

But what caught Lian’s attention was her gaze, she looked across the crowd once, from the right, the representatives of the associations, and several times toward the Vorhelm section, as if she was looking for someone among them.
When she could not find the person she was looking for, for a moment her face became colder and more indifferent instead of showing disappointment.
But before she completely moved her gaze away, she also looked toward the front, where the stage was closer, and her gaze stopped directly on Lian.
She only looked at him for maybe one second, but all of that coldness and complete indifference disappeared.
No big smile appeared, Seris was still Seris, but her gaze became softer.
Then she lowered her head just a little, a greeting that probably most of the people present did not even notice.
Lian answered just as briefly.
A few seconds later, she moved her gaze away and went to her place.
They had seen each other again.
But on the other side of the field, not everyone was indifferent, Caelen briefly looked between Seris and Lian, and this time his jaw became slightly tighter.
The other two young Pendragons also exchanged a few quiet words, apparently that one-second greeting meant much more to those who knew Seris well than it should have.
After the introductions ended, the atmosphere of the field changed.
The main part of the ceremony was beginning.
The six rings around the altar lit up at the same time with a weak golden light.
A deep sound passed through the stones beneath the field and the Dragon Mark rose a few centimeters higher.
The golden lines on its black surface moved slowly.
The ceremony host said.
"Every generation, the members who are considered worthy of standing before the Dragon Mark will make the family oath."

chapters.title: Chapter 546: The Dragon Mark Ceremony IV
paragraphs: Then the ranks appeared one after another on the six rings on the floor of the altar.
Scale Mark — First Grade.
Fang Mark — Second Grade.
Wing Mark — Third Grade.
Crown Mark — Fourth Grade.
Sovereign Mark — Fifth Grade.
Ancestral Mark — Sixth Grade.
Even the host’s tone changed slightly when he reached that one.
"First and Second Grade are the most common Marks recorded throughout the generations."
"Third Grade is only given to those whose potential is clearly above the normal level of their generation."
"The Crown Mark is rare."
"The Sovereign Mark may not appear for several complete generations."
Then—
"And the Ancestral Mark..."
The man paused for a moment.
"In the entire history of the family, only three members have ever received it."
A short murmur spread among the guests.

This was not only a family title, it was the remaining power of a Demon, the artifact itself measured the potential of the new generation and gave them a blessing that could greatly help them on their path.
The first person entered the altar, a young man whose name Lian had heard during the recognition section, but he was not very important.
He stood in the center of the six rings, moved closer to the first Dragon Mark, and with a small blade given to him by one of the family priests, he cut the tip of his finger.
A drop of blood fell onto the black surface of the Mark, and at that moment one of the golden lines lit up.
The young man placed his palm on the Mark and closed his eyes.
And he read the oath.
"My blood for the family."
"My power for the generation after me."
"As long as the dragon flies above Verendal, my oath will never be broken."
Thum.
The first ring lit up, light rose from beneath the young man’s feet, the second ring also responded a few seconds later.
Then it stopped.
Golden letters appeared above the altar.
[The Fang Mark — Second Grade.]
The light entered the young man’s body, red-golden lines formed on the back of his right hand, it was a simple image of a dragon’s head.
The crowd applauded.
The young man gave a short bow and went down.
The next person also received the Scale Mark, the next one received the Fang Mark, and two others, one received the Wing Mark and then another Scale Mark.
Lian did not watch every step with the same attention as the first time, the ceremony had found its own rhythm and had become somewhat repetitive.

No one among them was able to receive anything higher than the Wing Mark, of course they were only young people who had gained some achievements and had proven that they were worthy of receiving a Dragon Mark.
There were still five people remaining, and as they got closer to the five main names, the atmosphere became heavy again.

Three.

[Wing Mark — Third Grade.]

Third.
Fourth.
The light of the fourth ring became stronger than the previous ones.
[Crown Mark — Fourth Grade.]
This time, several elders also nodded with satisfaction, finally, someone at this ceremony had managed to receive the first Crown Mark.
They had been somewhat worried that in this generation, only one person might be able to go beyond the Wing Mark, but fortunately, that did not happen.

Even before entering, he gave a short look toward the young members of the family, as if he knew exactly what result he wanted.
Three rings lit up quickly and the fourth one lit up with a slight delay.
[Crown Mark — Fourth Grade.]
Clear satisfaction appeared on his face, when he came down, he gave Lysandra a short look but the girl did not react.

A strong golden light rose from the fifth ring.

Lucien came down from the altar, only when he stood beside the other four, he looked at the new Mark on his hand for a moment.
Satisfaction was enough.
Now only one person remained.
The ceremony host did not even need to ask for silence, the entire field had already become silent by itself.
"The final selected member of the new generation."
"Seris Pendragon."
Seris moved from her place, this time there was no applause, of course, it was not out of disrespect but because of the expectations they had for her.
Thousands of eyes followed her to the center of the altar.
Lian did the same.
She stood before the Dragon Mark.
Isolde leaned her body slightly forward, Rhaenar remained calm, but the hand resting on the armrest of his chair was no longer still.
This girl was the jewel of their family, a genius who might be able to break through the chains and go beyond everything.
Caelen did not take his eyes off the altar, Lucien was also completely serious this time, Lysandra and Tristan were also watching seriously, but there was no hostility in their eyes.
Even for them, she was considered the jewel of the family and they all supported her.
Seris took the small blade, cut the tip of her finger, and a drop of blood fell onto the black surface of the Mark.
She closed her eyes.
"My blood for the family."
Her voice was calm, clear, and without any shaking.
"My power for the generation after me."
A very weak light moved beneath the six rings.
"As long as the dragon flies above Verendal, my oath will never be broken."
Silence covered the entire place.
But she did not remove her hand and then thum!
The sound came from the Mark itself.
Even from several dozen meters away, Lian felt a very weak vibration under his feet.
The golden lines on the black surface lit up at the same time.
The first ring lit up.
Then the second.
Third.
Fourth.
A murmur appeared among the crowd.
Caelen slowly clenched his fingers.
Fifth.
This time, the murmuring completely stopped.
The Sovereign Mark.
The same thing Lucien had received, but the light was still moving inside the Mark.
Seris did not open her eyes.
The sixth ring was still dark.
One second.
Two.
Three.
Nothing happened.
Then the entire Dragon Mark was covered in white-golden light.
Vooom!

A wave of light shot from the center of the altar into the sky, it had no heat and did not destroy anything, but it carried an ancient pressure that made many weaker people unconsciously tense their bodies.
The light did not stop at a height of several dozen meters, it spread out and two huge wings opened from it.
A long neck, horns, claws, and within a few seconds, the huge shape of a dragon formed above the entire field.
It was nothing but light, but when its mouth opened, a deep roar shook all of Verendal.
Grrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrr!
Birds flew into the sky from all the towers around them, the flags were pulled backward by the wave of air that passed over the field.
And at that exact moment, the sixth ring lit up, its golden light was even brighter than the previous five rings.
Letters much larger than before appeared above the altar.
[Ancestral Dragon Mark.]

chapters.title: Chapter 547: From Now On, No One Leaves The City
paragraphs: Birds flew into the sky from all the towers around them, the flags were pulled backward by the wave of air that passed over the field.
And at that exact moment, the sixth ring lit up, its golden light was even brighter than the previous five rings.
Letters much larger than before appeared above the altar.
[Ancestral Dragon Mark.]
[Sixth Grade.]
For perhaps two seconds, no one reacted.
Even some of the elders who had probably lived for decades only stared at the altar.
Then the sound came.
First from the Pendragon section...and then the entire field, applause rose like a huge wave.
The sound of thousands of hands hitting together and the shouts of Seris’s name could be heard.
Even some of the outside representatives stood up without hiding their admiration.
Only the Vorhelms and the other six families and some members of the twelve ancient associations remained in their seats and did not stand.
They did not need to applaud anyone, and besides, applauding the genius of a rival family did not make sense.
Lian continued looking at the center of the altar, the light from the Dragon Mark entered Seris’s hand and golden lines formed on the back of her right hand.
But they were much more complex than the Marks he had seen before.
The head of a dragon, a body that wrapped around part of her hand, and two open wings whose thin lines continued almost to her wrist.
For a moment, it seemed as if the Mark was alive and the golden lines inside it moved, then they slowly became still.
The image of the dragon in the sky also slowly disappeared and the lights came down.
She removed her hand from the Mark.
Rhaenar gave a very small smile, of course, he was not surprised, as if he had seen more of something he had expected.
Isolde, however, did not hide it, satisfaction and pride were clear in her eyes.
Seris first looked at the two of them, then slightly lowered her head.
Then her gaze moved, first toward the family section, then among the guests and once again toward Lian.
This time, no one could say it was a coincidence, her gaze was direct, he answered her gaze and a very faint smile appeared on his face.
It was not enough for everyone to see from a distance, but Seris saw it, because the cold expression on her face became slightly softer for a moment.
And that alone was enough for several young Pendragons who had been watching her throughout the entire ceremony to have hostility appear in their eyes again.
Lian felt Caelen’s gaze, which contained killing intent, even from the other side of the field, but he ignored it.
The applause did not last long, the ceremony had to continue, Seris stepped back from the center of the altar, but she still remained near the Mark.
Rhaenar stood up from his seat.
Everyone knew what important part remained, the results of the Marks had been decided and now it was time to announce the heir of the next generation.
The ceremony host also stepped back, from this moment onward, the Patriarch himself would speak.
But before he even had a chance to speak, a voice from one of the great family sections interrupted him.
"Stop the ceremony!"
Almost all heads turned at the same time, they wanted to see which idiot had dared to interrupt the words of a Celestial.
And it was the Valemont section, one of the six great families.
A middle-aged man with dark gray hair had said it, he was wearing formal dark blue clothes with the symbol of a white tower on them.
Gregor Valemont, the leader of the delegation that had been sent.
One of his guards was standing beside him.
The guard’s face had lost its normal color and it was clear that he had told Gregor some news a few seconds earlier.
The atmosphere of the field changed in an instant and the entire situation became chaotic, they were not stupid enough to think that someone had simply gone crazy.
If someone, especially a representative of a great family, had dared to interrupt a Celestial before he could speak, then something had definitely happened.
Rhaenar did not even frown, as if he did not care about the insult, he only moved his gaze toward Gregor.
"Did something happen?"
His tone had the same calmness as always.
But everyone present knew that interrupting such a ceremony without a reason was not something that could simply be ignored.
Gregor came down from his section, his steps were fast.
"A problem?"
His voice was heavy with controlled anger.
"One of the members of my delegation was killed inside your city less than ten minutes ago!"
An immediate murmur spread across the field and several other representatives looked toward their own people.
Even Lian looked surprised.
"Where?" Rhaenar asked, but there was no calmness left anymore, instead, there was a coldness as deep as the ocean in his eyes.
"Inside the accommodation that your family itself provided for us."
This time, even several main members of the Pendragon family changed their expressions, the official guest accommodations inside the area were under the complete protection of the Pendragons.
A murder in the street was one thing, a murder inside the official accommodation of a great family was something else.
Gregor continued.
"No security seal was broken, and no intrusion warning was recorded either."
Isolde, without standing from her place, turned her head toward one of the commanders beside the stage, said a few short sentences, and the commander immediately moved.
Three security groups quietly left the field.
"Is the cause of death known?" the Patriarch asked.
This time, Gregor remained silent for a few seconds, his jaw was tight, then his gaze moved away from the Patriarch and slowly went toward another section of the field.
Stormheart.
The people of that family understood almost immediately why he was looking at them.
One of their elders frowned.
"My people checked the place, the remaining Mana traces on the body are clear, what was used was one of their skills."
"Watch your words, Gregor." One of the Stormheart members stood up from his seat.
"Shut up! Do you think we don’t know that you bastards have been plotting behind our backs because of the northern mines in the newly obtained areas in the Heavenly Realm?"
Complete silence filled the place, everyone looked at each other and tried to understand what had suddenly happened.
Lian moved his gaze between the two sections.
Valemont.
Stormheart.
The members of both families were now sitting in a completely different way from a few seconds ago.
Some had their hands tightly gripping the armrests, some had their eyes fixed directly on the opposing side.
Some representatives of the twelve ancient associations began exchanging short whispers with their companions.
Rhaenar said nothing for several seconds, among all the people present, perhaps he was the only one who had completely kept the same calm as before, although there was coldness in it.
His gaze remained on Gregor first, then Stormheart, and then he slowly checked the entire field.
When he spoke, his voice was not loud, but everyone heard it.
"From this moment, no one leaves Verendal."

chapters.title: Chapter 548: Reunion With Seris ( Bonus - )
paragraphs: "No one leaves Verendal."
Rhaenar Pendragon’s sentence was not loud.
It did not need to be, everyone heard his voice easily.
Lian was still sitting in his place when he saw the first change.
A tower on the western side of the city lit up, then the second tower and behind it the third tower.
Golden light passed over the old buildings of Verendal and ran across the stone walls like thin lines.
A few seconds later, similar lines appeared from the other directions and completed a huge ring around the main part of the city.
Only part of it could be seen from that distance, but he could guess its path.
The main gates were being closed and the transportation systems were being shut down.
The city’s security network was leaving ceremony mode and entering lockdown status.
Fortunately, there was no painful alarm sound and no soldier started running across the field.
Everything happened with an order that showed the Pendragons were prepared for situations like this more than any display of power could.
He moved his gaze away from the golden lines and placed it on Rhaenar, the man had not even moved from his place.
The Patriarch had not asked if he could close a city where thousands of guests from the greatest powers in the world were present.
He had simply made the decision and the city had obeyed, this was the difference between the owner of this territory and his guests.
Gregor Valemont was still standing below his family’s section, the anger had not left his face and several other Valemont members had gathered behind him.
On the other side, the members of Stormheart were also no longer sitting calmly.
A man stood among them, he was in his forties, and was known to many of the people there, Adrian Stormheart.
The leader of that family’s delegation and an Awakened who had passed three Evolutions.
He walked down a few steps, but did not enter the field.
"Finding Stormheart’s trace on the body does not prove that one of us is the killer."
"Mana traces?, the type of burn, the remaining lightning, the Mana pressure and the type of damage to the nervous pathways also match you exactly." Gregor turned his head toward him.
Adrian did not even frown.
"Then there are two possibilities, either one of my people committed the murder... or someone really wants you to believe that."
"Are you saying we made the evidence?" One of the younger Valemonts stood up at the same moment.
From the other side, one of the Stormhearts also moved, the atmosphere of the field changed in only a few seconds, not enough for a battle to begin.
But a kind of silence formed where everyone was waiting to see who would make the mistake of taking the next step.

The problem was that these two families had had conflicts and arguments with each other during the past few months, although the tension was controlled, their argument was something that had the potential to grow.
The argument was about a special resource mine that was extremely important to Overlords, a resource that could directly help them obtain a considerable number of Stat Points.
"Sit down." Rhaenar said only one word.
That was all.
No aura was released and no pressure fell over the field, but the young Valemont became silent, and the Stormheart man sat down again.
Gregor was still standing, but said nothing.
The Patriarch moved his gaze across the two families.
"Closing the city is not against either of you. Until the cause of the murder is clear, the safety of everyone who entered Verendal is the responsibility of the Pendragons."
Then his gaze moved toward Isolde Pendragon.
The Matriarch did not need any extra explanation and stood from her place.
If Rhaenar controlled the field with his heavy calmness, Isolde was different.
"Do not move the body."
One of the commanders lowered his head.
"Seal the Valemont residence until the investigation is complete., Save all security records from the past twelve hours separately and lock the original copy."
Second order.
"No Stormheart member will be arrested."
This sentence made several Valemonts look unhappy, but Isolde continued without paying attention.
"But until the first investigation is complete, the members of the delegation will not leave the assigned area unless they are accompanied by our forces."
Then she gave the last order.

"Form a joint investigation group. One specialist from the Pendragons, one person from Valemont, one person from Stormheart, one Federation representative, and one independent specialist from one of the ancient guilds."
This time, even Gregor said nothing, it was a smart move.
If the Pendragons investigated by themselves, any result could be accused of being biased.
If the Valemonts were responsible, Stormheart would not accept it and the same would happen the other way around.
But when five different sides recorded every step, changing the truth became much harder.
Lian watched everything from his place.

This was not a place where a nineteen-year-old young man, even if he had the Vorhelm name, could stand among the elders of the six families and the twelve ancient guilds and give his opinion about the investigation method.
There were people in this field who had probably managed security files and family wars before he was even born.
He also did not consider himself important enough to think that all the problems in the world were waiting for him to enter them.
For now, he only watched, however, one small point would not leave his mind.
The Stormheart trace was very clear.

If someone from the Stormheart family really intended to assassinate a Valemont member in the middle of Pendragon territory, leaving something that would scream the name of their family during the first investigation was a strange choice.
Of course, it was not impossible, maybe hiding was not the goal at all, maybe it was a message, maybe there was a conflict that Lian did not know about.
He had not seen the scene, he had not seen the body, and he had not examined the structure of the attack, so he put the thought aside, a guess without information was only a guess.
A few minutes later, Rhaenar stepped forward again.
His gaze briefly stayed on the altar and then on Seris.
The Ancestral Mark was still shining with a very weak light on the back of the girl’s hand.
The ceremony had almost reached its most important part and only the official announcement of the heir remained.
"The announcement of the heir will be delayed until the situation becomes clear."
This time, the reaction came from inside the Pendragons, no one dared to object, but the whispers became louder.
Some members of the older generation exchanged unhappy looks.
It was natural.
A ceremony held once every twenty-five years had been stopped exactly one step before the announcement of the heir.
But Lian was looking at Seris more than anyone else, the girl was still standing beside the altar.
If she was unhappy with her father’s decision, nothing could be seen on her face, she only looked toward the Valemont section once and then toward the forces leaving the field.
And without a word, she walked down from the altar.
The young Vorhelm leaned his head slightly against the back of his chair.

If the only thing that mattered to Seris was the title of heir, she should have been more unhappy than anyone else right now, she had received the highest possible Mark of the generation only a few minutes ago.
Almost the entire field knew what the next step would be but someone had been killed and for her, it seemed clear that her title could wait.
But honestly, from what he knew about her, he found it unlikely that the position of heir mattered to her even a little.
About half an hour later, the younger generation and most of the guests who had no role in the investigation left the main field.
The family leaders, elders, and security specialists remained.
Cassius was also there as the leader of the Vorhelm delegation.
Lian did not even see him before leaving, this was also natural, Cassius had the duty of staying beside the family’s official representatives, besides, that man had passed two Evolutions.
Himself? He had no duty.
For a while, he walked without a goal in one of the inner gardens of the Pendragon estate.

The path passed between old trees and short stone walls, the sound of the main field could no longer be heard from this distance and if someone did not know about what had happened an hour ago, they might think Verendal was still having its normal day.
He stopped near a stone pond, the reflection of the sky and part of the tree branches could be seen in the water.
The sound of footsteps came from behind him, they were calm and regular.
"You found me quickly."
"It was not hard to follow you."
Lian turned around, Seris was standing a few meters away.
She was still wearing the same formal clothes from the ceremony, but she had removed some of the decorations and now her appearance was a little more normal.
The first thing that caught his eye was her right hand.

The golden Mark on the back of her hand was a dragon with open wings whose lines continued almost to her wrist, its light was no longer strong, but even when it was not glowing, it did not look completely normal.
"Congratulations."
"Thank you." Seris raised her hand slightly and looked at the Mark.
"Many people seemed to expect you to get at least an Ancestral Mark beforehand, well, I expected the same."
She looked at her Mark for a few moments and nodded, she was also confident that she would receive something like this.
But she did not seem excited about it at all, if anything, seeing him seemed more pleasant to her.
"What did my father want from you yesterday?" Her tone became a little more direct and it was clear that Aurelia had told her some things.
The question was very direct, and Lian saw no reason to avoid it.
"He told me to stay away from you."

sentences.text: "No one leaves Verendal."

It did not need to be, everyone heard his voice easily.
Lian was still sitting in his place when he saw the first change.
A tower on the western side of the city lit up, then the second tower and behind it the third tower.
Golden light passed over the old buildings of Verendal and ran across the stone walls like thin lines.
A few seconds later, similar lines appeared from the other directions and completed a huge ring around the main part of the city.
Only part of it could be seen from that distance, but he could guess its path.
The main gates were being closed and the transportation systems were being shut down.
The city’s security network was leaving ceremony mode and entering lockdown status.
Fortunately, there was no painful alarm sound and no soldier started running across the field.
Everything happened with an order that showed the Pendragons were prepared for situations like this more than any display of power could.
He moved his gaze away from the golden lines and placed it on Rhaenar, the man had not even moved from his place.
The Patriarch had not asked if he could close a city where thousands of guests from the greatest powers in the world were present.
He had simply made the decision and the city had obeyed, this was the difference between the owner of this territory and his guests.
Gregor Valemont was still standing below his family’s section, the anger had not left his face and several other Valemont members had gathered behind him.
On the other side, the members of Stormheart were also no longer sitting calmly.
A man stood among them, he was in his forties, and was known to many of the people there, Adrian Stormheart.
The leader of that family’s delegation and an Awakened who had passed three Evolutions.

Adrian did not even frown.
"Then there are two possibilities, either one of my people committed the murder... or someone really wants you to believe that."
"Are you saying we made the evidence?" One of the younger Valemonts stood up at the same moment.

The Matriarch did not need any extra explanation and stood from her place.
If Rhaenar controlled the field with his heavy calmness, Isolde was different.
"Do not move the body."
One of the commanders lowered his head.

Second order.
"No Stormheart member will be arrested."
This sentence made several Valemonts look unhappy, but Isolde continued without paying attention.
